items.stem: A circle with center \(O\) has a radius of 12. Sector \(AOB\) of the circle has an area of \(24\pi\). What is the measure, in radians, of central angle \(AOB\)?
solution: With \(\theta\) in radians, sector area \(= \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta\).
\(\frac{1}{2}(144)\theta = 24\pi\), so \(72\theta = 24\pi\) and \(\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(\theta = \frac{2(24\pi)}{144} = \frac{\pi}{3}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. The angle measures \(60^{\circ}\), but the question asks for radians; 60 radians is a different angle.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This drops the \(\frac{1}{2}\): \(144\theta = 24\pi\) gives \(\frac{\pi}{6}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This treats \(24\pi\) as the arc length: \(\frac{24\pi}{12} = 2\pi\).

items.stem: A cycle rickshaw in Dhaka has a rear wheel with a diameter of 70 centimeters. On one trip, the wheel turns exactly \(1{,}500\) times without slipping. The distance the rickshaw travels on this trip is \(k\pi\) meters. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Each turn moves the rickshaw one circumference: \(\pi d = 70\pi\) centimeters, which is \(0.7\pi\) meters.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, a circle has its center at \((4, -3)\) and is tangent to the \(x\)-axis. Which equation represents the circle?
solution: A circle tangent to the \(x\)-axis has a radius equal to the distance from its center to that axis, the absolute value of the \(y\)-coordinate: \(r = 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This circle has center \((-4, 3)\); the signs inside the parentheses are reversed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The right side must be \(r^{2} = 9\), not \(r = 3\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses the distance to the \(y\)-axis, 4, as the radius; that circle is tangent to the \(y\)-axis instead.
explanation.D: Correct. Center \((4, -3)\), radius 3, so \(r^{2} = 9\).

items.stem: Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is inscribed in the circle shown. The measure of angle \(ABC\) is \((2x + 14)^{\circ}\), and the measure of angle \(ADC\) is \((3x + 6)^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ADC\)?
solution: Opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle are supplementary: \((2x + 14) + (3x + 6) = 180\).
Angle \(ADC\) measures \(3(32) + 6 = 102^{\circ}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the value of \(x\), not the measure of the angle.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is angle \(ABC\), \(2(32) + 14\), not angle \(ADC\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This sets the two angles equal; opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to \(180^{\circ}\), they are not equal.
explanation.D: Correct. \(x = 32\), so angle \(ADC\) is \(102^{\circ}\).

items.stem: The minute hand of a wall clock is 15 centimeters long. How far, in centimeters, does the tip of the minute hand travel from 3:00 to 3:40?
solution: In 40 minutes the minute hand turns \(\frac{40}{60} = \frac{2}{3}\) of a full circle.
The tip travels \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot 2\pi(15) = \frac{2}{3} \cdot 30\pi = 20\pi\) centimeters.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \pi(15)^{2}\), the area swept by the hand, not the distance the tip travels.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot \pi(15)\); the circumference is \(2\pi r\), not \(\pi r\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot 30\pi = 20\pi\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses 30, the diameter, as the radius: \(\frac{2}{3} \cdot 2\pi(30) = 40\pi\).

items.stem: A paper fan opens into the shape of a sector of a circle with a radius of 6 inches. When fully open, the fan has an area of \(15\pi\) square inches. What is the measure, in degrees, of the central angle of the open fan?
solution: The full circle has area \(\pi(6)^{2} = 36\pi\).
The fan is \(\frac{15\pi}{36\pi} = \frac{5}{12}\) of the circle.
The angle is \(\frac{5}{12} \cdot 360 = 150^{\circ}\).

items.stem: A straight fence touches a circular pond at exactly one point, \(T\), as shown. The pond has center \(O\) and a radius of 10 meters. A post \(P\) on the fence is 26 meters from \(O\). What is the distance, in meters, from the post to point \(T\)?
solution: The fence is tangent to the circle at \(T\), so radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to the fence and triangle \(OTP\) has a right angle at \(T\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This adds the squares, \(\sqrt{26^{2} + 10^{2}}\); \(OP\) is the hypotenuse, so subtract.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This subtracts the lengths, \(26 - 10\), instead of using the Pythagorean theorem.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the diameter, 20, in place of the radius: \(\sqrt{26^{2} - 20^{2}}\).

items.stem: In the circle with center \(O\), the radius is 4 and central angle \(AOB\) measures \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians. What is the length of chord \(AB\)?
solution: \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) radians is \(60^{\circ}\). Triangle \(AOB\) has \(OA = OB = 4\), so its base angles are equal: \(\frac{180 - 60}{2} = 60^{\circ}\).
All three angles are \(60^{\circ}\), so the triangle is equilateral and \(AB = 4\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(r\theta\), the length of arc \(AB\), not the straight chord.
explanation.B: Correct. Triangle \(AOB\) is equilateral, so \(AB = 4\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(r\sqrt{3}\) is the chord for a central angle of \(\frac{2\pi}{3}\) (\(120^{\circ}\)), not \(\frac{\pi}{3}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the height of the equilateral triangle \(AOB\), not the length of its side \(AB\).

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the line \(3x + 4y = 20\) intersects the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2}\), where \(r\) is a positive constant, at exactly one point. What is the value of \(r\)?
solution: Meeting at exactly one point means the line is tangent, so \(r\) equals the distance from the center \((0, 0)\) to the line.
(Or substitute \(y = \frac{20 - 3x}{4}\) into the circle and set the discriminant of the quadratic to 0.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(r^{2}\); the question asks for \(r\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This divides by \(3 + 4\) instead of \(\sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}} = 5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses the numerator 20 without dividing by \(\sqrt{3^{2} + 4^{2}}\).
explanation.D: Correct. The distance from the origin to the line is \(\frac{20}{5} = 4\).

items.stem: A circular fountain is surrounded by a walkway that is 3 meters wide everywhere, so the outer edge of the walkway is a circle with the same center as the fountain. The area of the walkway alone is \(51\pi\) square meters. What is the radius of the fountain, in meters?
solution: Let \(r\) be the radius of the fountain. The outer circle has radius \(r + 3\).

items.stem: In a circle with center \(O\), minor arc \(AB\) has the same length as the diameter of the circle. The area of sector \(AOB\) is what fraction of the area of the circle?
solution: Arc length \(= r\theta\) with \(\theta\) in radians. The arc equals \(2r\), so \(r\theta = 2r\) and \(\theta = 2\).
A full circle is \(2\pi\) radians, so the sector is \(\frac{2}{2\pi} = \frac{1}{\pi}\) of the circle (its area is the same fraction of the circle's area).

explanation.A: Correct. \(\theta = 2\) radians, and \(\frac{2}{2\pi} = \frac{1}{\pi}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats \(\theta = 2\) as degrees, \(\frac{2}{360}\); the formula \(s = r\theta\) gives \(\theta\) in radians.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This divides \(\theta = 2\) by \(\pi\) instead of \(2\pi\), the radian measure of a full circle.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This sets the arc equal to the radius, giving \(\theta = 1\); the arc equals the diameter, \(2r\).

items.stem: A square fountain base with sides 8 meters long sits inside a circular lawn in a park in Chennai, with all four corners of the square on the edge of the lawn, as shown. Grass covers the part of the lawn outside the square. What is the area, in square meters, of the part covered by grass?
solution: The diagonal of the square is a diameter of the circle: \(8\sqrt{2}\), so \(r = 4\sqrt{2}\) and \(r^{2} = 32\).
Circle area \(= 32\pi\); square area \(= 64\).
Grass area \(= 32\pi - 64\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses the side of the square, 8, as the radius; the radius is half the diagonal, \(4\sqrt{2}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the area of the whole lawn; the square's area, 64, still has to be subtracted.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the whole diagonal, \(8\sqrt{2}\), as the radius instead of half of it.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, a circle passes through the points \((0, 0)\), \((8, 0)\), and \((0, 6)\). What is the radius of the circle?
solution: The segments from \((0, 0)\) to \((8, 0)\) and to \((0, 6)\) are perpendicular, so the inscribed angle at the origin is \(90^{\circ}\).
A right inscribed angle intercepts a diameter, so the segment from \((8, 0)\) to \((0, 6)\) is a diameter: \(\sqrt{8^{2} + 6^{2}} = 10\).
The radius is \(\frac{10}{2} = 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 25 is \(r^{2}\); the radius is its square root.
explanation.B: Incorrect. 10 is the diameter, the distance from \((8, 0)\) to \((0, 6)\); the radius is half of it.
explanation.C: Correct. The diameter is 10, so the radius is 5.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This averages 8 and 6; the radius is not the mean of the intercepts.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the line \(y = k\), where \(k\) is a positive constant, intersects the circle \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 10y = 0\) at exactly one point. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Complete the square: \(x^{2} + (y - 5)^{2} = 25\). The center is \((0, 5)\) and the radius is 5.
A horizontal line touches the circle at exactly one point only at the top or the bottom of the circle: \(y = 5 + 5 = 10\) or \(y = 5 - 5 = 0\).

items.stem: A goat is tied with a 10-meter rope to one outside corner of a square shed whose sides are 6 meters long. The goat can move anywhere outside the shed that the rope allows, but it cannot enter the shed. What is the area, in square meters, of the region the goat can reach?
solution: Away from the shed, the goat sweeps \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a circle of radius 10: \(\frac{3}{4} \cdot 100\pi = 75\pi\).

Along each of the two walls that meet at the corner, the rope wraps around the next corner with \(10 - 6 = 4\) meters left, sweeping a quarter circle of radius 4 behind the shed: \(\frac{1}{4} \cdot 16\pi = 4\pi\) each.
These two quarter circles do not overlap (each reaches only 4 of the 6 meters along the back walls). Total: \(75\pi + 4\pi + 4\pi = 83\pi\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This adds two half circles of radius 4 (\(16\pi\)) instead of two quarter circles (\(8\pi\)).
explanation.B: Correct. \(75\pi + 2(4\pi) = 83\pi\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This counts only the three-quarter circle and misses the two regions the goat reaches by wrapping the rope around the shed's corners.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is a full circle of radius 10; the shed blocks one quarter of it.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x + 6y + c = 0\), where \(c\) is a constant, is a circle for which of the following values of \(c\)?
solution: Complete the square: \((x - 2)^{2} + (y + 3)^{2} = 13 - c\).
The graph is a circle only when the right side is positive: \(13 - c > 0\), so \(c < 13\).
Of the choices, only \(c = 12\) works (radius \(\sqrt{1} = 1\)).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the condition: \(c = 20\) gives \(r^{2} = -7\), and no points satisfy the equation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses the condition: \(c = 14\) gives \(r^{2} = -1\), and no points satisfy the equation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. With \(c = 13\) the right side is 0, so the graph is the single point \((2, -3)\), not a circle.
explanation.D: Correct. \(13 - 12 = 1 > 0\), so the graph is a circle of radius 1.

items.stem: On a running track, each end of a lane is a semicircle, and the two straight sections have the same length in every lane. Two runners each run one lap along the inside edge of their own lane. The semicircular ends of the outer runner's path have a radius 1.2 meters greater than those of the inner runner's path. How many more meters does the outer runner run in one lap than the inner runner?

choices.C: It cannot be determined without the radius of the inner runner's path.

solution: Let \(R\) be the radius of the inner path's ends. The two semicircles together make one full circle, so the inner lap is \(2L + 2\pi R\), where \(L\) is the length of a straight section.
The outer lap is \(2L + 2\pi(R + 1.2)\).
Difference: \(2\pi(R + 1.2) - 2\pi R = 2.4\pi\), whatever the values of \(R\) and \(L\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This doubles 1.2 as if it were a diameter: \(2\pi(2.4)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This counts the extra distance for only one semicircular end, \(\pi(1.2)\); there are two ends.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The radius cancels when the two laps are subtracted, so the difference can be found.
explanation.D: Correct. The \(R\) terms cancel, leaving \(2\pi(1.2) = 2.4\pi\).

items.stem: In a circle with center \(O\) and radius \(r\), chord \(AB\) has a length of 12, and central angle \(AOB\) measures \(120^{\circ}\). What is the value of \(r^{2}\)?
solution: Triangle \(AOB\) is isosceles with \(OA = OB = r\) and a \(120^{\circ}\) angle at \(O\), so its base angles are \(30^{\circ}\).
The perpendicular from \(O\) to \(AB\) splits it into two \(30^{\circ}\)-\(60^{\circ}\)-\(90^{\circ}\) triangles with long leg 6, so the hypotenuse is \(r = \frac{6 \cdot 2}{\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3}\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((3x^{2} + 5x - 2) - (x^{2} - 4x + 6)\)?
solution: Distribute the negative sign to every term in the second polynomial: \(3x^{2} + 5x - 2 - x^{2} + 4x - 6\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting only \(x^{2}\) and adding the other terms of the second polynomial, as if the negative sign applied to its first term only.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the two polynomials instead of subtracting them.
explanation.C: Correct. Subtracting every term of the second polynomial gives \(2x^{2} + 9x - 8\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the \(x\)-terms correctly but adding the constants: \(-2 + 6 = 4\) instead of \(-2 - 6 = -8\).

items.stem: A rectangular vegetable garden in Multan has a length of \((x + 5)\) meters and a width of \((x - 2)\) meters, as shown. Which expression represents the area of the garden, in square meters?
solution: Area of a rectangle = length \(\times\) width: \((x + 5)(x - 2)\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only the first terms and the last terms, leaving out the middle terms \(-2x\) and \(5x\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip on the constant term: \(5 \cdot (-2) = -10\), not \(10\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the perimeter, \(2(x + 5) + 2(x - 2)\), not the area.

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{x\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt[4]{x}}\)?
solution: Write each factor as a power of \(x\): \(x\sqrt{x} = x^{1} \cdot x^{\frac{1}{2}} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}\) and \(\sqrt[4]{x} = x^{\frac{1}{4}}\).
Dividing powers with the same base subtracts the exponents: \(\frac{3}{2} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\).
So the expression equals \(x^{\frac{5}{4}}\). Check with a calculator: for \(x = 16\), both give \(32\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the exponents, \(\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{8}\), instead of subtracting them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the exponents, \(\frac{3}{2} + \frac{1}{4}\), as if the fourth root were in the numerator.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the exponents, \(\frac{3}{2} \div \frac{1}{4} = 6\), instead of subtracting them.

items.stem: The expression \((7x - 2)(x + 6) - 3x(x + 4)\) is equivalent to \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: Expand the second term: \(3x(x + 4) = 3x^{2} + 12x\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{2}{x - 3} - \frac{1}{x + 2}\) for \(x \neq 3\) and \(x \neq -2\)?
solution: Use the common denominator \((x - 3)(x + 2) = x^{2} - x - 6\).
Rewrite each fraction: \(\frac{2(x + 2)}{(x - 3)(x + 2)} - \frac{x - 3}{(x - 3)(x + 2)}\).
Subtract the numerators, keeping the parentheses: \(2x + 4 - (x - 3) = 2x + 4 - x + 3 = x + 7\).
The result is \(\frac{x + 7}{x^{2} - x - 6}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting only \(x\) from \(2x + 4\) and then also subtracting \(3\): \(2x + 4 - x - 3\). The \(-3\) inside \(x - 3\) becomes \(+3\) when subtracted.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the original numerators, \(2 - 1\), over the common denominator without first multiplying each numerator by the missing factor.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \((x - 3)(x + 2)\) incorrectly; the product is \(x^{2} - x - 6\), not \(x^{2} - 6\).
explanation.D: Correct. Over the common denominator, the numerator is \(2(x + 2) - (x - 3) = x + 7\).

items.stem: A rectangular solar panel array has an area of \((6x^{2} + 7x - 20)\) square meters. The length of the array is \((3x - 4)\) meters, as shown. Which expression represents the perimeter of the array, in meters?
solution: The width is the area divided by the length. Factor the area: \(6x^{2} + 7x - 20 = (3x - 4)(2x + 5)\), so the width is \((2x + 5)\) meters.

explanation.A: Correct. The width is \(2x + 5\), so the perimeter is \(2(3x - 4) + 2(2x + 5) = 10x + 2\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the length and width once, \((3x - 4) + (2x + 5)\), which is half the perimeter.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when factoring, which gives a width of \(2x - 5\); but \((3x - 4)(2x - 5)\) has middle term \(-23x\), not \(7x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the width of the array, not its perimeter.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(2(x - 3)^{2} + 5(x - 3) - 12\)?
solution: Notice the repeated expression: let \(u = x - 3\). The expression becomes \(2u^{2} + 5u - 12\).
So the expression equals \((2x - 9)(x + 1)\). (Expanding both gives \(2x^{2} - 7x - 9\).)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \((2u - 3)(u + 4)\) with \(x\) written in place of \(u\); the result was never converted back using \(u = x - 3\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when substituting back; \((2x + 9)(x - 1) = 2x^{2} + 7x - 9\), whose middle term has the wrong sign.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of computing \(2(x - 3) - 3\) as \(2x - 3 - 3\) instead of \(2x - 6 - 3 = 2x - 9\).
explanation.D: Correct. With \(u = x - 3\), the expression is \((2u - 3)(u + 4) = (2x - 9)(x + 1)\).

items.stem: In the equation \((ax + 3)(bx + 7) = 15x^{2} + cx + 21\), \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants, and the equation is true for all values of \(x\). If \(a + b = 8\), what is one possible value of \(c\)?
solution: Expanding the left side gives \(abx^{2} + (7a + 3b)x + 21\), so \(ab = 15\) and \(c = 7a + 3b\).
Two numbers with sum \(8\) and product \(15\) are \(3\) and \(5\), so either \(a = 3,\ b = 5\) or \(a = 5,\ b = 3\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(5(x^{2} - 2) - 3x^{2}\)?
solution: Distribute the 5: \(5x^{2} - 10 - 3x^{2}\).
Combine the \(x^{2}\)-terms: \(5x^{2} - 3x^{2} = 2x^{2}\), so the expression is \(2x^{2} - 10\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(x^{2}\) by 5 and leaving \(-2\) unchanged.
explanation.B: Correct. Distributing the 5 and combining like terms gives \(2x^{2} - 10\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the exponents when combining like terms; \(5x^{2} - 3x^{2} = 2x^{2}\), and the exponent does not change.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3x^{2}\) instead of subtracting it.

items.stem: Sunita is making 3 identical gift boxes for her cousins in Kathmandu. Each box holds \(x\) sweets that cost 45 rupees each and one card that costs 20 rupees. The total cost, in rupees, of the 3 boxes is \(3(45x + 20)\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Multiply each term inside the parentheses by 3: \(3(45x) + 3(20)\).
This gives \(135x + 60\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of combining \(135x\) and \(60\), which are not like terms.
explanation.B: Correct. Multiplying both terms by 3 gives \(135x + 60\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(45x\) by 3; the 20 must also be multiplied by 3.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 3 to each term instead of multiplying each term by 3.

items.stem: For \(x \neq 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{12x^{8}}{4x^{2}}\)?
solution: Divide the coefficients: \(12 \div 4 = 3\).
Subtract the exponents: \(x^{8 - 2} = x^{6}\), so the expression is \(3x^{6}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the coefficients, \(12 - 4\), instead of dividing them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the exponents, which is the rule for multiplying powers, not dividing them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the exponents, \(8 \div 2\), instead of subtracting them.
explanation.D: Correct. Dividing the coefficients and subtracting the exponents gives \(3x^{6}\).

items.stem: The expression \((x - 4)(x + 9)\) is equivalent to \(x^{2} + bx + c\), where \(b\) and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(c\)?
solution: Multiply each term: \(x \cdot x + 9x - 4x + (-4)(9)\).
Combine like terms: \(x^{2} + 5x - 36\), so \(c = -36\).

items.stem: Theo had \((5x - 3)\) dollars and spent \((2x - 7)\) dollars of it. Which expression represents the amount of money, in dollars, Theo has left?
solution: Subtract the amount spent: \((5x - 3) - (2x - 7)\).
Distribute the negative sign: \(5x - 3 - 2x + 7\).
Combine like terms: \(3x + 4\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the two expressions instead of subtracting the amount spent.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of computing \(-3 + 7\) as \(-4\) instead of \(4\).
explanation.C: Correct. Subtracting \((2x - 7)\) from \((5x - 3)\) gives \(3x + 4\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting only \(2x\) and not distributing the negative sign to \(-7\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(x^{2} - 49\)?
solution: The expression is a difference of two squares: \(x^{2} - 7^{2}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(x^{2} - 14x + 49\), not \(x^{2} - 49\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(x^{2} - 48x - 49\), not \(x^{2} - 49\).
explanation.C: Correct. A difference of squares factors as \((x - 7)(x + 7)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(x^{2} + 14x + 49\); the constant term has the wrong sign and there is an extra \(x\)-term.

items.stem: A theater section has \((x + 6)\) rows, and each row has \((2x + 5)\) seats. Which expression represents the total number of seats in the section?
solution: Total seats = rows \(\times\) seats per row \(= (x + 6)(2x + 5)\).

explanation.A: Correct. Multiplying \((x + 6)(2x + 5)\) gives \(2x^{2} + 17x + 30\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(6 + 5\) as the coefficient of \(x\); the middle terms are \(x \cdot 5 + 6 \cdot 2x = 17x\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only the first terms and the last terms and leaving out \(5x\) and \(12x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the number of rows and the number of seats per row instead of multiplying.

items.stem: When the expression \(4x^{2} - 3(2x - 7) + x\) is simplified, what is the coefficient of \(x\)?
solution: Combine the \(x\)-terms: \(-6x + x = -5x\). The expression is \(4x^{2} - 5x + 21\), so the coefficient of \(x\) is \(-5\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((2x^{3})^{4}\)?
solution: Raise each factor to the fourth power: \(2^{4} \cdot (x^{3})^{4}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying 2 by 4 instead of raising 2 to the fourth power.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the exponents 3 and 4 instead of multiplying them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of raising only \(x^{3}\) to the fourth power and not the coefficient 2.

items.stem: A teacher buys \(3x\) packs of pencils. Each pack contains \(4x\) pencils. Which expression represents the total number of pencils the teacher buys?
solution: Total pencils = packs \(\times\) pencils per pack \(= (3x)(4x)\).
Multiply the coefficients and the variables: \(12x^{2}\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the coefficients 3 and 4 instead of multiplying them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the coefficients but not multiplying \(x\) by \(x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3x\) and \(4x\) instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(2x^{2} + 7x - 15\)?
solution: Look for factors \((2x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -15\) and \(2q + p = 7\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(2x^{2} + x - 15\); the factors 3 and 5 are in the wrong places.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(2x^{2} - x - 15\); the factors 3 and 5 are in the wrong places.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(2x^{2} - 7x - 15\); the signs of the factors are switched.
explanation.D: Correct. Expanding gives \(2x^{2} + 10x - 3x - 15 = 2x^{2} + 7x - 15\).

items.stem: The expression \((2x - 3)^{2} - 4x(x - 5)\) is equivalent to \(ax + b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(a\)?
solution: Expand the square: \((2x - 3)^{2} = 4x^{2} - 12x + 9\).
Expand the product: \(4x(x - 5) = 4x^{2} - 20x\).

items.stem: Imran, a student in Lahore, scored \((x + 14)\), \((2x - 5)\), and \((3x + 9)\) points on three quizzes. Which expression represents the mean of his three quiz scores?
solution: Divide by 3: \(\frac{6x + 18}{3} = 2x + 6\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing only \(6x\) by 3; the constant 18 must also be divided by 3.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the sum by 2 instead of by 3, the number of quizzes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the sum of the three scores; it still must be divided by 3 to find the mean.
explanation.D: Correct. The sum is \(6x + 18\), and dividing by 3 gives \(2x + 6\).

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(\sqrt{x}\right)^{3}\)?
solution: Write the square root as a power: \(\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\).
Multiply the exponents: \(\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{3} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of inverting the exponent; \(x^{\frac{2}{3}}\) is the cube root of \(x^{2}\).
explanation.B: Correct. \(\left(x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{3} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\) instead of multiplying them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying 3 by 2 instead of by \(\frac{1}{2}\); a square root is the power \(\frac{1}{2}\).

items.stem: A museum lowers its ticket price from 18 dollars by \(d\) dollars. The museum's daily ticket revenue, in dollars, is then \((18 - d)(150 + 10d)\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Combine like terms: \(-10d^{2} + 30d + 2{,}700\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only the first terms and the last terms and leaving out \(180d\) and \(-150d\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(-d \cdot 150\) as \(+150d\).
explanation.C: Correct. Expanding and combining \(180d - 150d\) gives \(-10d^{2} + 30d + 2{,}700\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(-d \cdot 10d\) as \(+10d^{2}\).

items.stem: The expression \((x^{2} + 3x - 2)(x - 4)\) is equivalent to \(x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + 8\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: The \(x\)-terms come from \(3x \cdot (-4)\) and \(-2 \cdot x\).
(The full product is \(x^{3} - x^{2} - 14x + 8\).)

items.stem: A cyclist rides \((x^{2} - 9)\) kilometers in \((x - 3)\) hours, where \(x > 3\). Which expression represents the cyclist's average speed, in kilometers per hour?
solution: Average speed is distance divided by time: \(\frac{x^{2} - 9}{x - 3}\).
Factor the numerator: \(\frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x - 3}\).
Since \(x > 3\), cancel \(x - 3\): the speed is \(x + 3\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the distance by the time instead of dividing.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring \(x^{2} - 9\) as \((x - 3)^{2}\); the correct factors are \((x - 3)(x + 3)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the time by the distance, which gives hours per kilometer.

items.stem: For \(x \neq 5\) and \(x \neq -5\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{2} + 5x}{x^{2} - 25}\)?
solution: Factor the numerator: \(x^{2} + 5x = x(x + 5)\).
Factor the denominator: \(x^{2} - 25 = (x - 5)(x + 5)\).
Cancel the common factor \(x + 5\): \(\frac{x}{x - 5}\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(\frac{x(x + 5)}{(x - 5)(x + 5)} = \frac{x}{x - 5}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of cancelling the factor \(x\) from the numerator instead of the common factor \(x + 5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of cancelling the \(x^{2}\)-terms, which are terms of a sum, not common factors.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of cancelling \(x - 5\) instead of \(x + 5\); only \(x + 5\) appears in both the numerator and the denominator.

items.stem: A carpenter cuts a board that is \((8x + 20)\) inches long into 4 pieces of equal length and then trims 3 inches off each piece. Which expression represents the length, in inches, of each trimmed piece?
solution: Each piece is \(\frac{8x + 20}{4} = 2x + 5\) inches long before trimming.
Trim 3 inches: \(2x + 5 - 3 = 2x + 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing only \(8x\) by 4 and leaving 20 undivided.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of trimming 3 inches from the whole board instead of from each piece.
explanation.C: Correct. Each piece is \(2x + 5\) inches, and trimming 3 inches leaves \(2x + 2\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the length of each piece before the 3 inches are trimmed off.

items.stem: Anil, who lives in Jaipur, saves \((x + 250)\) rupees each week for 8 weeks. He then spends \((3x - 400)\) rupees on a gift. The amount, in rupees, he has left is equivalent to \(ax + b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
Which of the following is equivalent to \(4x^{2} - 12x + 9\)?
solution: The first and last terms are squares: \(4x^{2} = (2x)^{2}\) and \(9 = 3^{2}\).
The middle term is \(-2(2x)(3) = -12x\), so the expression is a perfect square: \((2x - 3)^{2}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(4x^{2} + 12x + 9\); the middle term has the wrong sign.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(4x^{2} - 13x + 9\); its first and last terms match, but its middle term does not.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This expression expands to \(4x^{2} - 9\), a difference of squares with no \(x\)-term.

items.stem: A food truck sets the price of a meal at \(p\) dollars. Its daily revenue, in dollars, is \(-2p^{2} + 60p\), and its daily cost, in dollars, is \(-3p + 150\). Profit is revenue minus cost. Which expression represents the food truck's daily profit, in dollars?
solution: Distribute the negative sign: \(-2p^{2} + 60p + 3p - 150\).
Combine like terms: \(-2p^{2} + 63p - 150\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 150 instead of subtracting it.
explanation.B: Correct. Subtracting the cost gives \(-2p^{2} + 63p - 150\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting \(3p\) instead of \(-3p\); subtracting \(-3p\) adds \(3p\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the revenue and the cost instead of subtracting the cost.

items.stem: For \(x \neq 0\) and \(x \neq -2\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{x^{2} - 4}{3x} \cdot \frac{6x^{2}}{x + 2}\)?
solution: Simplify \(\frac{6x^{2}}{3x} = 2x\): the expression is \(2x(x - 2)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of inverting \(\frac{6x^{2}}{3x}\) to \(\frac{3x}{6x^{2}}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of cancelling \(x - 2\) instead of \(x + 2\).
explanation.C: Correct. After cancelling \(x + 2\), \(\frac{6x^{2}}{3x} = 2x\), leaving \(2x(x - 2)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of cancelling all of \(x^{2}\) with \(x\); \(\frac{x^{2}}{x} = x\), so a factor of \(x\) remains.

items.stem: The expression \((4x - 1)(x + 3) - 11x\) is equivalent to \(ax^{2} + c\), where \(a\) and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(a - c\)?
A parking garage has 3 levels with \((4n + 10)\) parking spaces each and 2 levels with \((5n - 4)\) parking spaces each. Which expression represents the total number of parking spaces in the garage?
solution: Distribute: \(12n + 30 + 10n - 8\).
Combine like terms: \(22n + 22\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only the \(n\)-terms by the number of levels and adding the constants \(10 - 4\) once.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 8 instead of subtracting it; \(2(-4) = -8\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the number of spaces on one level of each type, not on all 5 levels.

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\)?
solution: A negative exponent means a reciprocal: \(x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}}\).
The exponent \(\frac{1}{2}\) means a square root, so the expression is \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of treating the negative exponent as making the value negative; a negative exponent gives a reciprocal.
explanation.B: Correct. \(x^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{x^{\frac{1}{2}}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of inverting the exponent \(\frac{1}{2}\) to 2; the exponent \(\frac{1}{2}\) means a square root.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(x\) by the exponent \(-\frac{1}{2}\) instead of using it as a power.

items.stem: Priyanka buys \((2x + 3)\) kilograms of rice at a shop in Chennai. The rice costs \((x + 40)\) rupees per kilogram. Which expression represents the total cost, in rupees, of the rice?
solution: Total cost = kilograms \(\times\) price per kilogram \(= (2x + 3)(x + 40)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of leaving out the product \(3 \cdot x\) when expanding.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only the first terms and the last terms and leaving out \(80x\) and \(3x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the quantity and the price instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: The expression \(x^{3} - 64\) is equivalent to \((x - 4)(x^{2} + ax + b)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(a + b\)?
solution: Match coefficients with \(x^{3} - 64\): \(a - 4 = 0\), so \(a = 4\), and \(-4b = -64\), so \(b = 16\).

items.stem: Leena runs 6 kilometers at an average speed of \(x\) kilometers per hour and then runs another 6 kilometers at an average speed of \((x + 2)\) kilometers per hour. Her total running time, in hours, is \(\frac{6}{x} + \frac{6}{x + 2}\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Use the common denominator \(x(x + 2) = x^{2} + 2x\).
Rewrite: \(\frac{6(x + 2)}{x(x + 2)} + \frac{6x}{x(x + 2)}\).
Add the numerators: \(6x + 12 + 6x = 12x + 12\), giving \(\frac{12x + 12}{x^{2} + 2x}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the numerators and adding the denominators, which is not how fractions are added.
explanation.B: Correct. Over the common denominator \(x^{2} + 2x\), the numerator is \(6(x + 2) + 6x = 12x + 12\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \(6(x + 2)\) as \(6x + 2\) instead of \(6x + 12\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the original numerators over the common denominator without multiplying each by the missing factor.

items.stem:
For \(x 
eq 3\), \(x 
eq -3\), \(x 
eq 4\), and \(x 
eq -5\), which of the following is equivalent to \( rac{x^{2} - x - 12}{x^{2} - 9} \div  rac{x - 4}{x + 5}\)?
solution: Dividing by a fraction is multiplying by its reciprocal: \(\frac{x^{2} - x - 12}{x^{2} - 9} \cdot \frac{x + 5}{x - 4}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring \(x^{2} - x - 12\) as \((x - 4)(x - 3)\); the correct factors are \((x - 4)(x + 3)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying by \(\frac{x - 4}{x + 5}\) instead of by its reciprocal.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the reciprocal of the correct expression.

items.stem: Pump A alone can fill a tank in \(x\) hours, and pump B alone can fill the same tank in \((x + 4)\) hours. Working together, the two pumps fill the tank in \(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x + 4}}\) hours. Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Add the rates: \(\frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{x + 4} = \frac{(x + 4) + x}{x(x + 4)} = \frac{2x + 4}{x^{2} + 4x}\).
Take the reciprocal: \(\frac{x^{2} + 4x}{2x + 4}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the two times, \(x + (x + 4)\); working together takes less time than either pump alone.
explanation.B: Correct. The combined rate is \(\frac{2x + 4}{x^{2} + 4x}\), and its reciprocal is \(\frac{x^{2} + 4x}{2x + 4}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the combined rate in tanks per hour; it still must be inverted to give the time.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of averaging the two times instead of combining the rates.

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), the expression \(\sqrt{18x} \cdot \sqrt{2x^{3}}\) is equivalent to \(kx^{2}\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Multiply under one radical: \(\sqrt{18x \cdot 2x^{3}} = \sqrt{36x^{4}}\).

items.stem: For \(x > 0\) and \(y > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\left(27x^{6}y^{3}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}\)?
solution: Apply the exponent to each factor: \(27^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot (x^{6})^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot (y^{3})^{\frac{2}{3}}\).
The expression is \(9x^{4}y^{2}\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(\frac{2}{3}\) to the exponents of \(x\) and \(y\) instead of multiplying them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying 27 by \(\frac{2}{3}\) instead of raising 27 to the power \(\frac{2}{3}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the cube root of 27 but not squaring it.

items.stem: An auditorium has \((2x^{2} + 19x + 35)\) seats arranged in \((x + 7)\) rows, with the same number of seats in each row. Which expression represents the number of seats in each row?
solution: Seats per row \(= \frac{2x^{2} + 19x + 35}{x + 7}\).
Factor the numerator: \(2x^{2} + 19x + 35 = (x + 7)(2x + 5)\).
Cancel \(x + 7\): each row has \(2x + 5\) seats.

explanation.A: Correct. \((x + 7)(2x + 5) = 2x^{2} + 19x + 35\), so each row has \(2x + 5\) seats.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of ignoring the leading coefficient 2; \((x + 7)(x + 5) = x^{2} + 12x + 35\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This expression times \(x + 7\) gives \(2x^{2} + 9x - 35\); the sign of 5 is wrong.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the number of rows from the number of seats instead of dividing.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((x + 2)^{3}\)?
solution: Combine like terms: \(x^{3} + 6x^{2} + 12x + 8\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of cubing each term separately; \((a + b)^{3} \neq a^{3} + b^{3}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring \(x + 2\) as \(x^{2} + 4\) and then multiplying by \(x + 2\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of using the coefficients 1, 3, 3, 1 without the powers of 2 in the middle terms.

items.stem: An orchard has \((2x + 5)\) rows of trees with \((x + 9)\) trees in each row. A storm destroys \(7x\) of the trees. The number of trees remaining can be written as \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: Subtract the destroyed trees: \(2x^{2} + 23x + 45 - 7x = 2x^{2} + 16x + 45\), so \(b = 16\).

items.stem: For \(x \neq 2\) and \(x \neq -2\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{x + 1}{x^{2} - 4} - \frac{1}{x - 2}\)?
solution: Since \(x^{2} - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)\), rewrite the second fraction: \(\frac{1}{x - 2} = \frac{x + 2}{x^{2} - 4}\).
Subtract the numerators: \((x + 1) - (x + 2) = -1\).
The expression is \(-\frac{1}{x^{2} - 4}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the numerators \(x + 1\) and \(x + 2\) instead of subtracting.
explanation.B: Correct. Over the common denominator, the numerator is \((x + 1) - (x + 2) = -1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting only \(x\) from \(x + 1\) and then adding 2: \(x + 1 - x + 2\). The whole numerator \(x + 2\) must be subtracted.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the original numerators, \((x + 1) - 1\), without rewriting the second fraction over the common denominator.

items.stem: A recipe calls for \(\frac{x}{3}\) cups of flour for the dough and \(\frac{x + 4}{6}\) cups of flour for the topping. Which expression represents the total amount of flour, in cups, the recipe calls for?
solution: Use the common denominator 6: \(\frac{x}{3} = \frac{2x}{6}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of changing the denominator of \(\frac{x}{3}\) to 6 without multiplying its numerator by 2.
explanation.B: Correct. \(\frac{2x}{6} + \frac{x + 4}{6} = \frac{3x + 4}{6}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the numerators and adding the denominators.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the two amounts instead of adding them.

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{\sqrt{12x^{5}}}{\sqrt{3x}}\)?
solution: Combine under one radical: \(\sqrt{\frac{12x^{5}}{3x}} = \sqrt{4x^{4}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting 3 from 12 under the radical instead of dividing: \(\sqrt{9x^{4}}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the square root of \(x^{4}\) but not of 4.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the square root of 4 but not of \(x^{4}\).

items.stem: The expression \(2x^{2} - 12x + 23\) can be written as \(2(x - h)^{2} + k\), where \(h\) and \(k\) are constants. What is the value of \(h + k\)?
solution: Factor 2 from the \(x\)-terms: \(2(x^{2} - 6x) + 23\).

items.stem: A group of \(n\) hikers shares the 480-dollar cost of a cabin equally. If 4 more hikers join the group and the cost is shared equally among everyone, each of the original hikers pays \(\frac{480}{n} - \frac{480}{n + 4}\) dollars less. Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Use the common denominator \(n(n + 4) = n^{2} + 4n\).
The numerator is \(480(n + 4) - 480n = 1{,}920\).
The expression is \(\frac{1{,}920}{n^{2} + 4n}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the two fractions instead of subtracting them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of computing the numerator \(480(n + 4) - 480n\) as 480 instead of \(480 \cdot 4\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of expanding the denominator \(n(n + 4)\) as \(n^{2} + 4\) instead of \(n^{2} + 4n\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((3x^{2} - 2x)(x + 4) - 3x^{3}\)?

explanation.A: Correct. The product is \(3x^{3} + 10x^{2} - 8x\), and subtracting \(3x^{3}\) leaves \(10x^{2} - 8x\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of leaving out the product \((-2x)(x) = -2x^{2}\) when expanding.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \((-2x)(4)\) as \(+8x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3x^{3}\) instead of subtracting it.

items.stem: A bakery in Colombo makes \(n\) cakes each day. Its daily revenue, in rupees, is \(n(900 - 5n)\), and its daily cost, in rupees, is \((n + 20)(300 - n)\). Which expression represents the bakery's daily profit (revenue minus cost), in rupees?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the cost's constant term 6,000 instead of subtracting it.
explanation.B: Correct. Revenue minus cost is \(-4n^{2} + 620n - 6{,}000\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting \(n^{2}\) instead of \(-n^{2}\); subtracting \(-n^{2}\) adds \(n^{2}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of combining \(300n\) and \(-20n\) in the cost as \(320n\) instead of \(280n\).

items.stem: For \(x \neq 1\) and \(x \neq -1\), \(\frac{3}{x + 1} + \frac{2}{x - 1} = \frac{ax + b}{x^{2} - 1}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(a + b\)?
solution: Use the common denominator \((x + 1)(x - 1) = x^{2} - 1\).
The numerator is \(3(x - 1) + 2(x + 1) = 3x - 3 + 2x + 2 = 5x - 1\).

items.stem: In the polynomial \(2x^{3} + kx^{2} - 5x + 6\), \(k\) is a constant. If \(x - 2\) is a factor of the polynomial, what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: If \(x - 2\) is a factor, the polynomial equals 0 when \(x = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of solving \(4k = -12\) with a sign error.
explanation.B: Correct. Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(12 + 4k = 0\), so \(k = -3\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \(k(2)^{2}\) as \(2k\) instead of \(4k\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of substituting \(x = -2\) instead of \(x = 2\); the factor \(x - 2\) means the polynomial is 0 at \(x = 2\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((x^{2} + 3)^{2} - 4x^{2}\)?
solution: The expression is a difference of squares: \(A^{2} - B^{2}\) with \(A = x^{2} + 3\) and \(B = 2x\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring \(x^{2} + 3\) as \(x^{4} + 9\) and leaving out the middle term \(6x^{2}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(x^{2} - 3\) instead of \(x^{2} + 3\); this product equals \((x^{2} - 3)^{2} - 4x^{2}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(4x\) instead of \(\sqrt{4x^{2}} = 2x\) as the second square root.

items.stem: A courier drives \(d\) kilometers from a depot to a customer at an average speed of \(x\) kilometers per hour and returns along the same route at an average speed of \(y\) kilometers per hour. The average speed for the whole trip is the total distance divided by the total time, \(\frac{2d}{\frac{d}{x} + \frac{d}{y}}\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Total time: \(\frac{d}{x} + \frac{d}{y} = \frac{dy + dx}{xy} = \frac{d(x + y)}{xy}\).
Divide: \(2d \div \frac{d(x + y)}{xy} = \frac{2d \cdot xy}{d(x + y)}\).
Cancel \(d\): \(\frac{2xy}{x + y}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of dropping the factor 2 from the total distance \(2d\).
explanation.B: Correct. \(\frac{2d \cdot xy}{d(x + y)} = \frac{2xy}{x + y}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the reciprocal of the correct expression: total time divided by total distance.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the mean of the two speeds; the trip spends more time at the slower speed, so the average speed is not this mean.

items.stem: If \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 20\) and \(xy = 8\), what is the value of \((x - y)^{2}\)?
solution: Substitute: \(20 - 2(8) = 4\).

items.stem: If \(x - \frac{1}{x} = 3\), what is the value of \(x^{2} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\)?
solution: Square both sides: \(\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^{2} = x^{2} - 2 + \frac{1}{x^{2}} = 9\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting 2 instead of adding 2 after squaring: the middle term of the square is \(-2\), so 2 must be added to 9.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring each term separately, as if \(\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^{2} = x^{2} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\), and leaving out the middle term.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is a possible value of \(x + \frac{1}{x}\), not of \(x^{2} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\).

items.stem: The expression \(x^{2} + bx + c\), where \(b\) and \(c\) are constants, is equivalent to \((x + 4)^{2} - 9\). It is also equivalent to \((x + m)(x + n)\), where \(m\) and \(n\) are constants and \(m < n\). What is the value of \(m\)?
solution: Write \(9 = 3^{2}\) and use the difference of squares: \((x + 4)^{2} - 3^{2} = (x + 4 - 3)(x + 4 + 3)\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring \((x - 4)^{2} - 9\) instead; the sign of 4 was changed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of writing the factors as \((x - 1)(x + 7)\); \(x + 4 - 3 = x + 1\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the value of \(n\), the greater of the two constants.

items.stem: In a cricket league in Pakistan, each of \(n\) teams plays every other team exactly once, so the league has \(\frac{n(n - 1)}{2}\) matches. If 3 new teams join the league and the same format is used, which expression represents the number of additional matches the league will have?
solution: With \(n + 3\) teams, the number of matches is \(\frac{(n + 3)(n + 2)}{2} = \frac{n^{2} + 5n + 6}{2}\).
Subtract the original number: \(\frac{n^{2} + 5n + 6 - (n^{2} - n)}{2} = \frac{6n + 6}{2}\).
This simplifies to \(3n + 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of forgetting to divide the difference of the products by 2.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the total number of matches after the new teams join, not the number of additional matches.
explanation.C: Correct. The difference is \(\frac{6n + 6}{2} = 3n + 3\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting \(n^{2} - n\) as \(n^{2} + n\): \(\frac{4n + 6}{2}\).

items.stem: If \(2^{a} = 5\), what is the value of \(4^{a + 1}\)?
Which of the following is equivalent to \(4(2x - 5) + 3x\)?
solution: Distribute the 4 to both terms in the parentheses: \(8x - 20 + 3x\).
Combine the \(x\)-terms: \(8x + 3x = 11x\), so the expression is \(11x - 20\).

explanation.A: Correct. Distributing gives \(8x - 20 + 3x\), which simplifies to \(11x - 20\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: \(4 \cdot (-5)\) is \(-20\), not \(20\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(2x\) by 4 and leaving \(-5\) unchanged.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(4 + 2\) instead of multiplying \(4 \cdot 2\), giving \(6x\) instead of \(8x\).

items.stem: The side lengths of a triangular flower bed, in feet, are \((2x + 1)\), \((3x - 4)\), and \((x + 6)\), as shown. Which expression represents the perimeter of the flower bed, in feet?
solution: The perimeter is the sum of the three side lengths: \((2x + 1) + (3x - 4) + (x + 6)\).
Combine the \(x\)-terms: \(2x + 3x + x = 6x\). Combine the constants: \(1 - 4 + 6 = 3\).
The perimeter is \(6x + 3\) feet.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the \(x\)'s together instead of adding like terms: \(2x + 3x + x\) is \(6x\), not \(6x^{3}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(-4\) as \(+4\) when adding the constants.
explanation.C: Correct. Adding the three sides gives \(6x + 3\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of doubling the sum of the sides, as if using the perimeter rule for a rectangle.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((2x^{3})(5x^{4})\)?
solution: Multiply the coefficients: \(2 \cdot 5 = 10\).
Multiply the powers of \(x\) by adding the exponents: \(x^{3} \cdot x^{4} = x^{3 + 4} = x^{7}\).
The product is \(10x^{7}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the exponents \(3 \cdot 4\) instead of adding them.
explanation.B: Correct. Multiply the coefficients and add the exponents: \(10x^{7}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the coefficients and multiplying the exponents, the reverse of the correct rules.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the coefficients \(2 + 5\) instead of multiplying them.

items.stem: The expression \((5x^{2} - 3x + 8) + (2x^{2} + 7x - 11)\) is equivalent to \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(c\)?
Ayesha buys 5 packets of biscuits at a shop in Karachi. Each packet costs \((p + 30)\) rupees. Which expression represents the total cost, in rupees, of the 5 packets?
solution: The total cost is 5 times the cost of one packet: \(5(p + 30)\).
Distribute the 5 to both terms: \(5p + 150\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of combining \(5p\) and 30 into one term; they are not like terms.
explanation.B: Correct. Five packets cost \(5(p + 30) = 5p + 150\) rupees.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing 30 by 5 instead of multiplying.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(p\) by 5 and not the 30 rupees.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(6x^{2} + 9x\)?
solution: The greatest common factor of \(6x^{2}\) and \(9x\) is \(3x\).
Divide each term by \(3x\): \(6x^{2} \div 3x = 2x\) and \(9x \div 3x = 3\).
So \(6x^{2} + 9x = 3x(2x + 3)\). Expanding the result gives back the original expression.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing only the first term by \(3x\); \(3x(2x + 9) = 6x^{2} + 27x\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of combining unlike terms; \(6x^{2}\) and \(9x\) cannot be added.
explanation.C: Correct. Factoring out \(3x\) gives \(3x(2x + 3)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring \(x^{2}\) out of both terms, but \(9x\) does not contain \(x^{2}\); this expression equals \(6x^{2} + 9x^{3}\).

items.stem: A rectangular poster has a length of \((4x - 1)\) inches and a width of \((x + 3)\) inches, as shown. Which expression represents the perimeter of the poster, in inches?
solution: The perimeter of a rectangle is \(2(\text{length}) + 2(\text{width})\): \(2(4x - 1) + 2(x + 3)\).
Distribute: \(8x - 2 + 2x + 6\).
Combine like terms: \(10x + 4\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the sum of one length and one width only; the perimeter includes each side twice.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(-1\) as \(+1\), which gives \(2(5x + 4)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the area of the poster, \((4x - 1)(x + 3)\), not the perimeter.

items.stem: The expression \(3(x + 4) - (x - 2)\) is equivalent to \(ax + b\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: Distribute: \(3x + 12 - x + 2\). The negative sign changes \(-2\) to \(+2\).
Combine like terms: \(2x + 14\), so \(b = 14\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \((x + 6)^{2}\)?
solution: Write the square as a product: \((x + 6)(x + 6)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of computing \(6 \cdot 2\) instead of \(6^{2}\) for the constant term.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of including the middle product \(6x\) only once instead of twice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring each term separately; \((x + 6)^{2}\) also has the middle term \(12x\).

items.stem: A theater charges 15 dollars for an adult ticket and 9 dollars for a child ticket. A group buys \(a\) adult tickets and \((a + 2)\) child tickets. Which expression represents the total cost, in dollars, of the tickets?
solution: The adult tickets cost \(15a\) dollars and the child tickets cost \(9(a + 2) = 9a + 18\) dollars.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(a\) by 9 and not the 2 extra child tickets.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 9 and 2 instead of multiplying them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of charging the 2 extra tickets at the adult price of 15 dollars instead of the child price.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(x^{2} - 5x - 24\)?
solution: Look for two numbers whose product is \(-24\) and whose sum is \(-5\): they are \(-8\) and \(3\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. These numbers have the right product, \(-24\), but their sum is \(-10\), not \(-5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of reversing the signs; \((x + 8)(x - 3) = x^{2} + 5x - 24\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. These numbers have the right product, \(-24\), but their sum is \(-2\), not \(-5\).

items.stem: The expression \((3x - 1)^{2} - (x + 2)^{2}\) is equivalent to \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(a + b + c\)?
solution: Shortcut: \(a + b + c\) is the value of the expression at \(x = 1\): \(2^{2} - 3^{2} = -5\).

items.stem: A rectangular courtyard in Lahore is \((2x + 3)\) meters long and \((x + 4)\) meters wide. A square fountain with sides of \(x\) meters is built in the courtyard, as shown. Which expression represents the area, in square meters, of the courtyard that is not covered by the fountain?
solution: The area of the courtyard is \((2x + 3)(x + 4) = 2x^{2} + 8x + 3x + 12 = 2x^{2} + 11x + 12\).
The area of the fountain is \(x^{2}\).

explanation.A: Correct. The courtyard area minus the fountain area is \(x^{2} + 11x + 12\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of an expansion slip: the \(x\)-terms of \((2x + 3)(x + 4)\) are \(8x + 3x = 11x\), not \(7x\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the area of the whole courtyard; the fountain's area still has to be subtracted.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the fountain's area instead of subtracting it.

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(x^{\frac{2}{3}}\)?
solution: A rational exponent \(\frac{m}{n}\) means the \(n\)th root of the \(m\)th power: \(x^{\frac{m}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{x^{m}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of treating the exponent as a coefficient; an exponent is not multiplied by the base.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of swapping the roles of the numerator and denominator: \(\sqrt{x^{3}} = x^{\frac{3}{2}}\).
explanation.C: Correct. The denominator 3 gives the cube root and the numerator 2 gives the power: \(\sqrt[3]{x^{2}}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This equals \(x^{-\frac{2}{3}}\); a reciprocal corresponds to a negative exponent, which the expression does not have.

items.stem: A jacket has a list price of \(p\) dollars. It is sold at a 15% discount, and then an 8% sales tax is added to the discounted price. The total amount paid, in dollars, is given by the expression \(0.85p + 0.08(0.85p)\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Multiply: \(0.85 \cdot 1.08 = 0.918\), so the expression is equivalent to \(0.918p\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting 0.08 from 0.85 instead of adding the tax.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the factors, \(0.85 + 0.08\), instead of multiplying \(0.85\) by \(1.08\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is only the tax, \(0.08(0.85p)\); the discounted price must be added to it.

items.stem: In the equation \((kx + 7)(4x - 3) = 12x^{2} + bx - 21\), \(k\) and \(b\) are constants, and the equation is true for all values of \(x\). What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: Expand the left side: \(4kx^{2} - 3kx + 28x - 21 = 4kx^{2} + (28 - 3k)x - 21\).
Match the \(x^{2}\) coefficients: \(4k = 12\), so \(k = 3\).

items.stem: A square photo has sides of \(s\) centimeters. It is placed in a square frame that adds a border 3 centimeters wide on every side, as shown. Which expression represents the area, in square centimeters, of the border?
solution: Each side of the framed square is \(s + 3 + 3 = s + 6\) centimeters, so its area is \((s + 6)^{2} = s^{2} + 12s + 36\).
Subtract the area of the photo, \(s^{2}\): \(s^{2} + 12s + 36 - s^{2} = 12s + 36\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \((s + 6)^{2}\) as \(s^{2} + 36\), leaving out the middle term \(12s\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the 3-centimeter border to only one side of the photo, using \((s + 3)^{2} - s^{2}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the area of the whole framed square; the area of the photo still has to be subtracted.

items.stem: For \(x \neq 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\frac{6x^{3} + 4x^{2} - 10x}{2x}\)?
solution: Divide each term of the numerator by \(2x\).
The expression is equivalent to \(3x^{2} + 2x - 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 1 to each exponent, as if multiplying by \(x\) instead of dividing.
explanation.B: Correct. Dividing each term by \(2x\) gives \(3x^{2} + 2x - 5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing \(-10x\) by \(x\) only, instead of by \(2x\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing only the coefficients by 2 and not dividing the powers of \(x\) by \(x\).

items.stem: A company sells a gadget at a price of \(p\) dollars. At this price, it expects to sell \((200 - 4p)\) gadgets. Revenue is the price per gadget times the number of gadgets sold. Which expression represents the expected revenue, in dollars?
solution: Revenue is \(p(200 - 4p)\).
Distribute \(p\) to both terms: \(200p - 4p^{2}\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of combining \(200\) and \(-4p\) into \(196\) before multiplying; they are not like terms.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(4p\) by \(p\) and not the 200.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \(p \cdot 4p\) as \(4p\) instead of \(4p^{2}\).

items.stem: A box has a square base with sides of \((x + 2)\) centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. The volume of the box, in cubic centimeters, can be written as \(ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: The volume is base area times height: \(5(x + 2)^{2}\).

items.stem:
For \(x 
eq 0\), \(x 
eq 2\), and \(x 
eq -2\), which of the following is equivalent to \( rac{1 +  rac{2}{x}}{1 -  rac{4}{x^{2}}}\)?
solution: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by \(x^{2}\): \(\frac{x^{2} + 2x}{x^{2} - 4}\).
Cancel the common factor \(x + 2\): \(\frac{x}{x - 2}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the reciprocal of the correct expression; the numerator and denominator were switched.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of dropping the factor \(x\) from the numerator: \(x^{2} + 2x = x(x + 2)\), not \(x + 2\).
explanation.C: Correct. Clearing the small fractions and cancelling \(x + 2\) gives \(\frac{x}{x - 2}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip in the numerator: writing \(1 + \frac{2}{x}\) as \(\frac{x - 2}{x}\) and then cancelling \(x - 2\) instead of \(x + 2\).

items.stem: An online seller's total cost to make and ship \(n\) mugs is \((2.5n + 40)\) dollars, and each mug sells for 7 dollars. The seller's profit per mug is the total profit divided by the number of mugs. Which expression represents the profit per mug, in dollars, when \(n\) mugs are sold?
solution: Total profit is revenue minus cost: \(7n - (2.5n + 40) = 4.5n - 40\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the cost per mug, 2.5, to the price instead of subtracting it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying 40 by \(n\) instead of dividing it by \(n\).
explanation.C: Correct. The total profit \(4.5n - 40\) divided by \(n\) is \(4.5 - \frac{40}{n}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the total profit for \(n\) mugs; it still has to be divided by \(n\).

items.stem: For \(x > 0\), which of the following is equivalent to \(\sqrt{50x^{3}} - x\sqrt{8x}\)?
solution: Simplify each radical: \(\sqrt{50x^{3}} = \sqrt{25x^{2} \cdot 2x} = 5x\sqrt{2x}\) and \(x\sqrt{8x} = x\sqrt{4 \cdot 2x} = 2x\sqrt{2x}\).
The terms are now like terms: \(5x\sqrt{2x} - 2x\sqrt{2x} = 3x\sqrt{2x}\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(5x\sqrt{2x} - 2x\sqrt{2x} = 3x\sqrt{2x}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the numbers under the radicals, \(50 - 8\); a difference of square roots is not the square root of the difference.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the like terms \(5x\sqrt{2x}\) and \(2x\sqrt{2x}\) instead of subtracting.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of taking \(x^{2}\) instead of \(x\) out of \(\sqrt{x^{3}}\); \(\sqrt{x^{3}} = x\sqrt{x}\).

items.stem: For \(x \neq -2\), the expression \(\frac{2x^{2} + 7x + 9}{x + 2}\) is equivalent to \(2x + 3 + \frac{k}{x + 2}\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Multiply both expressions by \(x + 2\): \(2x^{2} + 7x + 9 = (2x + 3)(x + 2) + k\).

items.stem: A mobile data plan in Colombo charges a monthly amount, in rupees, of \(150 + 40(g - 5)\) for \(g\) gigabytes of data, where \(g \ge 5\). Which of the following expressions is equivalent to the monthly charge?
solution: Combine the constants: \(150 - 200 = -50\), so the charge is \(40g - 50\) rupees.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying only \(g\) by 40 and not the 5.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 150 and 40 first, which ignores the order of operations; the 150 is not multiplied by \(g - 5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: \(40 \cdot (-5) = -200\), so 200 must be subtracted from 150, not added.

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(x^{4} - 81\)?
solution: Write it as a difference of squares: \(x^{4} - 81 = (x^{2})^{2} - 9^{2} = (x^{2} + 9)(x^{2} - 9)\).
The factor \(x^{2} - 9\) is again a difference of squares: \((x + 3)(x - 3)\).
So \(x^{4} - 81 = (x^{2} + 9)(x + 3)(x - 3)\). The factor \(x^{2} + 9\) is a sum of squares and does not factor further.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of treating a difference of squares as a perfect square; \((x^{2} - 9)^{2} = x^{4} - 18x^{2} + 81\).
explanation.B: Correct. Factoring a difference of squares twice gives \((x^{2} + 9)(x + 3)(x - 3)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when factoring \(x^{2} - 9\); it is \((x + 3)(x - 3)\), not \((x - 3)^{2}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the fourth root of each term; \((x - 3)^{4}\) has many middle terms.

items.stem: A window is shaped like a rectangle with a semicircle on top. The rectangle has height \(h\) feet and width \(2r\) feet, and the semicircle has radius \(r\) feet, so its diameter is the top side of the rectangle. Which expression represents the distance, in feet, around the outside edge of the window?
solution: The outside edge consists of the bottom side \((2r)\), the two vertical sides \((h + h)\), and the curved semicircle.
The length of the semicircle is half the circumference of a circle of radius \(r\): \(\frac{1}{2}(2\pi r) = \pi r\).
The total is \(2h + 2r + \pi r\). The top side of the rectangle is inside the window, so it is not included.

explanation.A: Correct. Bottom \(2r\), two sides \(2h\), and the semicircular arc \(\pi r\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of using the full circumference \(2\pi r\) instead of half of it for the semicircle.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of also counting the top side of the rectangle, which lies inside the window under the semicircle.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(\pi r^{2}\), an area expression, for the length of the curved edge.

items.stem: The expression \((2x + 5)^{2} - (2x - 5)^{2}\) is equivalent to \(kx\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Use the difference of squares \(A^{2} - B^{2} = (A + B)(A - B)\) with \(A = 2x + 5\) and \(B = 2x - 5\).
\(A + B = 4x\) and \(A - B = 10\), so the expression is \(4x \cdot 10 = 40x\).
So \(k = 40\). (Expanding both squares gives the same result: \(4x^{2} + 20x + 25 - (4x^{2} - 20x + 25) = 40x\).)

items.stem: Priya invests \(x\) dollars in account A, which earns 6% interest per year, and the rest of 10,000 dollars in account B, which earns 4% interest per year. The total interest, in dollars, earned in one year is \(0.06x + 0.04(10{,}000 - x)\), which is equivalent to \(0.02x + 400\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of 400 in this context?

choices.A: The interest, in dollars, earned in one year from account B for every value of \(x\)
choices.B: The total amount, in dollars, invested in the two accounts
choices.C: The interest, in dollars, earned in one year if all 10,000 dollars are invested in account B
choices.D: The interest, in dollars, earned in one year if all 10,000 dollars are invested in account A

solution: The constant 400 is the value of the expression when \(x = 0\), that is, when nothing is invested in account A.
Then all 10,000 dollars are in account B, which earns \(0.04(10{,}000) = 400\) dollars. So 400 is the interest earned if all 10,000 dollars are invested in account B.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The interest from account B is \(0.04(10{,}000 - x)\), which changes with \(x\); it equals 400 only when \(x = 0\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. The total amount invested is 10,000 dollars, not 400 dollars.
explanation.C: Correct. When \(x = 0\), all 10,000 dollars are in account B, and the interest is \(0.04(10{,}000) = 400\) dollars.
explanation.D: Incorrect. If all 10,000 dollars were in account A, the interest would be \(0.06(10{,}000) = 600\) dollars; this is the value at \(x = 10{,}000\), not the constant term.

items.stem: When \((2x^{2} - 3x + 5)(4x^{2} + x - 6)\) is expanded and like terms are combined, what is the coefficient of \(x^{2}\)?
solution: An \(x^{2}\) term comes from each product of a term in the first factor and a term in the second factor whose exponents add to 2.
Those products are \(2x^{2} \cdot (-6) = -12x^{2}\), \(-3x \cdot x = -3x^{2}\), and \(5 \cdot 4x^{2} = 20x^{2}\).
Add them: \(-12 - 3 + 20 = 5\). The coefficient of \(x^{2}\) is 5.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: using \(+3x^{2}\) instead of \(-3x^{2}\) for the product \(-3x \cdot x\).
explanation.B: Correct. The three \(x^{2}\) products are \(-12x^{2}\), \(-3x^{2}\), and \(20x^{2}\), which add to \(5x^{2}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is only one of the three products that give \(x^{2}\), \(5 \cdot 4x^{2}\); the other two must be included.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the coefficient of \(x^{4}\), \(2 \cdot 4 = 8\), not of \(x^{2}\).

items.stem: For \(x \neq -2\), \(\frac{3x^{2} + kx + 10}{x + 2} = 3x + m\), where \(k\) and \(m\) are constants. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Multiply both sides by \(x + 2\): \(3x^{2} + kx + 10 = (x + 2)(3x + m) = 3x^{2} + (m + 6)x + 2m\).
Match the constant terms: \(2m = 10\), so \(m = 5\).
Match the \(x\)-terms: \(k = m + 6 = 11\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(m = 5\) from the constant terms, and then \(k = m + 6 = 11\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(3 \cdot m = 15\) instead of adding the two \(x\)-products, \(mx + 2 \cdot 3x\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the value of \(m\), not \(k\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of taking \(m = 10\) from the constant term without dividing by 2, since the constant term is \(2m\).

items.stem: The expression \(x^{2} + kx + 36\), where \(k\) is a constant, can be written as \((x + a)(x + b)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive integers. What is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?
solution: Expanding \((x + a)(x + b)\) gives \(x^{2} + (a + b)x + ab\), so \(ab = 36\) and \(k = a + b\).
The positive integer pairs with product 36 are 1 and 36, 2 and 18, 3 and 12, 4 and 9, and 6 and 6.
Their sums are 37, 20, 15, 13, and 12. The greatest possible value of \(k\) is 37.

items.stem:
For \(h 
eq 0\), \(x 
eq 0\), and \(x 
eq -h\), which of the following is equivalent to \( rac{ rac{1}{x} -  rac{1}{x + h}}{h}\)?
solution: Combine the fractions in the numerator over the common denominator \(x(x + h)\): \(\frac{(x + h) - x}{x(x + h)} = \frac{h}{x(x + h)}\).
Divide by \(h\): \(\frac{h}{x(x + h)} \cdot \frac{1}{h} = \frac{1}{x(x + h)}\).

explanation.A: Correct. The numerator simplifies to \(\frac{h}{x(x + h)}\), and dividing by \(h\) gives \(\frac{1}{x(x + h)}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting in the wrong order, \(x - (x + h) = -h\), when combining the fractions.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting the denominators, \(\frac{1}{x - (x + h)} = -\frac{1}{h}\), which is not how fractions are subtracted.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the simplified numerator only; it still has to be divided by \(h\).

items.stem: A store raises the price of an item, originally \(p\) dollars, by \(r\) percent. Later, it lowers the new price by \(r\) percent. Which expression represents the final price, in dollars?
solution: Raising by \(r\) percent multiplies the price by \(1 + \frac{r}{100}\); lowering by \(r\) percent multiplies by \(1 - \frac{r}{100}\).
The final price is \(p\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)\left(1 - \frac{r}{100}\right)\).
This is a difference of squares: \(p\left(1 - \frac{r^{2}}{100^{2}}\right) = p\left(1 - \frac{r^{2}}{10{,}000}\right)\). The final price is less than \(p\) for any \(r > 0\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of assuming that an increase and a decrease of the same percent cancel; the decrease is taken of a larger amount.
explanation.B: Correct. \(p\left(1 + \frac{r}{100}\right)\left(1 - \frac{r}{100}\right) = p\left(1 - \frac{r^{2}}{10{,}000}\right)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring \(r\) but not the 100 when squaring \(\frac{r}{100}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip in the difference of squares: \((1 + u)(1 - u) = 1 - u^{2}\), not \(1 + u^{2}\).

items.stem: Which of the following is a factor of \(x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 9x + 36\)?
solution: Factor the difference of squares: \((x - 4)(x - 3)(x + 3)\). Of the choices, only \(x + 3\) is a factor.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \(x^{2} - 9\) as \(x^{2} + 9\); the grouping leaves \(x^{2}(x - 4) - 9(x - 4)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when grouping; \(-9x + 36 = -9(x - 4)\), so the common factor is \(x - 4\), not \(x + 4\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of reading the factor \(x^{2} - 9\) as \(x - 9\); \(x = 9\) does not make the expression 0.

items.stem: The number of cells in a lab culture \(t\) hours after an experiment begins is modeled by the expression \(4^{t} \cdot 2^{t + 3}\). This expression is equivalent to \(2^{at + b}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. What is the value of \(a + b\)?
solution: Write the base 4 as a power of 2: \(4^{t} = (2^{2})^{t} = 2^{2t}\).
Multiply powers with the same base by adding exponents: \(2^{2t} \cdot 2^{t + 3} = 2^{3t + 3}\).

items.stem: The expression \((2x + k)(x - 3) - 2x^{2}\), where \(k\) is a constant, is equal to the same number for all values of \(x\). What is that number?
solution: The value does not depend on \(x\) only if the coefficient of \(x\) is 0: \(k - 6 = 0\), so \(k = 6\).
The number is \(-3k = -3(6) = -18\).

explanation.A: Correct. The \(x\)-term vanishes when \(k = 6\), and then the expression equals \(-3k = -18\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: the constant term of \((2x + k)(x - 3)\) is \(-3k\), not \(3k\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of assuming the constant value must be 0; only the coefficient of \(x\) must be 0.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the value of \(k\), not the value of the expression.

items.stem: Ravi deposits \(P\) rupees in a savings account in Pune that earns 8% interest compounded annually. The interest, in rupees, earned after 2 years is \(P(1.08)^{2} - P\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Factor out \(P\): \(P\left((1.08)^{2} - 1\right)\).
So the interest is \(P(0.08)(2.08)\), which is \(0.1664P\) rupees.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the interest earned in the second year only, not the total interest over 2 years.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding 8% twice, as for simple interest; compound interest also earns interest on the first year's interest.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \((1.08)^{2} - 1\) as \((1.08 - 1)^{2}\); the square of a difference is not the difference of squares.

items.stem: A basketball player has made 9 of her first 15 free throws. If she then makes each of her next \(n\) free throws, the fraction of all her free throws that she has made is \(\frac{9 + n}{15 + n}\). Which of the following is equivalent to this expression?
solution: Write the numerator in terms of the denominator: \(9 + n = (15 + n) - 6\).
This form shows that the fraction gets closer to 1 as \(n\) grows but always stays below 1.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the 6 by \(n\) only instead of by the whole denominator \(n + 15\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of splitting the fraction as \(\frac{9}{15} + \frac{n}{n}\); a fraction cannot be split over a sum in the denominator.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: \(9 + n\) is 6 less than \(15 + n\), not 6 more.

items.stem: The first row of a stadium section has 21 seats, and each row after the first has 2 more seats than the row in front of it. The total number of seats in the first \(n\) rows is \(21n + n(n - 1)\). This expression can be written as \((n + a)^{2} - c\), where \(a\) and \(c\) are positive constants. What is the value of \(c\)?
solution: Complete the square: \(n^{2} + 20n = (n + 10)^{2} - 100\).

items.stem: What is the least integer value of \(x\) that satisfies the inequality \(3x - 5 > 10\)?
solution: Add 5 to both sides: \(3x > 15\).
Divide by 3: \(x > 5\).
The inequality is strict, so 5 itself does not work; the least integer greater than 5 is 6.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting 5 instead of adding it: \(3x > 5\) gives \(x > \frac{5}{3}\), whose least integer is 2.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(x = 5\) gives \(3(5) - 5 = 10\), which is not greater than 10; the boundary is not included in a strict inequality.
explanation.C: Correct. The solution is \(x > 5\), and the least integer greater than 5 is 6.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the least integer greater than 15, the bound on \(3x\); the last step, dividing by 3, was skipped.

items.stem: Dev has saved \$46 and earns \$12 per hour at a part-time job. What is the least number of whole hours he must work so that his total savings are at least \$315?
solution: Let \(h\) be the number of hours: \(46 + 12h \ge 315\).
22 hours is not quite enough (\(46 + 264 = 310\)), so he needs 23 whole hours.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This rounds \(22.41...\) down; after 22 hours Dev has only \(46 + 12(22) = 310\) dollars, less than \$315.
explanation.B: Correct. \(46 + 12h \ge 315\) gives \(h \ge 22.41...\), so 23 is the least whole number of hours.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This ignores the \$46 already saved: \(12h \ge 315\) gives \(h \ge 26.25\), so 27.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds the \$46 to the goal instead of subtracting it: \(12h \ge 361\) gives 31.

items.stem: Which of the following is the solution set of the inequality \(-4(x - 2) \ge 2x - 10\)?
solution: Distribute: \(-4x + 8 \ge 2x - 10\).
Subtract \(2x\) and 8 from both sides: \(-6x \ge -18\).
Divide by \(-6\) and reverse the inequality sign: \(x \le 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This forgets to reverse the inequality sign when dividing both sides by the negative number \(-6\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of distributing incorrectly, \(-4x - 8\) instead of \(-4x + 8\), which gives \(-6x \ge -2\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This drops a negative sign at the end: \(-6x \ge -18\) gives \(x \le 3\), not \(x \le -3\).
explanation.D: Correct. \(-4x + 8 \ge 2x - 10\) gives \(-6x \ge -18\); dividing by \(-6\) reverses the sign, so \(x \le 3\).
