items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = \sqrt{2x + 1}\). What is the value of \(f(12)\)?
The graph of the exponential function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. Which of the following could define \(f\)?
solution: The graph passes through \((0, 3)\), so the initial value is \(3\).
From \((0, 3)\) to \((1, 6)\) to \((2, 12)\), each output is \(2\) times the one before, so the base is \(2\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(f(0) = 3\), \(f(1) = 6\) and \(f(2) = 12\), matching the graph.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This linear function fits \((0, 3)\) and \((1, 6)\) but gives \(f(2) = 9\), not \(12\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This switches the initial value and the base. This graph would pass through \((0, 2)\), not \((0, 3)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the point \((1, 6)\) as the initial value. The initial value is \(f(0) = 3\).

items.stem: The number of users of a new mobile payment app in Dhaka \(t\) months after its launch is modeled by \(N(t) = 2{,}000(1.1)^{t}\). According to the model, how many users will the app have 2 months after its launch?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(10\%\) of the starting value, 200, each month instead of growing by \(10\%\) of the current value.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(1.1\) by \(2\) instead of raising it to the power \(2\): \(2{,}000(2.2) = 4{,}400\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(N(1)\), the number of users after only 1 month.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 6)(x + 2)\). At which points does the graph of \(y = f(x)\) cross the \(x\)-axis in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis where \(f(x) = 0\).
The points are \((6, 0)\) and \((-2, 0)\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. \(x + 2 = 0\) gives \(x = -2\), not \(2\); the sign of one zero slipped.
explanation.C: Incorrect. These are the result of using the signs shown in the factors: \(x - 6 = 0\) gives \(x = 6\), not \(-6\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. Points where a graph crosses the \(x\)-axis have \(y\)-coordinate \(0\), so they have the form \((a, 0)\).

items.stem: A pattern of square tiles is built in stages. The number of tiles in stage \(n\) is given by \(T(n) = n^{2} + 2n\). How many tiles are in stage 9?
What is the vertex of the graph of \(y = 2(x + 4)^{2} - 3\) in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: The graph of \(y = a(x - h)^{2} + k\) has vertex \((h, k)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses the \(+4\) inside the parentheses as \(h\). Since \(x + 4 = x - (-4)\), \(h = -4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This has the sign of both coordinates wrong.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This switches the \(x\)- and \(y\)-coordinates of the vertex.
explanation.D: Correct. In \(a(x - h)^{2} + k\) form, \(h = -4\) and \(k = -3\).

items.stem: The table shows the number of people who received an invitation message in each of the first four rounds of a message chain. The number of people in each round is a constant multiple of the number in the round before. If the pattern continues, how many people will receive the message in round 5?
solution: Each round is \(3\) times the round before: \(12 = 3(4)\), \(36 = 3(12)\), \(108 = 3(36)\).

explanation.A: Correct. Each round is 3 times the round before, so round 5 has \(3(108) = 324\) people.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying by 4, the round 1 value, instead of by the common factor 3.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of treating the pattern as linear and adding the last increase, 72, again: \(108 + 72 = 180\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of adding the round 3 value to the round 4 value, \(108 + 36\), instead of multiplying by the common factor.

items.stem: Which of the following equations has a graph in the \(xy\)-plane with vertex \((3, 5)\)?
solution: The graph of \(y = (x - h)^{2} + k\) has vertex \((h, k)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This graph has vertex \((3, -5)\); the sign of the constant is reversed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This graph has vertex \((5, 3)\); the coordinates are switched.
explanation.C: Correct. \(y = (x - 3)^{2} + 5\) is in vertex form with \(h = 3\) and \(k = 5\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This graph has vertex \((-3, 5)\); the sign inside the parentheses is reversed.

items.stem: An electric scooter was bought in Bengaluru for 96,000 rupees. Its value, in rupees, \(t\) years after it was bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 96{,}000(0.9)^{t}\). According to the model, what is the value, in rupees, of the scooter 2 years after it was bought?
Each function below models an amount \(Q(t)\) of a substance \(t\) years after it was first measured. Which function models an amount that decreases by \(30\%\) each year?
solution: A decrease of \(30\%\) each year keeps \(100\% - 30\% = 70\%\) of the amount each year.
So the amount is multiplied by \(0.7\) each year: \(Q(t) = 500(0.7)^{t}\).

explanation.A: Correct. Multiplying by \(0.7\) each year keeps \(70\%\), a decrease of \(30\%\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. A base of \(0.3\) keeps only \(30\%\) each year, a decrease of \(70\%\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. A base of \(1.3\) models an increase of \(30\%\) each year.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This linear function decreases by a fixed 0.3 unit each year, not by a percent.

items.stem: The owner of a food truck models the daily profit, in dollars, from selling sandwiches at a price of \(x\) dollars each with the function \(P(x) = -2(x - 15)^{2} + 450\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number \(450\) in this context?

choices.A: The greatest possible daily profit is 450 dollars.
choices.B: The daily profit is 450 dollars when the price is 0 dollars.
choices.C: The price that gives the greatest daily profit is 450 dollars.
choices.D: The daily profit increases by 450 dollars for each 1-dollar increase in price.

solution: \(P(x)\) is in vertex form with a negative leading coefficient, so its vertex \((15, 450)\) is a maximum.
The \(y\)-value of the vertex, \(450\), is the greatest possible daily profit, in dollars.

explanation.A: Correct. The vertex \((15, 450)\) is the highest point of the graph, so the greatest daily profit is 450 dollars, at a price of 15 dollars.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(P(0) = -2(225) + 450 = 0\), so the profit at a price of 0 dollars is 0 dollars.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The price that gives the greatest profit is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, 15 dollars.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(P\) is quadratic, so the profit does not change by a constant amount per dollar.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. What is the value of \(f(0)\)?
solution: \(f(0)\) is the \(y\)-value of the graph where \(x = 0\), the \(y\)-intercept.
The graph crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 3)\), so \(f(0) = 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(1\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, not the value of \(f(0)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(-1\) is the \(x\)-value where \(f(x) = 0\), not the value of \(f(0)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The graph crosses the \(y\)-axis above the \(x\)-axis, so \(f(0)\) is positive; the sign is reversed.
explanation.D: Correct. The graph passes through \((0, 3)\), so \(f(0) = 3\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3(x - 2)^{2} + 1\). If \(f(a) = 28\) and \(a > 2\), what is the value of \(a\)?

Mateo uses a copier to make a reduced copy of a drawing that is 25 centimeters wide. Each copy is \(80\%\) as wide as the drawing it is copied from. He copies the copy, then copies that copy, and so on. Which function gives the width \(W(n)\), in centimeters, of the \(n\)th copy?
solution: Each copy is \(80\%\) as wide as the one before, so the width is multiplied by \(0.8\) for each copy.
Starting from 25 centimeters, after \(n\) copies the width is \(W(n) = 25(0.8)^{n}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This subtracts a fixed 0.8 centimeter for each copy, a linear change, not a \(20\%\) reduction.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This switches the initial value and the growth factor; it gives \(W(1) = 20\) but \(W(2) = 500\).
explanation.C: Correct. The width starts at 25 and is multiplied by \(0.8\) for each copy.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A factor of \(0.2\) would make each copy only \(20\%\) as wide as the one before.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 10x + 21\). For what value of \(x\) does \(f(x)\) reach its minimum value?
solution: Factor: \(f(x) = (x - 3)(x - 7)\), so the zeros are \(3\) and \(7\).
The vertex of a parabola is halfway between its zeros: \(x = \frac{3 + 7}{2} = 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the minimum value, \(f(5) = -4\), not the \(x\)-value where it occurs.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(21\) is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph, \(f(0)\), not where the minimum occurs.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip in \(-\frac{b}{2a}\): with \(b = -10\), \(-\frac{-10}{2} = 5\).

items.stem: A stone is launched from a slingshot. The height of the stone above the ground, in meters, is modeled by \(h(x) = -0.02x^{2} + 0.8x + 1\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance, in meters, from the slingshot. According to the model, what is the maximum height, in meters, of the stone?
solution: The maximum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{0.8}{2(-0.02)} = 20\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the horizontal distance at which the maximum height occurs, not the height.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(0.02(400) = 8\) instead of subtracting it: \(8 + 16 + 1 = 25\).
explanation.C: Correct. The vertex is at \(x = 20\), and \(h(20) = 9\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the height of the stone when it leaves the slingshot, \(h(0) = 1\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} + bx + 7\), where \(b\) is a constant. If \(f(2) = 3\), what is the value of \(b\)?
The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 1)^{2}\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x + 5)\). What is the vertex of the graph of \(y = g(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: The vertex of \(y = (x + 4)^{2}\) is \((-4, 0)\). (The graph of \(f\), with vertex \((1, 0)\), is shifted 5 units left.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. Adding \(5\) inside the function shifts the graph horizontally, not 5 units up.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses only the shift of 5 units left and ignores that the vertex of \(f\) starts at \((1, 0)\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(g(x) = (x + 4)^{2}\), whose vertex is \((-4, 0)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This shifts the graph 5 units right instead of left: \(f(x + 5)\) moves the graph left.

items.stem: A pond plant spreads across the surface of a pond. When first measured, it covered 150 square centimeters, and the area it covers triples every 2 weeks. Which function gives the area \(A(w)\), in square centimeters, covered by the plant \(w\) weeks after it was first measured?
solution: The area is multiplied by \(3\) once every 2 weeks, so after \(w\) weeks it has tripled \(\frac{w}{2}\) times.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This switches the factor and the time: it models doubling every 3 weeks.
explanation.B: Incorrect. An exponent of \(2w\) makes the area triple twice every week, not once every 2 weeks.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This divides the factor \(3\) by \(2\). Growing by a factor of \(1.5\) each week gives \(2.25\) times in 2 weeks, not \(3\) times.
explanation.D: Correct. The area triples once every 2 weeks, so the exponent is \(\frac{w}{2}\).

items.stem: The graph of a quadratic function in the \(xy\)-plane has \(x\)-intercepts \((2, 0)\) and \((-5, 0)\) and \(y\)-intercept \((0, -20)\). Which of the following could define the function?
solution: \(x\)-intercepts \(2\) and \(-5\) give factors \((x - 2)\) and \((x + 5)\), so \(f(x) = a(x - 2)(x + 5)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This has \(x\)-intercepts \(-2\) and \(5\); the signs in the factors are reversed.
explanation.B: Correct. Its zeros are \(2\) and \(-5\), and \(f(0) = 2(-2)(5) = -20\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This has the right \(x\)-intercepts, but \(f(0) = -10\). The leading coefficient \(2\) was not found.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This has the right \(x\)-intercepts, but \(f(0) = 20\), not \(-20\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = -2x^{2} + 16x - 5\). What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: The maximum occurs at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{16}{2(-2)} = 4\).

items.stem: The number of visitors per year to a tea museum near Kandy, Sri Lanka, is modeled by \(T(t) = 8{,}000(1.25)^{t}\), where \(t\) is the number of years after 2020. According to the model, how many more visitors did the museum have in 2022 than in 2021?
solution: 2021 and 2022 correspond to \(t = 1\) and \(t = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the increase from 2020 to 2022, \(T(2) - T(0)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the number of visitors in 2022, \(T(2)\), not the increase from 2021.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(25\%\) of the 2020 value, 8,000. The increase from 2021 to 2022 is \(25\%\) of the 2021 value.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. If \(k\) is a constant and the equation \(f(x) = k\) has exactly one real solution, what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The solutions of \(f(x) = k\) are the \(x\)-values where the horizontal line \(y = k\) meets the graph.
A horizontal line meets a parabola exactly once only at its vertex.
The vertex is \((-2, -1)\), so \(k = -1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(3\) is the \(y\)-intercept. The line \(y = 3\) meets the graph twice, at \(x = 0\) and \(x = -4\).
explanation.B: Correct. The line \(y = -1\) touches the parabola only at its vertex \((-2, -1)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(-2\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex. The line \(y = -2\) lies below the graph and meets it 0 times.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The line \(y = 0\) crosses the graph at two points, \((-3, 0)\) and \((-1, 0)\).

items.stem: Water sprays from a fountain nozzle. The height of the water above the nozzle, in meters, is modeled by \(h(x) = -0.5x^{2} + 3x\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance, in meters, from the nozzle. The equation \(h(x) = 0\) has solutions \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the solution \(x = 6\)?

choices.A: The water returns to the height of the nozzle 6 meters horizontally from the nozzle.
choices.B: The greatest height of the water above the nozzle is 6 meters.
choices.C: The water reaches its greatest height 6 meters horizontally from the nozzle.
choices.D: The water stays in the air for 6 seconds.

solution: \(h(x) = 0\) means the water is at the same height as the nozzle.
\(x\) is a horizontal distance, so \(x = 6\) means the water comes back down to the height of the nozzle 6 meters from the nozzle.
(The highest point is at \(x = 3\), where \(h(3) = 4.5\).)

explanation.A: Correct. \(h(6) = 0\) means the water is back at the height of the nozzle when it is 6 meters away horizontally.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(x = 6\) is a horizontal distance where \(h(x) = 0\). The greatest height is \(h(3) = 4.5\) meters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The greatest height occurs halfway between the zeros, at \(x = 3\), not at \(x = 6\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(x\) measures horizontal distance in meters, not time.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2(3)^{x}\). For what value of \(x\) is \(f(x) = 162\)?
The point \((3, 7)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane. Which point must lie on the graph of \(y = f(x - 2) + 1\)?
solution: \(y = f(x - 2) + 1\) is the graph of \(f\) shifted 2 units right and 1 unit up.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This shifts the point 2 units left instead of right. Subtracting \(2\) inside the function moves the graph right.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This shifts the point 1 unit down instead of up. Adding \(1\) outside the function moves the graph up.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reverses both shifts: the graph moves 2 units right and 1 unit up, not left and down.

items.stem: After a swimming pool is treated, the amount of chlorine in the water decreases exponentially. The graph shows the amount \(A(t)\), in grams, of chlorine in the pool \(t\) hours after treatment. Which of the following best describes how the amount of chlorine changes over time?

choices.A: The amount decreases by 4% every hour.
choices.B: The amount decreases by half every 4 hours.
choices.C: The amount decreases by half every 8 hours.
choices.D: The amount decreases by 400 grams every 4 hours.

solution: From \((0, 800)\) to \((4, 400)\) the amount is halved, and from \((4, 400)\) to \((8, 200)\) it is halved again.
So the amount decreases by half every 4 hours: \(A(t) = 800\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{4}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This reads the 4 in the time interval as a percent. The amount is halved every 4 hours.
explanation.B: Correct. The amount goes from 800 to 400 to 200 grams at 4-hour intervals, halving each time.
explanation.C: Incorrect. In 8 hours the amount goes from 800 to 200 grams, a decrease to one-fourth, not one-half.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The first 4 hours show a drop of 400 grams, but the next 4 hours show a drop of only 200 grams.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3x^{2} - 2\). If \(f(a) = 46\) and \(a < 0\), what is the value of \(a\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(16\) is the value of \(a^{2}\); the square root was not taken.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the value of \(a^{2}\), not \(a\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(f(4) = 46\), but the condition \(a < 0\) requires the negative solution.

items.stem: A school in Jaipur is building a rectangular courtyard whose length is 6 meters greater than its width. The area, in square meters, of the courtyard is given by \(A(w) = w(w + 6)\), where \(w\) is the width, in meters. If the area of the courtyard is 135 square meters, what is its width, in meters?
solution: A width is positive, so \(w = 9\).

items.stem: The table shows the number of members of a cycling club \(t\) years after the club was founded. The number of members grows exponentially. By what percent does the number of members increase each year?
solution: A growth factor of \(1.2\) means an increase of \(20\%\) each year.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This treats the growth factor \(1.2\) as the percent increase.
explanation.B: Correct. Each year the number is multiplied by \(1.2\), an increase of \(20\%\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This misreads the growth factor \(1.2\) as a \(12\%\) increase. A factor of \(1.2\) adds \(0.2\), or \(20\%\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(120\%\) is the new number as a percent of the old one, not the percent increase.

items.stem: How many times does the graph of \(y = 2x^{2} - 4x + 5\) intersect the \(x\)-axis in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: The graph meets the \(x\)-axis where \(2x^{2} - 4x + 5 = 0\).
A negative discriminant means no real solutions, so the graph does not intersect the \(x\)-axis. (Its vertex, \((1, 3)\), is above the axis and it opens up.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. Not every parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis. This one has its lowest point, \((1, 3)\), above the axis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A parabola can meet a line at most twice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A parabola meets the \(x\)-axis exactly once only when the discriminant is \(0\); here it is \(-24\).
explanation.D: Correct. The discriminant is \(-24 < 0\), so \(2x^{2} - 4x + 5 = 0\) has no real solutions.

items.stem: A square photo with sides \(x\) centimeters long is placed in a frame. The frame adds a border 3 centimeters wide on every side of the photo. Which function gives the total area \(A(x)\), in square centimeters, of the photo and the frame together?
solution: The border adds 3 centimeters on each of two opposite sides, so each side of the framed square is \(x + 3 + 3 = x + 6\) centimeters.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This squares \(x\) and \(6\) separately; \((x + 6)^{2} = x^{2} + 12x + 36\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This adds the 3-centimeter border to only one side of the square.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds the border widths to the area instead of to the side length.
explanation.D: Correct. Each side of the framed square is \(x + 6\) centimeters, so the area is \((x + 6)^{2}\).

items.stem: The graph of \(y = (x - 3)(x + 7)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is a parabola. What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of the parabola?
solution: The \(x\)-intercepts are \(3\) and \(-7\).
The vertex is halfway between them: \(x = \frac{3 + (-7)}{2} = -2\).

items.stem: The population of a town in Nepal is modeled by \(P(t) = 18{,}000(0.98)^{t}\), where \(t\) is the number of years after 2020. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the expression \(18{,}000(0.98)^{5}\) in this context?

choices.A: The estimated decrease in the population of the town from 2020 to 2025
choices.B: The estimated population of the town after it decreases by 5% from its 2020 value
choices.C: The estimated population of the town in 2015
choices.D: The estimated population of the town in 2025

solution: \(18{,}000(0.98)^{5} = P(5)\), the value of the model when \(t = 5\).
\(t = 5\) corresponds to the year 2025, so the expression is the estimated population in 2025.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The decrease would be \(18{,}000 - 18{,}000(0.98)^{5}\). The expression itself is a population.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The exponent \(5\) is a number of years, not a percent. The population decreases by \(2\%\) each year.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(t = 5\) is 5 years after 2020, not 5 years before.
explanation.D: Correct. The expression is \(P(5)\), the estimated population 5 years after 2020.

items.stem: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) is shown. Which of the following could define \(f\)?
solution: So \(f(x) = 2^{x} - 3\): the graph of \(y = 2^{x}\) shifted 3 units down, which approaches \(y = -3\) as \(x\) decreases.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(y = 2^{x}\) shifted 3 units up; it passes through \((0, 4)\), not \((0, -2)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(y = 2^{x}\) shifted 3 units right; its outputs are all positive, but the graph goes below the \(x\)-axis.
explanation.C: Correct. It passes through \((0, -2)\), \((2, 1)\) and \((3, 5)\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the \(y\)-intercept \(-2\) as the constant. It passes through \((0, -1)\), not \((0, -2)\).

items.stem: A signal flare is fired straight up. Its height above the ground, in meters, \(t\) seconds after it is fired is given by \(h(t) = -5t^{2} + 30t + 2\). For how many seconds is the flare more than 42 meters above the ground?
solution: The flare is above 42 meters between these times, for \(4 - 2 = 2\) seconds.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the sum of the two times, \(2 + 4\), instead of their difference.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the time at which the flare comes back down to 42 meters, not how long it is above 42 meters.
explanation.C: Correct. The flare is at 42 meters at \(t = 2\) and \(t = 4\), so it is higher than that for 2 seconds.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the time at which the flare reaches its maximum height, not a length of time.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 4^{x}\). What is the value of \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\)?
The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x + 4)^{2} - 9\). Which of the following is an equivalent form of \(f(x)\) that displays the \(x\)-intercepts of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) as constants?
solution: The \(x\)-intercepts are shown as constants in factored form \((x - r)(x - s)\).
\((x + 4)^{2} - 9\) is a difference of squares: \(\left((x + 4) - 3\right)\left((x + 4) + 3\right) = (x + 1)(x + 7)\).
The \(x\)-intercepts are \(-1\) and \(-7\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This has the signs reversed; its zeros are \(7\) and \(1\), not \(-7\) and \(-1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This form is equivalent to \(f(x)\), but it displays the \(y\)-intercept, not the \(x\)-intercepts.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring as \((x + 4 - 9)(x + 4 + 9)\), using \(9\) instead of its square root \(3\).

items.stem: A stack of identical tinted glass sheets reduces the intensity of light passing through it. The intensity of the light, in lux, after it passes through \(n\) sheets is modeled by \(I(n) = 1{,}000(0.8)^{n}\). What is the least number of sheets the light must pass through for its intensity to be less than 500 lux?
solution: Evaluate the model: \(I(3) = 1{,}000(0.512) = 512\), which is not less than 500.
So the least number of sheets is 4.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This assumes each sheet removes half of the light. Each sheet keeps \(80\%\), so after 2 sheets the intensity is still 640 lux.
explanation.B: Incorrect. After 3 sheets the intensity is \(512\) lux, which is not yet less than 500.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The intensity is already below 500 lux after 4 sheets, so 5 is not the least number.
explanation.D: Correct. \(I(3) = 512\) and \(I(4) = 409.6\), so 4 sheets is the least number.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = -(x - 1)^{2} + 5\). Which of the following statements about \(f\) is true?

choices.A: The maximum value of \(f(x)\) is \(1\), and it occurs at \(x = 5\).
choices.B: The minimum value of \(f(x)\) is \(5\), and it occurs at \(x = 1\).
choices.C: The maximum value of \(f(x)\) is \(5\), and it occurs at \(x = -1\).
choices.D: The maximum value of \(f(x)\) is \(5\), and it occurs at \(x = 1\).

solution: \(f\) is in vertex form with \(a = -1 < 0\), so the graph opens down and the vertex is the highest point.
The vertex is \((1, 5)\), so the maximum value of \(f(x)\) is 5, at \(x = 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This switches the coordinates of the vertex \((1, 5)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. The coefficient \(-1\) makes the graph open down, so the vertex is a maximum, not a minimum.
explanation.D: Correct. The vertex is \((1, 5)\), and the graph opens down, so 5 is the maximum value.

items.stem: The value, in dollars, of a collectible stamp \(t\) years after it was bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 1{,}500(1.08)^{t}\). According to the model, the value of the stamp increases by \(p\%\) each year. What is the value of \(p\)?
solution: The base \(1.08 = 1 + 0.08\) is the yearly growth factor.
An increase of \(0.08\) of the value is an increase of \(8\%\), so \(p = 8\).

items.stem: A softball is thrown upward. The table shows the height \(h(t)\), in meters, of the softball at three times \(t\), in seconds, after it is thrown. The height is a quadratic function of time. At what time, in seconds, does the softball reach its maximum height?
solution: The graph of a quadratic function is symmetric about the vertical line through its vertex.
The softball is at the same height, 13 meters, at \(t = 1\) and \(t = 3\).
So the vertex is halfway between them, at \(t = \frac{1 + 3}{2} = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is halfway between \(t = 0\) and \(t = 3\), but those times have different heights, 1 and 13 meters.
explanation.B: Correct. The heights at \(t = 1\) and \(t = 3\) are equal, so the vertex is midway between them, at \(t = 2\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. At \(t = 1\) the softball is at 13 meters, and it is still at 13 meters at \(t = 3\), so it rose higher in between.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The softball is falling at \(t = 3\); it is at the same height as at \(t = 1\).

items.stem: Which of the following is equivalent to \(4(9)^{\frac{x}{2}}\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This also takes the square root of the coefficient \(4\). Only the base \(9\) is raised to the power \(\frac{x}{2}\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This divides the base \(9\) by \(2\) instead of taking its square root.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This squares the base instead of taking its square root: \(\frac{x}{2}\) means a square root, not a square.

items.stem: A furniture workshop models the average cost per chair, in dollars, of making \(x\) chairs in a month with the function \(C(x) = 0.02(x - 120)^{2} + 45\). Which of the following statements is true according to the model?

choices.A: The greatest average cost per chair is 45 dollars, when 120 chairs are made in a month.
choices.B: The least average cost per chair is 120 dollars, when 45 chairs are made in a month.
choices.C: The average cost per chair is 45 dollars when no chairs are made.
choices.D: The least average cost per chair is 45 dollars, when 120 chairs are made in a month.

solution: \(C\) is in vertex form with a positive leading coefficient, so its vertex \((120, 45)\) is a minimum.
The least average cost per chair is 45 dollars, when 120 chairs are made in a month.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The coefficient \(0.02\) is positive, so the graph opens up and the vertex is a minimum.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This switches the coordinates of the vertex: 120 is the number of chairs and 45 is the cost.
explanation.D: Correct. The vertex \((120, 45)\) is the lowest point of the graph, since \(0.02 > 0\).

items.stem: A ball is dropped from a height of 512 centimeters. After each bounce, it rises to \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the height from which it last fell. What is the height, in centimeters, that the ball reaches after its third bounce?
solution: The height after \(n\) bounces is \(H(n) = 512\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{n}\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 4x + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane has an \(x\)-intercept at \((1, 0)\). What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the other \(x\)-intercept?
solution: \(x^{2} - 4x + 3 = (x - 1)(x - 3)\), so the other \(x\)-intercept is at \(x = 3\).
(Or: the zeros are symmetric about the axis \(x = 2\), so the other zero is \(2 + 1 = 3\).)

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(4\) is the sum of the two zeros, \(1 + 3\), not the other zero.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: \(x - 3 = 0\) gives \(x = 3\), not \(-3\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(4\) to the known zero instead of using the axis of symmetry \(x = 2\).

items.stem: A cart is released from rest at the top of a ramp. The distance, in meters, that the cart has rolled \(t\) seconds after it is released is modeled by \(d(t) = 0.8t^{2}\). According to the model, how many meters does the cart roll between \(t = 2\) and \(t = 3\)?
solution: The distance rolled between those times is \(7.2 - 3.2 = 4\) meters.

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(0.8\) is the coefficient in the model, not a distance rolled over a time interval.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(d(2)\), the distance rolled in the first 2 seconds.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(d(3)\), the total distance rolled in 3 seconds, not the distance between \(t = 2\) and \(t = 3\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2x^{2} + 3x - 5\). Which of the following is equivalent to \(f(x + 1)\)?
solution: Combine like terms: \(2x^{2} + 7x\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of expanding \(2(x + 1)^{2}\) as \(2x^{2} + 2x + 2\), leaving out the doubled middle term.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(f(x) + 1\). It adds 1 to the output instead of replacing \(x\) with \(x + 1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of expanding \((x + 1)^{2}\) as \(x^{2} + 1\): \(2x^{2} + 2 + 3x + 3 - 5 = 2x^{2} + 3x\).

items.stem: Water is drained from a tank through a valve at its base. The depth of the water in the tank, in centimeters, \(t\) minutes after the valve is opened is modeled by \(d(t) = 0.25(t - 20)^{2}\) for \(0 \le t \le 20\). According to the model, how many minutes after the valve is opened is the depth of the water 25 centimeters?
solution: Only \(t = 10\) is in the interval \(0 \le t \le 20\), so the answer is 10.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane has its vertex on the line \(x = 3\). The point \((-1, 4)\) lies on the graph. Which of the following points must also lie on the graph?
solution: The graph of a quadratic function is symmetric about the vertical line through its vertex, here \(x = 3\).
The point \((-1, 4)\) is \(3 - (-1) = 4\) units to the left of that line.
Its mirror image is 4 units to the right of \(x = 3\), at \((7, 4)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the distance from \(-1\) to \(3\) as \(3 - 1 = 2\) instead of \(3 - (-1) = 4\).
explanation.B: Correct. The point \((-1, 4)\) is 4 units left of the axis of symmetry \(x = 3\), so its mirror image is 4 units right of it, at \((7, 4)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reflects \((-1, 4)\) across the \(y\)-axis. The graph is symmetric about the line \(x = 3\), not \(x = 0\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This reflects \((-1, 4)\) across the \(x\)-axis. A parabola is symmetric about its vertical axis \(x = 3\).

items.stem: A farmer near Multan estimates that if \(x\) mango trees are planted on each acre of an orchard, each tree will produce \(600 - 5x\) mangoes per season. The total number of mangoes produced per acre in a season is given by \(T(x) = x(600 - 5x)\). According to the model, how many trees should be planted per acre to produce the greatest total number of mangoes?
solution: The graph of \(T\) is a parabola that opens downward, so its maximum is halfway between the zeros.
\(x = \frac{0 + 120}{2} = 60\) trees per acre.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the number of mangoes each tree produces when 60 trees are planted per acre, not the number of trees.
explanation.B: Correct. \(T\) has zeros at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 120\), so its maximum occurs halfway between them, at \(x = 60\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the greatest total number of mangoes per acre, \(T(60)\), not the number of trees that produces it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of trees per acre at which each tree would produce 0 mangoes, so the total would be 0.

items.stem: The graph of the function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. Which of the following could define \(f\)?
solution: Check each choice at the three labeled points \((0, 1)\), \((1, 4)\), and \((2, 10)\).
Each other choice misses at least one of the points, so \(f(x) = 3(2)^{x} - 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This function gives \(f(0) = 3 + 2 = 5\), not 1.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This linear function passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((1, 4)\), but \(3(2) + 1 = 7\), not 10. The graph is curved, not a line.
explanation.C: Correct. \(3(1) - 2 = 1\), \(3(2) - 2 = 4\), and \(3(4) - 2 = 10\), so all three points lie on this graph.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This function passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((1, 4)\), but \(4^{2} = 16\), not 10.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(x - 3)^{2} + 2\), where \(a\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 20)\). What is the value of \(f(5)\)?

A ball machine launches a tennis ball upward. The height of the ball above the ground, in meters, \(t\) seconds after it is launched is modeled by \(h(t) = -4.9t^{2} + 9.8t + 3\). Which of the following equivalent forms of \(h(t)\) displays the maximum height of the ball, in meters, as a constant or coefficient?
solution: The maximum value of a quadratic appears as the constant \(k\) in vertex form \(a(t - h)^{2} + k\).
So \(h(t) = -4.9(t - 1)^{2} + 7.9\), which displays the maximum height, 7.9 meters.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This form is equivalent, but the constant 3 is the height of the ball when it is launched, not its maximum height.
explanation.B: Correct. This is vertex form. The vertex is \((1, 7.9)\), so the ball reaches a maximum height of 7.9 meters, shown as the constant 7.9.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This form is equivalent, but none of its constants is the maximum height of the ball.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This form is equivalent, but it is not vertex form because of the \(-9.8t\) term, so 22.6 is not the maximum height.

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 3x\) and \(g(x) = 2x - 1\). What is the value of \(g(f(2))\)?
solution: Work from the inside out. First, \(f(2) = 2^{2} - 3(2) = -2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(f(2)\). It still has to be used as the input of \(g\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(g(2)\), not \(g(f(2))\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(f(g(2)) = f(3) = 0\). The functions were applied in the wrong order.

items.stem: After an advertising campaign ended, the number of daily visitors to a website decreased exponentially. The table shows the number of daily visitors \(d\) days after the campaign ended for two values of \(d\). According to an exponential model that fits these values, how many daily visitors did the website have 4 days after the campaign ended?
solution: From \(d = 3\) to \(d = 4\) the number is multiplied by \(b\) once more.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the model's number of daily visitors when the campaign ended (\(d = 0\)), not 4 days later.
explanation.B: Correct. Over 2 days the number is multiplied by \(\frac{5{,}400}{9{,}600} = \frac{9}{16}\), so each day it is multiplied by \(\frac{3}{4}\). Day 4: \(5{,}400 \cdot \frac{3}{4} = 4{,}050\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the model's number of daily visitors 2 days after the campaign ended, not 4 days.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This assumes a linear decrease of 2,100 visitors per day. In an exponential model the number is multiplied by the same factor each day.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2^{x} + 2^{x + 3}\). For all values of \(x\), \(f(x) = k(2)^{x}\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?

A tailoring shop in Faisalabad models its weekly profit, in rupees, from making \(x\) school uniforms with the function \(P(x) = -20(x - 10)(x - 90)\). According to the model, what is the greatest weekly profit, in rupees, the shop can make?
solution: The zeros of \(P\) are \(x = 10\) and \(x = 90\), and the parabola opens downward.
The maximum is at the midpoint \(x = \frac{10 + 90}{2} = 50\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the size of the loss when no uniforms are made: \(P(0) = -18{,}000\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the number of uniforms that gives the greatest profit, not the greatest profit.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \((50 - 10)(90 - 50)\), which leaves out the factor 20 in the model.
explanation.D: Correct. The maximum occurs halfway between the zeros 10 and 90, at \(x = 50\): \(P(50) = -20(40)(-40) = 32{,}000\).

items.stem: The point \((-2, 5)\) lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = 3f(x + 4) - 1\). Which of the following points must lie on the graph of \(y = g(x)\)?
solution: To use \(f(-2) = 5\), the input of \(f\) must be \(-2\): \(x + 4 = -2\), so \(x = -6\).
So \((-6, 14)\) lies on the graph of \(y = g(x)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This shifts the point 4 units right. Adding 4 inside the function moves the graph 4 units left.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This applies the vertical changes but leaves out the horizontal shift: \(g(-2) = 3f(2) - 1\), and \(f(2)\) is not known.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This subtracts 1 before multiplying by 3: \(3(5 - 1) = 12\). The function multiplies \(f\) by 3 first, then subtracts 1.

items.stem: The number of active players, in thousands, of an online game \(t\) months after its release is modeled by an exponential function \(P\). The graph of \(y = P(t)\) is shown. According to the model, how many thousand active players will the game have 15 months after its release?
solution: From \((0, 60)\) to \((5, 30)\), the number of players is halved, so \(P(t) = 60\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{5}}\).
15 months is three 5-month periods.
\(P(15) = 60\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3} = 7.5\) thousand players.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This divides 60 by 3, the number of 5-month periods. Each period halves the amount, so 60 is divided by \(2^{3} = 8\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This assumes a linear decrease of 30 thousand every 5 months. An exponential model halves the amount every 5 months instead.
explanation.C: Correct. The number of players halves every 5 months: 60, 30, 15, then 7.5 thousand at 15 months.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of thousand players 10 months after release, after only two halvings.

items.stem: The main cable of a small suspension footbridge hangs between two towers. The height of the cable above the deck of the bridge, in meters, is modeled by \(h(x) = 0.01x^{2} - 0.8x + 20\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance, in meters, from one of the towers. According to the model, what is the least height, in meters, of the cable above the deck?
solution: The parabola opens upward, so its vertex gives the least height.
The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{-0.8}{2(0.01)} = 40\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane does not intersect the \(x\)-axis. Which of the following could be the value of \(k\)?
solution: Complete the square: \(f(x) = (x - 3)^{2} + (k - 9)\).
The graph opens upward with minimum value \(k - 9\). It misses the \(x\)-axis exactly when \(k - 9 > 0\), that is, \(k > 9\).
Of the choices, only \(10\) is greater than 9.

explanation.A: Incorrect. With \(k = 0\), \(f(x) = x(x - 6)\), which has \(x\)-intercepts at 0 and 6.
explanation.B: Incorrect. With \(k = 9\), \(f(x) = (x - 3)^{2}\), whose graph touches the \(x\)-axis at \((3, 0)\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(f(x) = (x - 3)^{2} + k - 9\), so the minimum value is \(k - 9 = 1 > 0\). The graph stays above the \(x\)-axis.
explanation.D: Incorrect. With \(k = -10\), the minimum value is \(-19\), so the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis twice. The condition is \(k > 9\), not \(k < -9\).

items.stem: A magazine had 25,000 print subscribers in 2023. Each year after 2023, the number of print subscribers is predicted to be \(6\%\) less than the number the year before. Which of the following statements is true according to this prediction?

choices.A: The number of print subscribers in 2025 is predicted to be 22,000.
choices.B: The decrease from 2024 to 2025 is less than the decrease from 2023 to 2024.
choices.C: The decrease from 2024 to 2025 is equal to the decrease from 2023 to 2024.
choices.D: The decrease from 2024 to 2025 is greater than the decrease from 2023 to 2024.

solution: Since \(1{,}410 < 1{,}500\), the decrease from 2024 to 2025 is less than the decrease from 2023 to 2024.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting 12% of 25,000. The second 6% decrease is taken from 23,500, giving 22,090.
explanation.B: Correct. The decrease from 2023 to 2024 is 6% of 25,000, or 1,500. The decrease from 2024 to 2025 is 6% of 23,500, or 1,410, which is less.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This treats the change as linear. Each year's decrease is 6% of a smaller number, so the decreases get smaller.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The second decrease is 6% of a smaller number of subscribers, so it is smaller, not greater.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 2x - 8\). For which values of \(x\) is \(f(x) < 0\)?
solution: Factor: \(f(x) = (x + 2)(x - 4)\), so the zeros are \(x = -2\) and \(x = 4\).
The graph is a parabola that opens upward, so \(f(x) < 0\) between the zeros.

explanation.A: Correct. \(f(x) = (x + 2)(x - 4)\), and the upward-opening graph is below the \(x\)-axis between its zeros \(-2\) and \(4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. These are the values for which \(f(x) > 0\). The graph opens upward, so it is below the \(x\)-axis between the zeros.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of factoring \(f(x)\) as \((x - 2)(x + 4)\). The zeros are \(-2\) and \(4\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. These are the values for which \(f\) is decreasing, to the left of the vertex. For example, \(f(-3) = 7 > 0\).

items.stem: The number of households using biogas units in a district of Sindh, Pakistan, is modeled by \(N(t) = 350(2)^{\frac{t}{6}}\), where \(t\) is the number of years after 2020. According to the model, in what year will 2,800 households be using biogas units?
solution: 18 years after 2020 is 2038.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 64\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x}\). For what value of \(x\) is \(f(x) = \frac{1}{2}\)?
solution: Write both sides as powers of 2: \(64\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x} = 2^{6} \cdot 2^{-x} = 2^{6 - x}\) and \(\frac{1}{2} = 2^{-1}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(64 \cdot \frac{1}{2}\), which treats the exponent as a factor. The value of \(f(x)\) is halved once for each increase of 1 in \(x\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(f(-7) = 64(2)^{7}\), which is very large. Each increase of 1 in \(x\) halves the value, so \(x\) must be positive.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(f(6) = 64\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{6} = 1\), not \(\frac{1}{2}\). One more halving is needed.

items.stem: A golf ball is hit from a tee box that is 1 meter above the fairway. The graph shows the height \(h(t)\), in meters, of the ball above the fairway \(t\) seconds after it is hit, where \(h\) is a quadratic function. What is the maximum height, in meters, of the ball above the fairway?
solution: The ball is at height 1 at \(t = 0\) and \(t = 4\), so the vertex is at \(t = 2\), and \(h(t) = at(t - 4) + 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the height at \(t = 1\), the highest labeled point. The ball keeps rising until \(t = 2\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the time, in seconds, at which the ball reaches its maximum height, not the maximum height.
explanation.C: Correct. By symmetry the vertex is at \(t = 2\). With \(h(t) = at(t - 4) + 1\) and \(h(1) = 16\), \(a = -5\), so \(h(2) = -5(2)(-2) + 1 = 21\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the maximum height of the ball above the tee box. The tee box is 1 meter above the fairway.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3(2)^{x - 4}\). Which of the following is equivalent to \(f(x)\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This multiplies 3 by 2 before applying the exponent. The exponent applies only to the base 2.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This multiplies by \(2^{4} = 16\) instead of dividing by it. \(2^{x - 4} = 2^{x} \cdot 2^{-4}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This treats \(2^{x - 4}\) as \(2^{x} - 2^{4}\). Subtracting in the exponent means dividing powers, not subtracting them.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 12x + 20\). In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = f(x)\) and the line \(y = 20\) intersect at two points. What is the distance between these two points?
solution: The points are \((0, 20)\) and \((12, 20)\).
They lie on the same horizontal line, so the distance between them is \(12 - 0 = 12\).

items.stem: Two savings plans each start with a balance of 8,000 dollars. Under plan P, the balance increases by 400 dollars each year. Under plan Q, the balance increases by \(5\%\) each year. After how many years will the balance under plan Q first be greater than the balance under plan P?
solution: After 1 year: P has 8,400 dollars and Q has 8,400 dollars, which are equal.
After 2 years: P has 8,800 dollars and Q has 8,820 dollars, so Q is first greater after 2 years.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses the percent, 5, as the number of years. Compare the balances year by year.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{8{,}000}{400}\), the number of years for plan P to add 8,000 dollars, not when Q passes P.
explanation.C: Incorrect. After 1 year both balances are equal, 8,400 dollars, so Q is not yet greater than P.
explanation.D: Correct. After 1 year both balances are 8,400 dollars. After 2 years, P has 8,800 dollars and Q has \(8{,}000(1.05)^{2} = 8{,}820\) dollars.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. What is the value of \(f(5)\)?
solution: The zeros are \(-1\) and \(3\), so \(f(x) = a(x + 1)(x - 3)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses \(-(x - 1)(x + 3)\), whose zeros are \(1\) and \(-3\). The zeros shown are \(-1\) and \(3\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats the \(y\)-intercept 3 as the maximum value: \(-(5 - 1)^{2} + 3\). The maximum occurs at \(x = 1\), where \(f(1) = 4\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses \(f(x) = (x + 1)(x - 3)\), which opens upward. The graph opens downward and \(f(0) = 3\), so \(a = -1\).

items.stem: Dilani deposits 200,000 rupees in a savings account in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The account earns \(0.5\%\) interest each month, and she makes no other deposits or withdrawals. Which of the following functions gives the balance \(B(t)\), in rupees, of the account after \(t\) years?
solution: Each month the balance grows by \(0.5\%\), so it is multiplied by \(1 + 0.005 = 1.005\).
In \(t\) years there are \(12t\) months.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This gives the balance after \(t\) months, not \(t\) years.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This writes \(0.5\%\) as 0.05 instead of 0.005.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This divides by 12 instead of multiplying. There are \(12t\) months in \(t\) years, not \(\frac{t}{12}\).
explanation.D: Correct. Each month the balance is multiplied by 1.005, and \(t\) years contain \(12t\) months.

items.stem: A print shop's daily profit, in dollars, from printing \(x\) hundred flyers is modeled by \(P(x) = -x^{2} + 16x - 39\). The shop breaks even, with a daily profit of 0 dollars, for two values of \(x\). What is the greater of these two values?
solution: The greater value is 13.

items.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the vertex of the graph of which of the following equations lies in quadrant IV?
solution: For \(y = ax^{2} + bx + c\), the vertex has \(x\)-coordinate \(-\frac{b}{2a}\).
Quadrant IV needs a positive \(x\)-coordinate and a negative \(y\)-coordinate.
For \(y = x^{2} - 4x + 1\): \(x = 2\) and \(y = -3\), so the vertex \((2, -3)\) is in quadrant IV.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The vertex of this graph is \((-2, 3)\), which is in quadrant II.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The vertex of this graph is \((2, 3)\), which is in quadrant I.
explanation.C: Correct. The vertex is at \(x = 2\), and \(y = 4 - 8 + 1 = -3\). The point \((2, -3)\) is in quadrant IV.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The vertex of this graph is \((-2, -3)\), which is in quadrant III.

items.stem: The table shows the number of electric cars registered in a city \(t\) years after 2010 for three values of \(t\). The number of electric cars increased by the same percent every 5 years. Which of the following functions best models the number of electric cars \(E(t)\) registered in the city \(t\) years after 2010?
solution: So the number is multiplied by 1.5 every 5 years, starting from 1,600.
In \(t\) years there are \(\frac{t}{5}\) five-year periods: \(E(t) = 1{,}600(1.5)^{\frac{t}{5}}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This applies the 5-year growth factor every year. It gives \(E(5) \approx 12{,}150\), not 2,400.
explanation.B: Correct. The number is multiplied by \(\frac{2{,}400}{1{,}600} = 1.5\) every 5 years, which is \(\frac{t}{5}\) times in \(t\) years.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This multiplies by 1.5 five times each year. The factor 1.5 applies once every 5 years, so the exponent is \(\frac{t}{5}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This splits the \(50\%\) increase into five equal yearly increases of \(10\%\). Then \(E(5) = 1{,}600(1.1)^{5} \approx 2{,}577\), not 2,400.

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = x^{2}\) and \(g(x) = x - 3\). For what value of \(x\) is \(f(g(x)) = g(f(x))\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of solving \(-6x + 9 = 3\) instead of \(-6x + 9 = -3\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of expanding \((x - 3)^{2}\) as \(x^{2} + 6x + 9\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes \(g(x) = 0\), so \(f(g(3)) = 0\), but \(g(f(3)) = 9 - 3 = 6\).

items.stem: During a cricket match in Rawalpindi, a batter hits the ball into the air. The height of the ball above the ground, in meters, is modeled by \(h(x) = -0.0125x^{2} + 0.9x + 1\), where \(x\) is the horizontal distance, in meters, from where the ball was hit. According to the model, at what horizontal distance, in meters, other than \(x = 0\), is the ball 1 meter above the ground?
solution: The distance other than 0 is 72 meters.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 6)^{2} + 1\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(2x)\). What is the vertex of the graph of \(y = g(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: Factor out 2 inside the square: \((2(x - 3))^{2} + 1 = 4(x - 3)^{2} + 1\).
So the vertex is \((3, 1)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the vertex of the graph of \(f\). Replacing \(x\) with \(2x\) compresses the graph horizontally, so the vertex moves.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This treats \(f(2x)\) as \(2f(x)\), doubling the \(y\)-coordinate. The change is inside the function, so it affects \(x\)-coordinates.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This multiplies the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(f\) by 2. Replacing \(x\) with \(2x\) divides \(x\)-coordinates by 2.

items.stem: The value of a rare coin increases by \(4\%\) every 6 months. By what percent does the value of the coin increase every year?
solution: Every 6 months the value is multiplied by 1.04.
A year has two 6-month periods, so the value is multiplied by \(1.04^{2} = 1.0816\).
That is an increase of \(8.16\%\) per year.

explanation.A: Correct. In a year the value is multiplied by \(1.04^{2} = 1.0816\), an increase of \(8.16\%\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the increase every 6 months, not every year.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds the two \(4\%\) increases. The second increase is \(4\%\) of a larger value, so the yearly increase is more than \(8\%\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring 4 instead of squaring the growth factor 1.04.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: The zeros are \(-1\) and \(5\), so \(f(x) = a(x + 1)(x - 5)\), and the vertex is at \(x = \frac{-1 + 5}{2} = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the \(y\)-intercept. The graph keeps rising to the right of \(x = 0\) until \(x = 2\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(-(3)(-3)\), which leaves out the leading coefficient \(-0.5\) found from the \(y\)-intercept.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, where the maximum occurs, not the maximum value.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3x^{2} - 12x + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane intersects the \(x\)-axis at exactly one point. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The graph touches the \(x\)-axis at exactly one point when the vertex lies on the \(x\)-axis.

items.stem: The table shows the population of a town in 2010 and in 2020. A model predicts that the population will increase by the same percent every 10 years. According to the model, what will the population of the town be in 2040?
solution: From 2010 to 2020 the population is multiplied by \(\frac{8{,}000}{6{,}400} = 1.25\).
From 2020 to 2040 there are two 10-year periods.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the predicted population in 2030. Two 10-year periods pass between 2020 and 2040.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This adds 1,600 people every 10 years, a linear model. The population increases by the same percent, not the same number.
explanation.C: Correct. The population is multiplied by \(\frac{8{,}000}{6{,}400} = 1.25\) every 10 years: \(8{,}000(1.25)^{2} = 12{,}500\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This applies the factor 1.25 three times after 2020, which gives the predicted population in 2050.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = -2(x - 3)^{2} - 5\). Which of the following describes all possible values of \(f(x)\)?
solution: The vertex of the graph is \((3, -5)\).
The leading coefficient \(-2\) is negative, so the parabola opens downward and \(-5\) is the maximum value.
So every value of \(f(x)\) satisfies \(f(x) \le -5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This treats \(-5\) as a minimum. The leading coefficient \(-2\) is negative, so the parabola opens downward and \(-5\) is the maximum.
explanation.B: Correct. \(-2(x - 3)^{2} \le 0\) for every \(x\), so \(f(x) \le -5\), and \(f(3) = -5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, 3, instead of its \(y\)-coordinate, \(-5\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This drops the negative sign of the constant. The vertex is \((3, -5)\).

items.stem: In Dhaka, Rafiq deposits 40,000 taka in an account that earns \(7\%\) interest compounded annually, and Nasreen deposits 50,000 taka in an account that earns \(3\%\) interest compounded annually. Neither makes any other deposits or withdrawals. At the end of which year will Rafiq's balance first be greater than Nasreen's balance?
solution: So Rafiq's balance is first greater at the end of year 6. A graphing calculator shows the same crossing.

explanation.A: Correct. At the end of year 6, Rafiq has about 60,029 taka and Nasreen has about 59,703 taka. At the end of year 5, Rafiq still has less.
explanation.B: Incorrect. At the end of year 5, Rafiq has about 56,102 taka and Nasreen has about 57,964 taka, so Rafiq's balance is still less.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses simple interest, 2,800 and 1,500 taka per year. With compound interest, Rafiq passes Nasreen sooner.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This divides the \(25\%\) gap by the 4-percentage-point difference in rates and rounds up. Compound growth does not work this way.

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = 2^{x}\) and \(g(x) = x^{2} - 1\). If \(f(g(x)) = 8\), what is one possible value of \(x\)?
solution: So \(x = -2\) or \(x = 2\); either value is correct.

items.stem: The number of people inside a festival venue \(t\) hours after the gates open is modeled by \(N(t) = -150t^{2} + 1{,}800t\). According to the model, how many hours after the gates open does the number of people inside the venue first reach 4,800?
solution: The first time is \(t = 4\) hours.

explanation.A: Incorrect. At \(t = 8\) there are again 4,800 people, but the number is decreasing then. It first reaches 4,800 at \(t = 4\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the time when the number of people is greatest, 5,400 people, not when it first reaches 4,800.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is when the model gives 0 people inside the venue again.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = ax^{2} + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants with \(a < 0\) and \(c > 0\). How many \(x\)-intercepts does the graph of \(y = f(x)\) have in the \(xy\)-plane?

choices.C: It depends on the value of \(b\)

solution: \(f(0) = c > 0\), so the graph passes through a point above the \(x\)-axis.
Since \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward, so it crosses the \(x\)-axis on both sides of its vertex.
Algebraically, \(b^{2} - 4ac > 0\) because \(b^{2} \ge 0\) and \(-4ac > 0\). So there are exactly two \(x\)-intercepts.

explanation.A: Correct. The graph opens downward and passes through \((0, c)\), which is above the \(x\)-axis, so it must cross the \(x\)-axis once on each side of the \(y\)-axis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A downward-opening parabola with a point above the \(x\)-axis cannot stay above it; it eventually falls below the \(x\)-axis.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The discriminant \(b^{2} - 4ac\) is positive for every \(b\), because \(-4ac > 0\) when \(a < 0\) and \(c > 0\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. Exactly one intercept requires the vertex on the \(x\)-axis, so the maximum would be 0. But \(f(0) = c > 0\), so the maximum is positive.

items.stem: A population of an invasive species of fish in a lake triples every 5 years. Which of the following is the factor by which the population is multiplied each year?
solution: Let \(r\) be the yearly growth factor. Over 5 years the population is multiplied by \(r^{5}\).

explanation.A: Correct. If the yearly factor is \(r\), then \(r^{5} = 3\), so \(r = 3^{\frac{1}{5}} \approx 1.246\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This divides the 5-year factor by 5. A factor less than 1 would make the population decrease.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the factor for 25 years, not for 1 year. The exponent should be \(\frac{1}{5}\), not 5.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This splits the \(200\%\) increase evenly into five yearly increases of \(40\%\). But \(1.4^{5} \approx 5.4\), not 3.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - p)(x - q)\), where \(p\) and \(q\) are constants. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 12)\), and its vertex has \(x\)-coordinate 4. What is the minimum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: \(f(0) = pq = 12\), and the vertex is midway between the zeros: \(\frac{p + q}{2} = 4\), so \(p + q = 8\).
The minimum value is \(f(4) = (2)(-2) = -4\).

items.stem: The graph of \(y = 2^{x}\) in the \(xy\)-plane is translated 3 units to the right. The resulting graph is also the graph of \(y = k(2)^{x}\), where \(k\) is a constant. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Translating 3 units to the right replaces \(x\) with \(x - 3\): \(y = 2^{x - 3}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This treats the translation as multiplying by \(-3\). Translating right by 3 replaces \(x\) with \(x - 3\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(2^{3}\), which corresponds to a translation 3 units to the left, \(y = 2^{x + 3}\).
explanation.C: Correct. The translated graph is \(y = 2^{x - 3} = 2^{-3} \cdot 2^{x} = \frac{1}{8}(2)^{x}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This treats \(2^{-3}\) as \(-8\). A negative exponent gives a reciprocal: \(2^{-3} = \frac{1}{8}\).

items.stem: The amount, in milligrams, of a radioactive tracer remaining in a laboratory sample \(t\) hours after the sample is prepared is modeled by \(A(t) = 200\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{k}}\), where \(k\) is a constant. According to the model, 25 milligrams of the tracer remain 18 hours after the sample is prepared. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: So \(k = 6\): the amount is halved every 6 hours.

explanation.A: Correct. \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{18}{k}} = \frac{25}{200} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3}\), so \(\frac{18}{k} = 3\) and \(k = 6\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{18}{8}\), which uses the factor 8 by which the amount decreased instead of the number of halvings, 3.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This assumes the amount is halved only twice in 18 hours, but \(200 \to 100 \to 50 \to 25\) is three halvings.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of times the amount is halved in 18 hours, \(\frac{18}{k}\), not \(k\).

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x) + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. For what value of \(k\) does the graph of \(y = g(x)\) have exactly one \(x\)-intercept?
solution: The vertex is at \(x = 1\), and \(f(1) = 2(2)(-2) = -8\).
\(g\) has exactly one \(x\)-intercept when its vertex is on the \(x\)-axis: \(-8 + k = 0\), so \(k = 8\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This shifts the graph down 8 units, so the vertex moves to \((1, -16)\) and the graph still crosses the \(x\)-axis twice.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats the \(y\)-intercept \((0, -6)\) as the vertex. The vertex is at \(x = 1\), where \(f(1) = -8\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This uses \(f(x) = (x + 1)(x - 3)\), leaving out the factor 2 that makes \(f(0) = -6\).
explanation.D: Correct. \(f(x) = 2(x + 1)(x - 3)\) has minimum \(f(1) = -8\). Shifting the graph up 8 units puts the vertex on the \(x\)-axis.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} + kx + 16\), where \(k\) is a positive constant. The minimum value of \(f(x)\) is 0. What is the value of \(f(-1)\)?
solution: The minimum value is at \(x = -\frac{k}{2}\): \(f\left(-\frac{k}{2}\right) = 16 - \frac{k^{2}}{4}\).

items.stem: The number of members of a hiking club \(t\) years after the club was founded is modeled by \(M(t) = 1{,}000(1.5)^{\frac{t}{3}}\). Which of the following functions is approximately equivalent to \(M\) and shows the approximate percent increase in the number of members each year?
solution: Rewrite the exponent: \(1.5^{\frac{t}{3}} = \left(1.5^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{t}\).
This shows an increase of about \(14.5\%\) each year.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This applies the 3-year growth factor every year, so it is not equivalent to \(M\).
explanation.B: Correct. \(1.5^{\frac{t}{3}} = \left(1.5^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^{t} \approx 1.145^{t}\), an increase of about \(14.5\%\) per year.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This splits the \(50\%\) increase into three equal yearly increases of about \(16.7\%\). Compounding makes the yearly increase smaller.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses \(1.5^{3}\) instead of \(1.5^{\frac{1}{3}}\) as the yearly factor.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(x - 3)^{2} + k\), where \(a\) and \(k\) are nonzero constants. If \(f(1) > f(4)\), which of the following must be true?
solution: So \(a > 0\). The condition gives no information about \(k\). (The point \(x = 1\) is farther from the vertex than \(x = 4\), so it is higher only if the parabola opens upward.)

explanation.B: Incorrect. The constant \(k\) cancels when \(f(4)\) is subtracted from \(f(1)\), so the condition says nothing about the sign of \(k\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The constant \(k\) cancels when \(f(4)\) is subtracted from \(f(1)\), so \(k\) could be positive or negative.
explanation.D: Incorrect. If \(a < 0\), then \(f(1) = 4a + k\) is less than \(f(4) = a + k\), which contradicts \(f(1) > f(4)\).

items.stem: A juice vendor in Kathmandu, Nepal, sells 200 cups of juice per day at a price of 50 rupees per cup. For each 5-rupee increase in the price, the vendor expects to sell 10 fewer cups per day. Based on these expectations, what price per cup, in rupees, gives the greatest daily revenue?
solution: Let \(n\) be the number of 5-rupee increases. Price: \(50 + 5n\). Cups sold: \(200 - 10n\).
The parabola opens downward, so the maximum is at \(n = \frac{-10 + 20}{2} = 5\).
The price is \(50 + 5(5) = 75\) rupees, with revenue \(75 \cdot 150 = 11{,}250\) rupees.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the price at which the vendor would sell 0 cups, so the revenue would be 0.
explanation.B: Correct. After \(n\) increases, revenue is \((50 + 5n)(200 - 10n)\), with zeros at \(n = -10\) and \(n = 20\). The maximum is at \(n = 5\), a price of \(50 + 25 = 75\) rupees.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This takes the midpoint of \(n = 0\) and \(n = 20\). The revenue is 0 at \(n = -10\) and \(n = 20\), so the maximum is midway between those, at \(n = 5\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of 5-rupee increases that gives the greatest revenue, not the price.

items.stem: The value of a painting increased by the same percent each year from 2019 to 2021. The painting was worth 8,000 dollars in 2019 and 9,680 dollars in 2021. By what percent did the value of the painting increase each year?
solution: Let \(r\) be the yearly growth factor. Then \(8{,}000r^{2} = 9{,}680\), so \(r^{2} = 1.21\).
A growth factor of 1.1 is an increase of \(10\%\) per year.

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2x\) and \(g(x) = x - k\), where \(k\) is a constant. The vertex of the graph of \(y = f(g(x))\) in the \(xy\)-plane has \(x\)-coordinate 4. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: \(f(g(x)) = (x - k + 1)^{2} - 1\), whose vertex is at \(x = k - 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of solving \(k - 1 = 4\) as \(k = 4 - 1\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This assumes the vertex of \(f\) is at \(x = 0\). The vertex of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2x\) is at \(x = -1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of treating \(g(x) = x - k\) as a shift of \(k\) units to the left. Subtracting \(k\) shifts the graph \(k\) units to the right.
explanation.D: Correct. The vertex of \(f\) is at \(x = -1\). \(f(g(x))\) reaches it when \(x - k = -1\), so \(x = k - 1 = 4\) and \(k = 5\).

items.stem: A ball is launched straight up from ground level. Its height, in meters, \(t\) seconds after it is launched is modeled by \(h(t) = -5t^{2} + vt\), where \(v\) is a positive constant that represents the launch speed, in meters per second. If the ball reaches a maximum height of 45 meters, what is the value of \(v\)?
solution: The vertex of \(h(t) = -5t^{2} + vt\) is at \(t = -\frac{v}{2(-5)} = \frac{v}{10}\).

explanation.A: Correct. The vertex is at \(t = \frac{v}{10}\), and \(h\left(\frac{v}{10}\right) = \frac{v^{2}}{20}\). So \(\frac{v^{2}}{20} = 45\) and \(v = 30\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This doubles the maximum height. With \(v = 90\), the maximum height would be \(\frac{90^{2}}{20} = 405\) meters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the time, in seconds, at which the ball reaches its maximum height when \(v = 30\), not the launch speed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the maximum height, not the launch speed. With \(v = 45\), the maximum height would be \(\frac{45^{2}}{20} = 101.25\) meters.

items.stem: The graph of \(y = f(x)\) is shown, where \(f(x) = a(b)^{x} + c\) and \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants with \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\). The line \(y = -3\), also shown, is a horizontal asymptote of the graph. Which of the following must be true?
solution: As \(x\) increases, \(a(b)^{x}\) approaches 0 when \(0 < b < 1\), so \(f(x)\) approaches \(c\). The asymptote is \(y = c\), so \(c = -3\).
The graph falls from left to right. With \(a > 0\), that happens only when \(0 < b < 1\).

explanation.A: Correct. With \(a > 0\), the graph decreases only if \(0 < b < 1\). The term \(a(b)^{x}\) approaches 0, so the asymptote is \(y = c\), and \(c = -3 < 0\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. With \(a > 0\) and \(b > 1\), the graph would increase from left to right. The graph shown decreases.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The asymptote is \(y = c\), and the asymptote shown is \(y = -3\), so \(c\) is negative.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The graph decreases, so \(b < 1\), and the asymptote \(y = c = -3\) is below the \(x\)-axis, so \(c < 0\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 3^{x}\). If \(f(a) = 5\), what is the value of \(f(2a + 1)\)?

The entrance to a garden is shaped like a parabolic arch. The table shows the height \(h(x)\), in meters, of the arch at three horizontal distances \(x\), in meters, from one end of its base. What is the maximum height, in meters, of the arch?
solution: The height is 0 at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 8\), so \(h(x) = ax(x - 8)\) and the vertex is at \(x = 4\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the greatest height in the table. The arch keeps rising after \(x = 2\) until \(x = 4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This assumes the height keeps rising at 3 meters per 2 meters, as for a line. A parabola rises more slowly near its vertex.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the width of the base of the arch, not its height.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + 13\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x + h)\), where \(h\) is a constant. In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = g(x)\) is symmetric about the \(y\)-axis. What is the value of \(h\)?
solution: \(f(x) = (x - 3)^{2} + 4\), so the graph of \(f\) is symmetric about \(x = 3\).
\(g(x) = f(x + h) = (x + h - 3)^{2} + 4\), which is symmetric about \(x = 3 - h\).
For symmetry about the \(y\)-axis, \(3 - h = 0\), so \(h = 3\).

explanation.A: Correct. The graph of \(f\) has its axis of symmetry at \(x = 3\). \(g(x) = f(x + 3)\) shifts it 3 units left, onto the \(y\)-axis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses the coefficient 6 directly. The axis of symmetry is at \(x = \frac{6}{2} = 3\), so the shift is 3.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(g(x) = f(x - 3)\) shifts the graph 3 units right, moving the axis of symmetry to \(x = 6\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the minimum value of \(f\), \(f(3) = 4\), not the needed shift.

items.stem: The population of a city is modeled by \(P(t) = 2.4(1.025)^{t}\), where \(P(t)\) is the population, in millions, \(t\) years after 2020. According to the model, which of the following is closest to the number of years after 2020 it will take for the population to reach 1.5 times its 2020 value?
solution: Graph \(y = 1.025^{x}\) and \(y = 1.5\), or use logarithms: \(t = \frac{\log 1.5}{\log 1.025} \approx 16.4\).
Of the choices, 16 is closest.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1}{0.025}\), which treats the question as the time for the population to grow by \(100\%\) without compounding.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{1.5}{0.025}\), which divides the factor 1.5 by the yearly rate instead of solving \((1.025)^{t} = 1.5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This divides the \(50\%\) increase by \(2.5\%\) per year, which ignores compounding. With compounding, the population reaches 1.5 times sooner.
explanation.D: Correct. Solve \((1.025)^{t} = 1.5\): \(t = \frac{\log 1.5}{\log 1.025} \approx 16.4\). A graphing calculator also shows \(y = 1.025^{t}\) meets \(y = 1.5\) near \(t = 16.4\).

items.stem: The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = 3(2)^{x}\). What is the value of \(g(3)\)?
solution: Evaluate the power first: \(2^{3} = 8\), so \(g(3) = 3 \cdot 8 = 24\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(3\) and \(2\) before applying the exponent: \(6^{3} = 216\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3\) to \(2^{3}\) instead of multiplying: \(3 + 8 = 11\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying instead of raising to a power: \(3 \cdot 2 \cdot 3 = 18\).

items.stem: The number of fish in a pond \(t\) years after 2024 is estimated by the function \(P(t) = 450(0.92)^{t}\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number \(450\) in this context?

choices.A: The estimated number of fish in the pond in 2024
choices.B: The estimated number of fish in the pond in 2025
choices.C: The estimated number of fish that leave the pond each year
choices.D: The estimated percent decrease in the number of fish each year

solution: In a model \(a(b)^{t}\), the value at \(t = 0\) is \(a(b)^{0} = a\).
Here \(t = 0\) is the year 2024, so \(P(0) = 450\) is the estimated number of fish in the pond in 2024.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of using \(t = 1\) instead of \(t = 0\); the estimate for 2025 is \(P(1) = 414\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This confuses the starting amount with a yearly change; in this model the yearly change is not constant, and \(450\) is the value at \(t = 0\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. The yearly percent decrease comes from the base \(0.92\): it is \(8\%\). The coefficient \(450\) is the starting value.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. For what value of \(x\) does \(f(x)\) reach its minimum value?
solution: The minimum of an upward-opening parabola is at its vertex, the lowest point of the graph.
The vertex shown is \((1, -4)\), so the minimum occurs at \(x = 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(-4\) is the minimum value of \(f(x)\), the \(y\)-coordinate of the vertex, not the value of \(x\) where it occurs.
explanation.B: Correct. The lowest point of the graph is the vertex \((1, -4)\), so the minimum occurs at \(x = 1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(x = 3\) is an \(x\)-intercept, where \(f(x) = 0\); the graph keeps going lower to the left of it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(-3\) is the \(y\)-intercept, \(f(0)\), not the \(x\)-value of the lowest point.

items.stem: The function \(h\) is defined by \(h(x) = x^{3} - 10\). What is the value of \(h(3)\)?

A volleyball is hit upward. Its height above the ground, in meters, \(t\) seconds after it is hit is given by \(h(t) = -5t^{2} + 15t + 1\). What is the height, in meters, of the ball 2 seconds after it is hit?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of dropping the negative sign on \(-5t^{2}\): \(20 + 30 + 1 = 51\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying \(-5\) by \(2\) instead of by \(2^{2}\): \(-10 + 30 + 1 = 21\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(1\) is \(h(0)\), the height at the moment the ball is hit, not 2 seconds later.

items.stem: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of \(y = 7(0.6)^{x} + 2\) in the \(xy\)-plane?
solution: The \(y\)-intercept is where \(x = 0\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of substituting \(x = 1\) instead of \(x = 0\): \(7(0.6) + 2 = 6.2\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of taking the added constant as the \(y\)-intercept, as for a line \(y = mx + b\); here \(7(0.6)^{0}\) is \(7\), not \(0\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of stopping after \(7(0.6)^{0} = 7\) and forgetting to add \(2\).

items.stem: The value, in dollars, of a laptop \(t\) years after it was bought is modeled by \(V(t) = 1{,}200(0.75)^{t}\). According to the model, what is the value, in dollars, of the laptop 2 years after it was bought?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting \(25\%\) of the original price each year (\(1{,}200 - 2 \cdot 300\)), a linear model instead of the exponential one given.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying by \(2\) instead of using \(2\) as the exponent: \(1{,}200 \cdot 0.75 \cdot 2 = 1{,}800\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(900\) is \(V(1)\), the value after 1 year; the model must be applied for a second year.

items.stem: A scientist models the number of cells in a sample \(h\) hours after the start of an experiment with the function \(C(h) = 50(3)^{h}\). According to the model, how many cells are in the sample 4 hours after the start of the experiment?
The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = -3(x - 2)^{2} + 5\). What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: In vertex form \(a(x - h)^{2} + k\) with \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward and its maximum value is \(k\).
Here \(a = -3\), \(h = 2\) and \(k = 5\), so the maximum value is \(5\), reached at \(x = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(2\) is the value of \(x\) at which the maximum occurs, not the maximum value of \(f(x)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of reading the \(-2\) inside \((x - 2)\) with its sign and as the output; the vertex is \((2, 5)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(-3\) is the leading coefficient; its sign shows the graph opens downward, but it is not the maximum value.
explanation.D: Correct. The vertex is \((2, 5)\) and the parabola opens downward, so the maximum value is \(5\).

items.stem: A bakery sells loaves of bread for \(p\) dollars each. The number of loaves sold per day is \(300 - 20p\), so the daily revenue, in dollars, is \(R(p) = p(300 - 20p)\). What is the daily revenue, in dollars, when the price is 5 dollars per loaf?

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of ignoring the \(-20p\) term: \(5 \cdot 300 = 1{,}500\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(200\) is the number of loaves sold per day at that price, not the revenue.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of subtracting \(20\) instead of \(20 \cdot 5\): \(5(300 - 20) = 1{,}400\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(b)^{x}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. If \(f(0) = 6\) and \(f(2) = 54\), which of the following defines \(f\)?

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of taking \(\frac{54}{6} = 9\) as the base; that is the growth over 2 steps of \(x\), so \(b^{2} = 9\).
explanation.B: Correct. \(a = f(0) = 6\) and \(b^{2} = 9\) with \(b > 0\) gives \(b = 3\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of swapping the roles of \(a\) and \(b\); this function gives \(f(0) = 3\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This linear function also passes through \((0, 6)\) and \((2, 54)\), but \(f\) must have the exponential form \(a(b)^{x}\).

items.stem: The vertex of the graph of \(y = x^{2} - 10x + 31\) in the \(xy\)-plane is \((h, k)\). What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: So \(y = (x - 5)^{2} + 6\), and the vertex is \((5, 6)\).
Therefore \(k = 6\).
