items.stem: A model rocket is launched from the ground. The graph shows its height \(h(t)\), in meters, \(t\) seconds after launch. The point \((3, 45)\) is the highest point of the graph. Which of the following is the best interpretation of this point?

choices.A: The rocket reaches its maximum height of 3 meters 45 seconds after launch.
choices.B: The rocket rises 45 meters every 3 seconds.
choices.C: The rocket lands 3 seconds after launch, 45 meters from where it was launched.
choices.D: The rocket reaches its maximum height of 45 meters 3 seconds after launch.

solution: The first coordinate is the time \(t\) in seconds and the second is the height \(h(t)\) in meters.
The highest point is the maximum height: \(45\) meters, reached \(3\) seconds after launch.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of swapping the coordinates: the first coordinate is time and the second is height.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats the graph as a line with a constant rate; the height of the rocket rises more slowly as it nears the top and then falls.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The rocket lands when \(h(t) = 0\), at \(t = 6\); the graph shows height, not horizontal distance.
explanation.D: Correct. At \(t = 3\) seconds the height reaches its greatest value, \(45\) meters.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2}\). The graph of \(y = g(x)\) is the result of shifting the graph of \(y = f(x)\) 3 units to the right and 2 units up. Which of the following defines \(g\)?
solution: Shifting a graph \(3\) units to the right replaces \(x\) with \(x - 3\): \(y = (x - 3)^{2}\).
Shifting \(2\) units up adds \(2\) to the output: \(g(x) = (x - 3)^{2} + 2\).
Check: the vertex moves from \((0, 0)\) to \((3, 2)\).

explanation.A: Correct. Replacing \(x\) with \(x - 3\) shifts right 3, and adding \(2\) shifts up 2; the vertex is \((3, 2)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip on the vertical shift: subtracting \(2\) moves the graph down.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of swapping the two shifts: this graph is 2 units right and 3 units up.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip: \((x + 3)^{2}\) shifts the graph 3 units to the left.

items.stem: Ayesha deposits 50,000 rupees in a savings account in Islamabad. The account earns \(8\%\) interest compounded annually, and she makes no other deposits or withdrawals. Which of the following functions gives the value \(V(t)\), in rupees, of the account after \(t\) years?
solution: Each year the balance is multiplied by \(1 + 0.08 = 1.08\).
Starting from \(50{,}000\), after \(t\) years the value is \(V(t) = 50{,}000(1.08)^{t}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is simple interest: it adds \(8\%\) of the original deposit each year and ignores interest earned on interest.
explanation.B: Correct. Each year the balance is multiplied by \(1.08\), starting from \(50{,}000\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of using the interest rate itself as the growth factor; multiplying by \(0.08\) would shrink the balance to \(8\%\) of its value each year.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of writing \(8\%\) as \(0.8\): the factor \(1.8\) is an \(80\%\) increase per year.

items.stem: The mass, in grams, of algae growing in a laboratory tank \(d\) days after the start of an experiment is modeled by \(M(d) = 20(2)^{\frac{d}{5}}\). According to the model, how many days after the start of the experiment will the mass of the algae be 160 grams?
solution: Therefore \(d = 15\).

items.stem: The table shows four values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(f(x)\) for an exponential function \(f\). Which of the following defines \(f\)?
solution: Each value of \(f(x)\) is \(3\) times the one before (\(36 = 3 \cdot 12\), \(108 = 3 \cdot 36\), \(324 = 3 \cdot 108\)), so the base is \(3\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This linear function fits only the first two rows; it gives \(f(3) = 60\), not \(108\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of swapping the coefficient and the base; it gives \(f(2) = 48\), not \(36\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of taking \(f(1) = 12\) as the starting value; \(12\) is the value at \(x = 1\), not at \(x = 0\), so this gives \(f(1) = 36\).

items.stem: A rectangular garden has a length that is 4 meters greater than its width. If the width of the garden is \(w\) meters, which function gives the area \(A(w)\), in square meters, of the garden?
solution: The length is \(w + 4\) meters.
Area is length times width: \(A(w) = w(w + 4) = w^{2} + 4w\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of a distribution slip: \(w(w + 4)\) is \(w^{2} + 4w\), not \(w^{2} + 4\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the perimeter of the garden, \(2w + 2(w + 4)\), not its area.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the width by \(4w\) instead of by \(w + 4\).
explanation.D: Correct. Area \(= w(w + 4) = w^{2} + 4w\).

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} + 1\) and \(g(x) = x - 3\). What is the value of \(f(g(5))\)?
solution: Work from the inside out: \(g(5) = 5 - 3 = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(g(f(5)) = 26 - 3 = 23\): the functions were applied in the wrong order.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of stopping at \(2^{2} = 4\) and forgetting to add \(1\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(f(5) + g(5) = 26 + 2\) instead of composing the functions.

items.stem: A shopkeeper in Chittagong sells packets of snacks for \(x\) taka per packet. The shopkeeper's daily profit, in taka, is modeled by \(P(x) = -2x^{2} + 120x - 1{,}000\). According to the model, what price per packet, in taka, gives the greatest daily profit?
solution: The graph of \(P\) is a parabola that opens downward, so the greatest profit is at the vertex.
The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{120}{2(-2)} = 30\).
So a price of \(30\) taka gives the greatest daily profit (\(P(30) = 800\) taka).

items.stem: The number of subscribers to an online newsletter \(t\) years after it was launched is modeled by \(S(t) = 800(1.44)^{t}\). Which of the following is equivalent to \(S(t)\) and shows that the number of subscribers increases by \(20\%\) every half year?
solution: An increase of \(20\%\) per half year means multiplying by \(1.2\) once every half year, which is \(2t\) times in \(t\) years.

explanation.A: Correct. \((1.2)^{2t} = ((1.2)^{2})^{t} = (1.44)^{t}\), and the base \(1.2\) with exponent \(2t\) shows a \(20\%\) increase every half year.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the exponent by 2 instead of multiplying it: \(t\) years contain \(2t\) half years, not \(\frac{t}{2}\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of splitting the \(44\%\) yearly increase into two halves of \(22\%\); percent increases compound, so this is not equivalent.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the growth factor \(1.44\) by 2; a factor of \(0.72\) would mean a decrease.

items.stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown. The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x - 3)\). For what value of \(x\) does \(g(x)\) reach its maximum value?
solution: From the graph, \(f\) reaches its maximum at the vertex \((-1, 4)\).
\(g(x) = f(x - 3)\) shifts the graph of \(f\) 3 units to the right, so the vertex of \(g\) is \((-1 + 3, 4) = (2, 4)\).
So \(g\) reaches its maximum at \(x = 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(4\) is the maximum value of \(g(x)\), not the value of \(x\) where it occurs.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(-1\) is where \(f\) reaches its maximum; the shift to \(g\) was not applied.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of shifting in the wrong direction: \(f(x - 3)\) moves the graph 3 units to the right, not to the left.
explanation.D: Correct. Replacing \(x\) with \(x - 3\) moves the vertex 3 units right, from \(x = -1\) to \(x = 2\).

items.stem: A laboratory in Pune is studying a substance that breaks down over time. The amount of the substance, in milligrams, \(t\) hours after the start of the study is \(A(t) = 640\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{6}}\). How many hours after the start of the study will 40 milligrams of the substance remain?
solution: Set \(640\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{6}} = 40\) and divide by \(640\): \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{t}{6}} = \frac{1}{16}\).
\(\frac{1}{16} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{4}\), so \(\frac{t}{6} = 4\): the amount halves 4 times.
Each halving takes 6 hours, so \(t = 24\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(16\) is the ratio \(\frac{640}{40}\), how many times smaller the amount becomes, not a number of hours.
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(4\) is the number of halvings, \(\frac{t}{6}\), not the number of hours; each halving takes 6 hours.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of multiplying the ratio \(\frac{640}{40} = 16\) by 6; the number of halvings is 4, not 16.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 4)(x + 10)\). What is the minimum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: The zeros of \(f\) are \(4\) and \(-10\). The vertex lies halfway between them, at \(x = \frac{4 + (-10)}{2} = -3\).
The parabola opens upward, so the minimum is \(f(-3) = (-3 - 4)(-3 + 10) = (-7)(7) = -49\).

items.stem: The table shows five values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(f(x)\), where \(f\) is a quadratic function. Which of the following defines \(f\)?
solution: The values \(f(1) = -1\) and \(f(3) = -1\) are equal, so the axis of symmetry is \(x = 2\), and \(f(2) = -2\) gives the vertex \((2, -2)\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip in vertex form: \((x + 2)^{2}\) puts the vertex at \(x = -2\); this gives \(f(0) = 2\) but \(f(1) = 7\).
explanation.B: Correct. The vertex is \((2, -2)\) and \(f(0) = 4 - 2 = 2\); every row of the table fits.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip on the constant: the vertex is \((2, -2)\), and this gives \(f(2) = 2\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This linear function fits only the first two rows; it gives \(f(1) = -3\), not \(-1\).

items.stem: The number of insects in a laboratory colony \(t\) days after the start of an experiment is modeled by \(P(t) = 2{,}000(1.5)^{\frac{t}{4}}\). Which of the following statements best describes how the number of insects changes, according to the model?

choices.A: The number of insects increases by 150% every 4 days.
choices.B: The number of insects increases by 50% every day.
choices.C: The number of insects increases by 12.5% every day.
choices.D: The number of insects increases by 50% every 4 days.

solution: When \(t\) increases by 4, the exponent \(\frac{t}{4}\) increases by 1, so the number of insects is multiplied by \(1.5\).
Multiplying by \(1.5 = 1 + 0.5\) is an increase of \(50\%\). So the number of insects increases by \(50\%\) every 4 days.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of reading the factor \(1.5\) as the increase; multiplying by \(1.5\) is a \(50\%\) increase, and a \(150\%\) increase would multiply by \(2.5\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This ignores the \(\frac{t}{4}\) in the exponent; the factor \(1.5\) applies once every 4 days, not every day.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of dividing the \(50\%\) by 4 days; percent growth compounds, so the daily increase is \((1.5)^{\frac{1}{4}} - 1\), about \(10.7\%\).
explanation.D: Correct. Every 4 days the exponent grows by 1, so the number is multiplied by \(1.5\), a \(50\%\) increase.

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 2x^{2} - 12x + k\), where \(k\) is a constant. If the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is \(5\), what is the value of \(k\)?
solution: The vertex is at \(x = -\frac{-12}{2(2)} = 3\).
The minimum value is \(f(3) = 2(9) - 36 + k = k - 18\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip when solving \(k - 18 = 5\): computing \(k = 18 - 5 = 13\) instead of \(k = 5 + 18 = 23\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. \(5\) is the minimum value of \(f(x)\), not the value of \(k\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of ignoring the coefficient \(2\) when completing the square: \(-9 + k = 5\) gives \(14\), but \(2x^{2} - 12x + k = 2(x - 3)^{2} - 18 + k\).

items.stem: A gardener uses 200 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular plot along a straight wall. No fencing is needed along the wall. If each of the two sides perpendicular to the wall is \(x\) meters long, the area of the plot, in square meters, is \(A(x) = x(200 - 2x)\). What is the greatest possible area, in square meters, of the plot?
solution: \(A(x) = -2x^{2} + 200x\) is a parabola that opens downward; its zeros are \(x = 0\) and \(x = 100\).
The vertex is halfway between the zeros, at \(x = 50\).

items.stem: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are defined by \(f(x) = 2x - 1\) and \(g(x) = x^{2} + 3\). Which of the following is equivalent to \(g(f(x))\)?
solution: Substitute \(f(x) = 2x - 1\) for the input of \(g\): \(g(f(x)) = (2x - 1)^{2} + 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the product \(f(x) \cdot g(x)\), not the composition \(g(f(x))\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(f(g(x)) = 2(x^{2} + 3) - 1\): the functions were composed in the wrong order.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of squaring \(2x - 1\) as \(4x^{2} + 1\), leaving out the middle term \(-4x\).

items.stem: A cup of coffee is left to cool in a room. Its temperature, in degrees Celsius, \(m\) minutes after it is poured is modeled by \(T(m) = 20 + 70(0.9)^{m}\). The graph of \(y = T(m)\) is shown. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number \(20\) in this context?

choices.A: The temperature, in degrees Celsius, that the coffee approaches as time passes
choices.B: The percent by which the temperature of the coffee decreases each minute
choices.C: The number of degrees Celsius that the coffee cools each minute
choices.D: The temperature, in degrees Celsius, of the coffee when it is poured

solution: At \(m = 0\), \(T(0) = 20 + 70 = 90\), the temperature when the coffee is poured.
As \(m\) increases, \((0.9)^{m}\) gets closer and closer to \(0\), so \(T(m)\) gets closer and closer to \(20\).
So \(20\) is the temperature, in degrees Celsius, that the coffee approaches over time (the room temperature).

explanation.A: Correct. As \(m\) grows, \(70(0.9)^{m}\) approaches \(0\), so \(T(m)\) approaches \(20\) degrees Celsius.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The percent change comes from the base \(0.9\): the difference between the coffee's temperature and \(20\) degrees shrinks by \(10\%\) each minute.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The model is not linear, so the coffee does not cool by a fixed number of degrees each minute; \(20\) is a constant added to the exponential part.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The temperature when the coffee is poured is \(T(0) = 90\) degrees Celsius, not \(20\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = a(x - 2)(x - 8)\), where \(a\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane passes through the point \((4, 16)\). What is the maximum value of \(f(x)\)?
solution: Use the point: \(f(4) = a(2)(-4) = -8a = 16\), so \(a = -2\). Since \(a < 0\), the parabola opens downward and has a maximum.
The vertex is halfway between the zeros \(2\) and \(8\), at \(x = 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(5\) is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex, where the maximum occurs, not the maximum value.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of a sign slip with \(a\): using \(a = 2\) gives \(f(5) = -18\), but \(-8a = 16\) means \(a = -2\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(a = -2\), the vertex is at \(x = 5\), and \(f(5) = -2(3)(-3) = 18\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(16\) is the value of \(f(4)\), given in the problem; \(x = 4\) is not the vertex, so this is not the maximum.

items.stem: For the exponential function \(f\), \(f(x) = a(b)^{x}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. If \(f(3) = 40\) and \(f(5) = 90\), what is the value of \(f(4)\)?
solution: Check: \(f(5) = 60 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 90\). (Each step multiplies by the same factor, so \(f(4)\) is the geometric mean of \(40\) and \(90\).)

items.stem: A wildlife survey estimates that a population of frogs in a protected wetland is 5,000 and that the population decreases by \(20\%\) every 3 years. Which of the following functions models the population \(P(m)\) of frogs \(m\) months after the survey?
solution: Every 3 years the population is multiplied by \(1 - 0.20 = 0.8\).
3 years is 36 months, so the number of 3-year periods in \(m\) months is \(\frac{m}{36}\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of inverting the conversion: \(36m\) would apply the \(20\%\) decrease 36 times every month.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of forgetting to convert years to months: \(\frac{m}{3}\) applies the decrease every 3 months, not every 3 years.
explanation.C: Correct. After \(m = 36\) months (3 years) the exponent is 1 and the population is \(0.8(5{,}000) = 4{,}000\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of using the percent decrease as the factor; keeping \(20\%\) each period would mean an \(80\%\) decrease.

items.stem: For the quadratic function \(f\), \(f(-1) = 3\) and \(f(7) = 3\), and the minimum value of \(f(x)\) is \(-13\). What is the value of \(f(0)\)?
solution: Equal outputs at \(x = -1\) and \(x = 7\) mean the axis of symmetry is halfway between them: \(x = \frac{-1 + 7}{2} = 3\).
So the vertex is \((3, -13)\) and \(f(x) = a(x - 3)^{2} - 13\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. \(-13\) is the minimum value, \(f(3)\); \(x = 0\) is not at the vertex.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(3\) is the value of \(f\) at \(x = -1\) and \(x = 7\), not at \(x = 0\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of stopping at \((0 - 3)^{2} = 9\) and forgetting the \(-13\).

items.stem: The number of homes using rooftop solar panels in a district of Bangladesh \(t\) years after 2022 is modeled by \(N(t) = 120(1.5)^{t}\). According to the model, in what year will the number of homes using rooftop solar panels first be more than 8 times the number in 2022?
solution: \((1.5)^{5} \approx 7.59\), which is less than \(8\), and \((1.5)^{6} \approx 11.39\), which is more than \(8\).
So the number first exceeds 8 times the 2022 number at \(t = 6\), which is the year 2028.

explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of treating the growth as doubling: \(2^{3} = 8\), but the factor is \(1.5\), not \(2\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of setting \(t = 8\) because the number must become 8 times as large; the exponent and the multiple are not the same.
explanation.D: Incorrect. In 2027 (\(t = 5\)), \((1.5)^{5} \approx 7.59\), which is still less than \(8\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^{2} - 6x + c\), where \(c\) is a constant. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane crosses the \(x\)-axis at two points that are 10 units apart. What is the value of \(c\)?
solution: The axis of symmetry is \(x = \frac{6}{2} = 3\), and the two \(x\)-intercepts are symmetric about it.
They are 10 units apart, so each is 5 units from \(x = 3\): \(x = -2\) and \(x = 8\).

items.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x - 1)^{2} + 4\). The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = -f(x + 2) + 3\). The graph of \(y = g(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane is a parabola. What are the coordinates of its vertex?
solution: The vertex of \(f\) is \((1, 4)\).
\(f(x + 2)\) shifts the graph 2 units left: vertex \((-1, 4)\).
The negative sign reflects it over the \(x\)-axis: vertex \((-1, -4)\). Adding \(3\) shifts it up: vertex \((-1, -1)\).

explanation.A: Correct. Shift left 2 to \((-1, 4)\), reflect to \((-1, -4)\), then shift up 3 to \((-1, -1)\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of shifting in the wrong direction: \(f(x + 2)\) moves the graph 2 units to the left, not to the right.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of adding \(3\) before reflecting, \(-(4 + 3) = -7\); the \(+3\) is applied after the negative sign.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of leaving out the reflection: without the negative sign the vertex would be \((-1, 4 + 3)\).

items.stem: The graphs of \(y = 2^{x}\) and \(y = x + 1\) are shown in the \(xy\)-plane. They intersect at \((0, 1)\) and \((1, 2)\). For which values of \(x\) is \(2^{x} < x + 1\)?
solution: \(2^{x} < x + 1\) where the exponential graph is below the line.
The graphs meet only at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 1\). Between them, for example at \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), \(2^{\frac{1}{2}} \approx 1.41 < 1.5\), so the curve is below the line.
Outside that interval the curve is above the line (for example \(2^{2} = 4 > 3\) and \(2^{-1} = 0.5 > 0\)). So \(0 < x < 1\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the result of reading the \(y\)-coordinates of the intersection points, \(1\) and \(2\), as \(x\)-values.
explanation.B: Incorrect. For \(x > 1\) the exponential curve rises above the line (for example \(2^{2} = 4 > 3\)).
explanation.C: Incorrect. On these intervals \(2^{x} > x + 1\): this describes where the curve is above the line, the opposite inequality.
explanation.D: Correct. Between the intersection points the exponential curve is below the line.

items.stem: A theater sells \(600 - 20p\) tickets for a show when the ticket price is \(p\) dollars, so the revenue, in dollars, is \(R(p) = p(600 - 20p)\). The revenue at a price of 10 dollars is the same as the revenue at one other price. What is that other price, in dollars?
solution: \(R(p) = p(600 - 20p)\) has zeros \(p = 0\) and \(p = 30\), so its graph is a parabola symmetric about \(p = 15\).
Prices with equal revenue are the same distance from \(15\). The price \(10\) is 5 below \(15\), so the other price is 5 above: \(20\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. \(30\) is a zero of \(R\): at that price no tickets are sold and the revenue is \(0\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the result of reflecting in the wrong direction, \(10 - 5\); the reflection of \(10\) about \(15\) is \(20\).
explanation.C: Correct. The graph is symmetric about \(p = 15\), and \(R(20) = R(10) = 4{,}000\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(15\) is the price that gives the greatest revenue, the vertex, not a second price with the same revenue as \(10\).

items.stem: The number of followers of a new online account \(w\) weeks after it was created is modeled by \(F(w) = a(b)^{w}\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are positive constants. According to the model, the account had 150 followers 1 week after it was created and 1,350 followers 3 weeks after it was created. According to the model, how many followers did the account have when it was created?
solution: When the account was created, \(w = 0\) and \(F(0) = a = 50\).

items.stem: The dot plot shows the number of books each of 11 students read during summer vacation. What is the median number of books read?
solution: There are 11 values, so the median is the 6th value when the values are in order.
In order: 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 9. The 6th value is 3.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the mode, the value that occurs most often, not the median.
explanation.B: Correct. With 11 values in order, the 6th value is the middle one, and it is 3.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the middle of the scale from 1 to 9, \(\frac{1 + 9}{2} = 5\). The median is the middle data value, not the middle of the range of values.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the range, \(9 - 1 = 8\), not the median.

items.stem: The table shows the number of runs a batter scored in each of five cricket matches. What is the mean number of runs per match?
solution: Divide by the number of matches: \(\frac{240}{5} = 48\).

explanation.A: Correct. The total is 240 runs in 5 matches, and \(\frac{240}{5} = 48\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the median: in order the runs are 18, 34, 52, 60, 76, and the middle value is 52.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the range, \(76 - 18 = 58\), not the mean.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the total number of runs. It still has to be divided by the 5 matches.

items.stem: The histogram summarizes the one-way commute times, in minutes, of the 30 employees at an office. Each interval includes its left endpoint but not its right endpoint. Which interval contains the median commute time?
solution: With 30 values, the median is the average of the 15th and 16th values in order.
Count up from the shortest times: 4 employees take under 10 minutes, \(4 + 9 = 13\) take under 20 minutes, and \(13 + 8 = 21\) take under 30 minutes.
The 15th and 16th values are both among the employees counted from 14 to 21, so the median is in the interval from 20 to 30 minutes.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Only the 4 shortest commute times are in this interval. The median is the average of the 15th and 16th values.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This interval has the tallest bar (the most employees), or it contains 15 minutes if the 15th position is mistaken for 15 minutes. Only 13 employees have commutes under 20 minutes, so the 15th and 16th values are not here.
explanation.C: Correct. 13 employees commute less than 20 minutes and 21 commute less than 30 minutes, so the 15th and 16th values, and therefore the median, are in this interval.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the interval whose bar height, 6, is the median of the bar heights 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9. The median must be found from the 30 commute times, not from the bar heights.

items.stem: The box plot summarizes the daily high temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit, in a coastal city for the 31 days of May. What is the interquartile range of the daily high temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit?
solution: The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first quartile.
From the box plot, \(Q_{3} = 79\) and \(Q_{1} = 66\), so the interquartile range is \(79 - 66 = 13\).

items.stem: The dot plot shows the number of goals scored in a season by each of the 10 players on a soccer team. A new player who scored 15 goals in the season joins the team, and that player's total is added to the data. Which statement best describes how the mean and the median of the data change?

choices.A: The mean increases, and the median does not change.
choices.B: The median increases, and the mean does not change.
choices.C: Both increase, and the median increases by more than the mean.
choices.D: Both increase, and the mean increases by more than the median.

solution: Before: the total is 46 goals, so the mean is \(\frac{46}{10} = 4.6\). In order the values are 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 8, so the median is \(\frac{4 + 5}{2} = 4.5\).
After: the total is \(46 + 15 = 61\) goals for 11 players, so the mean is \(\frac{61}{11} \approx 5.55\). The median is the 6th value of 11, which is 5.
The mean increases by about 0.95 and the median increases by 0.5, so both increase and the mean increases by more.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This assumes an extreme value never changes the median. With an even number of values, the median is the average of 4 and 5; after the new value it is the 6th value, 5, so it increases from 4.5 to 5.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Adding a value of 15, which is greater than the old mean of 4.6, must increase the mean. It rises to \(\frac{61}{11} \approx 5.55\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The median increases by only \(5 - 4.5 = 0.5\), while the mean increases by about \(5.55 - 4.6 = 0.95\).
explanation.D: Correct. The mean rises from 4.6 to about 5.55 (by about 0.95), and the median rises from 4.5 to 5 (by 0.5).

items.stem: The box plots summarize the delivery times, in minutes, of all orders delivered by two food-delivery riders, Ali and Bilal, in Karachi during one week. Which statement is true?

choices.A: Ali's delivery times have the greater median and the greater interquartile range.
choices.B: Bilal's delivery times have the greater range and the greater interquartile range.
choices.C: Ali's delivery times have the greater range, and Bilal's have the greater median.
choices.D: The two riders' delivery times have the same interquartile range.

solution: Ali: median 24, range \(44 - 12 = 32\), interquartile range \(30 - 18 = 12\).
Bilal: median 26, range \(40 - 15 = 25\), interquartile range \(28 - 20 = 8\).
So Ali's times have the greater range and the greater interquartile range, and Bilal's times have the greater median.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Ali's interquartile range (12) is greater, but Ali's median is 24, which is less than Bilal's median of 26.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This reverses the spreads. Bilal's range is \(40 - 15 = 25\) and interquartile range is \(28 - 20 = 8\); both are smaller than Ali's 32 and 12.
explanation.C: Correct. Ali's range is 32 and Bilal's is 25, while Bilal's median of 26 is greater than Ali's median of 24.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The boxes have different lengths: Ali's interquartile range is \(30 - 18 = 12\), and Bilal's is \(28 - 20 = 8\).

items.stem: A data set of daily high temperatures, in degrees Celsius, has a mean of \(20\) and a standard deviation of \(5\). Each temperature \(C\) is converted to degrees Fahrenheit using \(F = 1.8C + 32\). What are the mean and the standard deviation of the converted temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit?
solution: Multiplying every value by 1.8 multiplies both the mean and the standard deviation by 1.8.
Adding 32 to every value adds 32 to the mean but does not change the standard deviation, because the values do not become more or less spread out.
Mean: \(1.8 \cdot 20 + 32 = 68\). Standard deviation: \(1.8 \cdot 5 = 9\).

explanation.A: Correct. The mean is converted like any temperature, \(1.8 \cdot 20 + 32 = 68\); the standard deviation is only scaled, \(1.8 \cdot 5 = 9\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. Multiplying every value by 1.8 spreads the values out by a factor of 1.8, so the standard deviation changes to \(1.8 \cdot 5 = 9\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the result of converting the standard deviation with the full formula, \(1.8 \cdot 5 + 32 = 41\). Adding 32 to every value shifts the data but does not change its spread.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the result of forgetting to add 32 to the mean: \(1.8 \cdot 20 = 36\). Every converted value, and so the mean, is 32 degrees higher.

items.stem: The mean age of the \(n\) members of a chess club is 16 years. When a 46-year-old coach and a 40-year-old assistant coach join the club, the mean age of the group increases to 19 years. What is the value of \(n\)?
solution: The total age of the members is \(16n\). After the coaches join, the total is \(16n + 46 + 40 = 16n + 86\) for \(n + 2\) people.
Set up the new mean: \(16n + 86 = 19(n + 2) = 19n + 38\).

items.stem: The box plot summarizes the finishing times, in minutes, of the 50 runners in a 5-kilometer race. What is the range of the finishing times, in minutes?
solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value.
From the box plot, the least time is 19 minutes and the greatest is 42 minutes, so the range is \(42 - 19 = 23\).

explanation.A: Correct. The range is \(42 - 19 = 23\) minutes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the interquartile range, \(31 - 24 = 7\), not the range.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the median finishing time, not the range.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the greatest finishing time. The range subtracts the least time, 19, from it.

items.stem: The table shows the rainfall, in millimeters, recorded at a weather station in Sylhet on each of 7 days. What is the median daily rainfall, in millimeters?
solution: Put the 7 values in order: 8, 12, 17, 22, 30, 30, 45.
With 7 values, the median is the 4th value in order, which is 22.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the range, \(45 - 8 = 37\), not the median.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the middle entry of the table as listed (Day 4). The values must be put in order before finding the middle one.
explanation.C: Correct. In order the values are 8, 12, 17, 22, 30, 30, 45, and the middle (4th) value is 22.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the mode, the value that appears most often, not the median.

items.stem: The dot plot shows a data set of 8 values. What is the mean of the data set?
solution: The sum of the 8 values is \(2 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 7 = 40\).
The mean is \(\frac{40}{8} = 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the median, \(\frac{5 + 6}{2} = 5.5\), not the mean.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the mode, the value with the most dots, not the mean.
explanation.C: Correct. The sum is 40 and there are 8 values, so the mean is \(\frac{40}{8} = 5\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This divides the sum, 40, by the number of different values, 5, instead of by the number of data values, 8.

items.stem: At a factory, the 12 workers on the morning shift packed a mean of 45 boxes per hour, and the 18 workers on the evening shift packed a mean of 50 boxes per hour. What is the mean number of boxes packed per hour for all 30 workers?
solution: Morning total: \(12 \cdot 45 = 540\). Evening total: \(18 \cdot 50 = 900\).
The mean for all 30 workers is \(\frac{540 + 900}{30} = \frac{1{,}440}{30} = 48\).
Note that the answer is not 47.5, the average of 45 and 50, because the two shifts have different numbers of workers.

items.stem: The box plots summarize the heights, in centimeters, of tomato plants grown with Fertilizer P and of tomato plants grown with Fertilizer Q. Which statement is true?

choices.A: The interquartile range of the Fertilizer Q heights is greater than the interquartile range of the Fertilizer P heights.
choices.B: The tallest of all the plants was grown with Fertilizer P.
choices.C: The median height of the Fertilizer P plants is greater than the median height of the Fertilizer Q plants.
choices.D: The two data sets have the same range.

solution: Fertilizer P: median 44, range \(58 - 30 = 28\), interquartile range \(49 - 38 = 11\).
Fertilizer Q: median 46, range \(61 - 26 = 35\), interquartile range \(55 - 35 = 20\).
Only the statement about the interquartile ranges is true: 20 is greater than 11.

explanation.A: Correct. The interquartile range is \(55 - 35 = 20\) for Fertilizer Q and \(49 - 38 = 11\) for Fertilizer P.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The greatest height for Fertilizer P is 58 centimeters, but the greatest for Fertilizer Q is 61 centimeters.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The median for Fertilizer P is 44 and the median for Fertilizer Q is 46, so the Fertilizer Q median is greater.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The ranges are \(58 - 30 = 28\) and \(61 - 26 = 35\), which are not equal.

items.stem: The mean of the data set \(2, 5, 5, k, 9, 11\) is \(6\). What is the median of the data set?
solution: The sum of the 6 values is \(6 \cdot 6 = 36\), so \(2 + 5 + 5 + k + 9 + 11 = 36\) and \(k = 4\).
In order the values are 2, 4, 5, 5, 9, 11.
The median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: \(\frac{5 + 5}{2} = 5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This averages the 3rd and 4th values as listed, 5 and \(k = 4\), without first putting the values in order.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the value of \(k\), not the median of the data set.
explanation.C: Correct. With k = 4, the ordered values are 2, 4, 5, 5, 9, 11, and the median is 5.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the mean of the data set, which is given, not the median.

items.stem: The table shows the frequency of each value in data set X and in data set Y. Which statement is true?

choices.A: The mean of data set Y is greater than the mean of data set X.
choices.B: The standard deviations of the two data sets are equal.
choices.C: The standard deviation of data set Y is greater than the standard deviation of data set X.
choices.D: The standard deviation of data set X is greater than the standard deviation of data set Y.

solution: Both data sets have 18 values, and both are symmetric about 3, so both means are 3.
In data set X, 12 of the 18 values equal the mean, 3. In data set Y, 12 of the 18 values are at 1 or 5, the values farthest from the mean.
The values of Y are spread farther from the mean, so Y has the greater standard deviation.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Both data sets are symmetric about 3, so both means are 3.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The two data sets use the same values, 1 through 5, but with different frequencies. Data set Y has many more values far from the mean.
explanation.C: Correct. Most values of Y are at 1 and 5, far from the mean of 3, while most values of X are at 3, so Y has the greater standard deviation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The tall frequency at 3 in data set X means most of its values are at the mean, which makes the spread small, not large.

items.stem: The mean mass of 9 packages waiting at a mail counter is 2.4 kilograms. Another package, with a mass of 1.4 kilograms, is added to the group. What is the mean mass, in kilograms, of the 10 packages?
solution: The total mass of the 9 packages is \(9 \cdot 2.4 = 21.6\) kilograms.
With the new package, the total is \(21.6 + 1.4 = 23\) kilograms for 10 packages.
The mean is \(\frac{23}{10} = 2.3\) kilograms.

items.stem: For which of the following data sets is the median greater than the mean?
solution: For each data set of 5 values in order, the median is the 3rd value.
A: median 9, mean \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\). B: median 3, mean 4. C: median 5, mean 5. D: median 6, mean 7.
Only in choice A is the median greater than the mean. The low value 2 pulls the mean below the median.

explanation.A: Correct. The median is 9 and the mean is \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\), so the median is greater.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The median is 6 and the mean is \(\frac{35}{5} = 7\), so the mean is greater.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The values are evenly spaced, so the median and the mean are both 5.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The median is 3 and the mean is 4. The high value 10 makes the mean greater than the median, the reverse of what is asked.

items.stem: The histogram shows the lengths, in minutes, of the 24 songs on a playlist. Each interval includes its left endpoint but not its right endpoint. Which of the following could be the range of the song lengths, in minutes?
solution: The shortest song is in the interval from 2 to 3 minutes, so it is at least 2 and less than 3 minutes long.
The longest song is in the interval from 5 to 6 minutes, so it is at least 5 and less than 6 minutes long.
So the range is greater than \(5 - 3 = 2\) and less than \(6 - 2 = 4\). Of the choices, only 3.2 is in this interval.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the difference between the tallest and shortest bars, \(9 - 4 = 5\), which compares numbers of songs, not song lengths.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the width of each interval. The range is the longest length minus the shortest length, which must be greater than 2 minutes.
explanation.C: Correct. The range must be greater than 2 and less than 4 minutes, and 3.2 is in that interval (for example, songs of 2.5 and 5.7 minutes).
explanation.D: Incorrect. A range of 4 would need a song of 6 minutes and a song of 2 minutes, but no song is 6 minutes or longer, so the range is less than \(6 - 2 = 4\).

items.stem: The dot plot shows the number of customers who arrived at a bank during each of nine 10-minute intervals. The value 7 is removed from the data. Which statement best describes how the mean and the standard deviation of the data change?

choices.A: The mean does not change, and the standard deviation does not change.
choices.B: The mean decreases, and the standard deviation increases.
choices.C: The mean does not change, and the standard deviation decreases.
choices.D: The mean does not change, and the standard deviation increases.

solution: The sum of the 9 values is 63, so the mean is \(\frac{63}{9} = 7\). The removed value is equal to the mean.
After the removal, the sum is 56 for 8 values, and the mean is still \(\frac{56}{8} = 7\).
The removed value was at distance 0 from the mean. Every remaining value is farther from the mean on average, so the standard deviation increases.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The mean stays the same, but removing a value with zero distance from the mean leaves only values that are farther from it, so the spread about the mean increases.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The removed value, 7, equals the mean, so the mean stays \(\frac{56}{8} = 7\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. Removing a value makes the data set smaller, but the value removed was the one closest to the mean. That increases, not decreases, the typical distance from the mean.
explanation.D: Correct. The mean stays 7 because the removed value equals the mean, and the standard deviation increases because the value removed was the one closest to the mean.

items.stem: A survey asked a group of households in Lahore how many motorcycles they own. The table shows the percent of the surveyed households that own each number of motorcycles. What is the mean number of motorcycles per household for the surveyed households?
solution: Each percent tells what fraction of the households has that number of motorcycles.
(Using 100 households gives the same result: 135 motorcycles for 100 households.)

items.stem: In a diving competition, each dive is scored by 6 judges. For one dive, the mean of the 6 scores was 8.8. The highest score, 9.6, and the lowest score, 7.2, are then removed. What is the mean of the remaining 4 scores?
solution: The sum of the 6 scores is \(6 \cdot 8.8 = 52.8\).
Removing 9.6 and 7.2 leaves a sum of \(52.8 - 9.6 - 7.2 = 36\).
The mean of the remaining 4 scores is \(\frac{36}{4} = 9\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This divides the remaining sum, 36, by 6 instead of by the 4 scores that remain.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This removes only the lowest score: \(\frac{52.8 - 7.2}{5} = 9.12\). The highest score must be removed too.
explanation.C: Correct. The remaining sum is \(52.8 - 16.8 = 36\), and \(\frac{36}{4} = 9\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This assumes that removing one high score and one low score leaves the mean unchanged. The low score, 7.2, is farther below 8.8 than 9.6 is above it, so the mean increases.

items.stem: The data set \(7, 8, 9, 13, 24, x\) has a median of \(10\). What is the mean of the data set?
solution: With 6 values, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values in order.
If \(x \le 9\), the median is at most \(\frac{8 + 9}{2} = 8.5\); if \(x \ge 13\), the median is \(\frac{9 + 13}{2} = 11\). So \(9 < x < 13\), and \(\frac{9 + x}{2} = 10\) gives \(x = 11\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the mean of only the 5 known values, \(\frac{61}{5} = 12.2\); it leaves out \(x\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This divides the correct sum, 72, by 5 instead of by 6, the number of values.
explanation.C: Correct. The median condition gives \(x = 11\), and the mean is \(\frac{72}{6} = 12\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the median, which is given. The large value 24 makes the mean greater than the median.

items.stem: The bar graph shows the number of school days missed last term by each of the 25 students in a class. Which statement about the mean and the median of the data is true?

choices.A: The mean is equal to the median.
choices.B: The mean is greater than the median by 2.
choices.C: The median is greater than the mean.
choices.D: The mean is greater than the median by 0.72.

solution: The median is the 13th value in order. Six students missed 0 days (values 1 to 6) and eight missed 1 day (values 7 to 14), so the median is 1.
The mean is greater than the median by \(1.72 - 1 = 0.72\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. The mean is 1.72 and the median is 1; the student who missed 8 days and the long right side of the data raise the mean.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This finds the mean of the listed values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 as \(\frac{18}{6} = 3\) without using the numbers of students, and subtracts the median, 1.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The data are skewed to the right, and the mean, 1.72, is greater than the median, 1.
explanation.D: Correct. The mean is \(\frac{43}{25} = 1.72\) and the median is 1, so the mean is greater by 0.72.

items.stem: A data set consists of 10 numbers, including the numbers \(a\) and \(b\), and has a mean of 20. When \(a\) and \(b\) are both removed, the mean of the remaining 8 numbers is 18. When only \(a\) is removed, the mean of the remaining 9 numbers is 21. What is the value of \(b\)?
solution: The sum of all 10 numbers is \(10 \cdot 20 = 200\).
Without \(a\) and \(b\), the sum is \(8 \cdot 18 = 144\), so \(a + b = 200 - 144 = 56\).
Without only \(a\), the sum is \(9 \cdot 21 = 189\), so \(a = 200 - 189 = 11\).

items.stem: A data set consists of 5 positive integers. The only mode of the data set is 3, the median is 5, and the range is 8. Which of the following could be the mean of the data set?
solution: In order, call the values \(p \le q \le 5 \le r \le s\). The value 3 must appear at least twice, and only \(p\) and \(q\) can be less than 5, so \(p = q = 3\).
The range is 8, so \(s = 3 + 8 = 11\). Then \(r\) is between 5 and 11, and \(r\) cannot be 5 or 11, or that value would also appear twice and 3 would not be the only mode.
So \(r\) is 6, 7, 8, 9 or 10, and the mean \(\frac{22 + r}{5}\) is 5.6, 5.8, 6, 6.2 or 6.4. Only 6.2 (with \(r = 9\)) is a choice.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses a greatest value of \(5 + 8 = 13\), measuring the range from the median instead of from the least value, 3.
explanation.B: Correct. The data set 3, 3, 5, 9, 11 has only mode 3, median 5, range 8 and mean 6.2.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A mean of 5.4 needs \(r = 5\), but then 5 would appear twice, as often as 3, and 3 would not be the only mode.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A mean of 6.6 needs \(r = 11\), but then 11 would appear twice, as often as 3, and 3 would not be the only mode.

items.stem: A bakery in Colombo recorded the number of loaves of bread it sold on each of 15 days. The median of the data was 62 loaves, and the greatest value was 98 loaves. Later, the owner found that this greatest value had been recorded incorrectly; the correct value was 89 loaves. After the error is corrected, which of the following must be true? I. The mean decreases by 0.6 loaves. II. The median does not change. III. The range decreases by 9 loaves.
solution: I: The total decreases by \(98 - 89 = 9\), so the mean decreases by \(\frac{9}{15} = 0.6\). This must be true.
II: The value changes from 98 to 89, and both are greater than the median, 62. The value stays in the upper half of the ordered data, so the 8th value, the median, does not change. This must be true.
III: If another day's sales were, say, 95 loaves, then after the correction the greatest value is 95 and the range decreases by only 3. So III does not have to be true.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Statement III assumes 89 becomes the greatest value. If another day had more than 89 loaves, the range decreases by less than 9.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Statement II must also be true: the corrected value, 89, is still above the median, 62, so the middle value of the ordered data is unchanged.
explanation.C: Correct. Statements I and II must be true. Statement III need not be, because another day's value between 89 and 98 would become the new greatest value.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Statement I must also be true: lowering one of 15 values by 9 lowers the total by 9 and the mean by \(\frac{9}{15} = 0.6\).

items.stem: What is the mean of the data set \(3, 11, 6, 14, 6\)?
solution: Divide by the number of values: \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\).

explanation.A: Correct. The sum of the 5 values is 40, and \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the sum of the values. It still has to be divided by the 5 values.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the range, \(14 - 3 = 11\), not the mean.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the median (and also the mode) of the data set, not the mean.

items.stem: What is the median of the data set \(18, 26, 25, 21, 30, 22\)?
solution: Put the values in order: 18, 21, 22, 25, 26, 30.
There are 6 values, so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: \(\frac{22 + 25}{2} = 23.5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is only the lower of the two middle values. With an even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle values, 22 and 25.
explanation.B: Correct. In order the values are 18, 21, 22, 25, 26, 30, and the mean of the two middle values is \(\frac{22 + 25}{2} = 23.5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the range, \(30 - 18 = 12\), not the median.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values as listed, \(\frac{25 + 21}{2} = 23\). The values must be put in order first.

items.stem: A survey recorded the number of people living in each of 12 households in a village in Nepal. The table shows the results. What is the mode of the number of people per household?
solution: The mode is the value that occurs most often.
The greatest number of households, 6, have 5 people, so the mode is 5.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the mean household size, \(\frac{54}{12} = 4.5\), not the mode.
explanation.B: Correct. More households (6 of them) have 5 people than any other size, so 5 is the mode.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the range of the household sizes, \(6 - 3 = 3\), not the mode.
explanation.D: Incorrect. 6 is the number of households that have 5 people, not the household size that occurs most often.

items.stem: The dot plot shows a data set of 9 values. What is the range of the data set?
solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value.
The greatest value is 10 and the least is 4, so the range is \(10 - 4 = 6\).

items.stem: A cyclist recorded her times, in seconds, for four laps of a track: 72, 75, 69 and 76. What is her mean lap time, in seconds?
solution: Divide by the 4 laps: \(\frac{292}{4} = 73\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the total time for the 4 laps. It still has to be divided by 4.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the mean of only the fastest and slowest times, \(\frac{69 + 76}{2} = 72.5\). All four times must be used.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the median: in order the times are 69, 72, 75, 76, and \(\frac{72 + 75}{2} = 73.5\).
explanation.D: Correct. The total time is 292 seconds for 4 laps, and \(\frac{292}{4} = 73\).

items.stem: The box plot summarizes the ages, in years, of the volunteers at a city library. What is the median age, in years?
solution: In a box plot, the median is the line inside the box.
The line inside the box is at 41, so the median age is 41 years.

explanation.A: Correct. The median is marked by the line inside the box, at 41.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the midpoint of the box, \(\frac{30 + 45}{2} = 37.5\). The median is the line drawn inside the box, which need not be in the middle of the box.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the range, \(61 - 22 = 39\), not the median.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the third quartile, the right end of the box, not the median.

items.stem: In the data set \(5, 5, 8, 9, 13\), the value \(13\) is replaced with \(23\). Which of the following does NOT change?
solution: Before: mean \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\), median 8, range \(13 - 5 = 8\), largest value 13.
After: mean \(\frac{50}{5} = 10\), median 8, range \(23 - 5 = 18\), largest value 23.
Only the median stays the same: the middle value is still 8.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The sum increases by 10, so the mean increases from \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\) to \(\frac{50}{5} = 10\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. The range changes from \(13 - 5 = 8\) to \(23 - 5 = 18\).
explanation.C: Correct. The values stay in the same order and the middle (3rd) value is still 8, so the median does not change.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The largest value changes from 13 to 23.

items.stem: The mean of six numbers is \(15\). What is the sum of the six numbers?
solution: The mean is the sum divided by the number of values, so the sum is the mean times the number of values.

items.stem: The histogram shows the scores of the students in a class in Lahore on a mathematics test. Each interval includes its left endpoint but not its right endpoint. How many students scored at least 70?
solution: A score of at least 70 is in one of the intervals 70 to 80, 80 to 90 or 90 to 100.
Add those bars: \(9 + 6 + 2 = 17\).

explanation.A: Correct. \(9 + 6 + 2 = 17\) students scored 70 or more.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is only the bar for 70 to 80. The bars for 80 to 90 and 90 to 100 must be added too.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This counts only the students who scored 80 or more. Students who scored from 70 up to 80 also scored at least 70.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the number of students who scored less than 70, \(3 + 7 = 10\).

items.stem: Which of the following data sets has a range of \(10\)?
solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value, wherever those values appear in the list.
For \(9, 3, 13, 7\): the greatest value is 13 and the least is 3, so the range is \(13 - 3 = 10\).
The other ranges are 7, 13 and 20.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The first value minus the last value is \(12 - 2 = 10\), but the range uses the greatest and least values: \(15 - 2 = 13\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This data set contains the value 10, but its range is \(11 - 4 = 7\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. The gaps between neighboring values are 10, but the range is \(21 - 1 = 20\).
explanation.D: Correct. The greatest value is 13 and the least is 3, and \(13 - 3 = 10\).

items.stem: Mateo's scores on his first four tests were 82, 76, 91 and 85. What score does he need on the fifth test so that the mean of all five scores is 84?
solution: For a mean of 84 over 5 tests, the total must be \(5 \cdot 84 = 420\).
His first four scores add to \(82 + 76 + 91 + 85 = 334\).

explanation.A: Correct. The five scores must total \(5 \cdot 84 = 420\), and \(420 - 334 = 86\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the total of all five scores needed. The first four scores, which add to 334, must be subtracted.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the mean of the first four scores, \(\frac{334}{4} = 83.5\), not the score needed on the fifth test.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the target mean, not the score needed. A fifth score of 84 gives a total of 418 and a mean of 83.6, because the first four scores average less than 84.

items.stem: A bakery recorded the number of wedding cakes it sold each day for 10 days. The table shows the results. What is the mean number of wedding cakes sold per day?
solution: Total cakes: \(3 \cdot 2 + 4 \cdot 3 + 5 \cdot 4 + 6 \cdot 1 = 6 + 12 + 20 + 6 = 44\).
There are 10 days, so the mean is \(\frac{44}{10} = 4.4\).

items.stem: What is the interquartile range of the data set \(2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20\)?
solution: The 8 values are in order. The lower half is 2, 5, 7, 8 and the upper half is 10, 12, 15, 20.
First quartile: \(\frac{5 + 7}{2} = 6\). Third quartile: \(\frac{12 + 15}{2} = 13.5\).
Interquartile range: \(13.5 - 6 = 7.5\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the third quartile. The first quartile, 6, must be subtracted from it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the 7th value minus the 2nd value, \(15 - 5 = 10\). Each quartile is the median of one half of the data: the mean of the two middle values of that half.
explanation.C: Correct. \(Q_{1} = 6\) and \(Q_{3} = 13.5\), so the interquartile range is \(13.5 - 6 = 7.5\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the range, \(20 - 2 = 18\), not the interquartile range.

items.stem: Over the same five days, the daily high temperatures, in degrees Celsius, were 20, 21, 22, 23 and 24 in Town P and 12, 22, 22, 22 and 32 in Town Q. Which statement about the standard deviations of the two data sets is true?

choices.A: The standard deviations are equal, because the two data sets have the same mean.
choices.B: Town Q's temperatures have the greater standard deviation.
choices.C: The standard deviations are equal, because the two data sets have the same median.
choices.D: Town P's temperatures have the greater standard deviation.

solution: Both data sets have a mean of 22, so compare how far the values are from 22.
In Town P every value is within 2 degrees of 22. In Town Q two values are 10 degrees away from 22.
The values for Town Q are more spread out from the mean, so Town Q has the greater standard deviation.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The means are equal (22), but data sets with the same mean can be spread out differently. Town Q's values are farther from 22.
explanation.B: Correct. Both means are 22, and Town Q has two values 10 degrees from the mean, while every Town P value is within 2 degrees of it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The medians are equal (22), but the median says nothing about spread. Town Q's values are farther from the center.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Town P has more different values, but they are all close to the mean of 22. Standard deviation measures distance from the mean, not how many different values there are.

items.stem: The ages of the 7 people in a study group are 10, 12, 13, 15, 15, 19 and 56 years. The 56-year-old is the group's tutor. If the tutor's age is removed from the data, by how many years does the mean age decrease?
solution: With the tutor: the total is 140 years, so the mean is \(\frac{140}{7} = 20\).
Without the tutor: the total is \(140 - 56 = 84\) years, so the mean is \(\frac{84}{6} = 14\).
The mean decreases by \(20 - 14 = 6\) years.

explanation.A: Correct. The mean drops from \(\frac{140}{7} = 20\) to \(\frac{84}{6} = 14\), a decrease of 6 years.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the new mean age, not the amount by which the mean decreases.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the difference between the tutor's age and the new mean, \(56 - 14 = 42\), not the change in the mean.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{56}{7} = 8\), the tutor's share of the old total. Removing a value also changes the number of values from 7 to 6, so both means must be computed.

items.stem: The table shows the number of siblings reported by each of 20 students. What is the median number of siblings?
solution: With 20 values, the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th values in order.
3 students have 0 siblings, and \(3 + 7 = 10\) have 0 or 1. So the 10th value is 1 and the 11th value is 2.
The median is \(\frac{1 + 2}{2} = 1.5\).

items.stem: The mean hourly wage of the 25 employees at a store is \$31. If every employee receives a raise of \$4 per hour, what is the new mean hourly wage, in dollars?
solution: Adding the same amount to every value adds that amount to the mean.
New mean: \(31 + 4 = 35\) dollars.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Every wage goes up by 4 dollars, so the total goes up and the mean goes up too.
explanation.B: Correct. The total of the wages increases by \(25 \cdot 4 = 100\) dollars, so the mean increases by \(\frac{100}{25} = 4\) dollars, to 35.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This adds the total of all the raises, \(25 \cdot 4 = 100\), to the mean. That total must be shared among the 25 employees, so the mean rises by only 4.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(31 \cdot 4\). The raise is added to each wage, not multiplied.

items.stem: The histogram summarizes the monthly electricity bills, in taka, of 40 households in Chattogram. Each interval includes its left endpoint but not its right endpoint. What percent of the households had a bill of at least 2,000 taka?
solution: Bills of at least 2,000 taka are in the intervals 2,000 to 2,500 and 2,500 to 3,000: \(12 + 8 = 20\) households.
As a percent of 40 households: \(\frac{20}{40} = 0.5\), or \(50\%\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This uses only the bar for 2,000 to 2,500 taka: \(\frac{12}{40} = 30\%\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This adds the bars for 1,500 to 2,000 and 2,000 to 2,500 taka, \(\frac{14 + 12}{40} = 65\%\). Bills in the 1,500 to 2,000 interval are less than 2,000 taka.
explanation.C: Correct. \(12 + 8 = 20\) of the 40 households had bills of at least 2,000 taka, and \(\frac{20}{40} = 50\%\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses only the bar for 2,500 to 3,000 taka: \(\frac{8}{40} = 20\%\).

items.stem: The mean of \(x\), \(2x\), \(9\) and \(13\) is \(10\). What is the value of \(x\)?
solution: The four values must add to \(4 \cdot 10 = 40\): \(x + 2x + 9 + 13 = 40\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is the value of \(2x\), not \(x\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This comes from leaving the 9 out of the sum: \(3x + 13 = 40\) gives \(x = 9\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the value of \(3x\). It still has to be divided by 3.

items.stem: A farmer weighed 5 pumpkins, and their mean weight was 12 kilograms. After the farmer sold one of the pumpkins, the mean weight of the remaining 4 pumpkins was 10 kilograms. What was the weight, in kilograms, of the pumpkin that was sold?
solution: Total weight of the 5 pumpkins: \(5 \cdot 12 = 60\) kilograms.
Total weight of the remaining 4: \(4 \cdot 10 = 40\) kilograms.
The pumpkin sold weighed \(60 - 40 = 20\) kilograms.

items.stem: The table shows the annual salaries, in thousands of dollars, of the 10 employees of a small company. Which statement about the mean and the median of the salaries is true?

choices.A: The median is greater than the mean by 10.5 thousand dollars.
choices.B: The mean is greater than the median by 8 thousand dollars.
choices.C: The mean is greater than the median by 10.5 thousand dollars.
choices.D: The mean is greater than the median by 28.75 thousand dollars.

solution: Total: \(40 \cdot 4 + 45 \cdot 3 + 50 \cdot 2 + 160 \cdot 1 = 555\), so the mean is \(\frac{555}{10} = 55.5\) thousand dollars.
With 10 values, the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values. The first 4 salaries are 40 and the next 3 are 45, so both are 45, and the median is 45 thousand dollars.
The mean is greater than the median by \(55.5 - 45 = 10.5\) thousand dollars.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The difference is 10.5 thousand dollars, but the direction is reversed. The one large salary of 160 thousand dollars pulls the mean (55.5) above the median (45).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This uses a median of \(\frac{45 + 50}{2} = 47.5\), the middle of the listed salaries. The median must be found from all 10 values: the 5th and 6th values are both 45.
explanation.C: Correct. The mean is 55.5 thousand dollars and the median is 45 thousand dollars, a difference of 10.5 thousand dollars.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the mean of the four listed salaries, \(\frac{40 + 45 + 50 + 160}{4} = 73.75\), which ignores how many employees earn each salary. \(73.75 - 45 = 28.75\).

items.stem: The data set \(4, 8, 10, 12, 16\) has a mean of \(10\). Which of the following values, if added to the data set, would decrease the standard deviation?
solution: The standard deviation measures how far the values are from the mean, on average.
Adding a value equal to the mean, 10, keeps the mean at 10 and adds a value with a distance of 0, so the typical distance from the mean becomes smaller.
Values such as 2, 15 and 20 are far enough from the mean to make the data more spread out, which increases the standard deviation.

explanation.A: Incorrect. A small number does not make a small standard deviation. The value 2 is 8 away from the mean, which makes the data more spread out.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The value 15 is within the range of the data, but it is 5 away from the mean, which is more than the typical distance, so the standard deviation increases.
explanation.C: Correct. The value 10 is equal to the mean, so it adds no distance from the mean and the standard deviation decreases.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The value 20 is 10 away from the mean, which makes the data more spread out and increases the standard deviation.

items.stem: The dot plot shows the number of times each of the 13 members of a climbing club visited the climbing gym last month. Which statement about the data is true?

choices.A: The mean and the median are equal.
choices.B: The median is greater than the mean.
choices.C: The mean is greater than the median.
choices.D: The mode is greater than the median.

solution: The total is 48 visits, so the mean is \(\frac{48}{13} \approx 3.7\).
With 13 values, the median is the 7th value in order, which is 2. The mode is 1.
The few large values (9 and 13) pull the mean above the median.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The mean is about 3.7 and the median is 2. They would be equal only for data that are balanced around the center.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The median is 2, but the large values 9 and 13 pull the mean up to about 3.7.
explanation.C: Correct. The mean is \(\frac{48}{13} \approx 3.7\) and the median is 2. The data are skewed to the right, so the mean is greater.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The mode is 1, which is less than the median of 2.

items.stem: The table shows how many of the 25 students in a class earned each score on a 10-point quiz, where \(k\) is a constant. What is the median score?
solution: There are 25 students, so \(3 + 5 + k + 7 + 4 = 25\) and \(k = 6\).
With 25 values, the median is the 13th value in order.
3 students scored 6, \(3 + 5 = 8\) scored 7 or less, and \(8 + 6 = 14\) scored 8 or less. So the 13th score is 8.

items.stem: The table shows the number of goals a futsal team in Kathmandu scored in each of its matches last season, where \(k\) is a positive integer. The mean number of goals per match was 2. What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Total goals: \(0 \cdot 3 + 1 \cdot 5 + 2 \cdot 4 + 3k = 13 + 3k\). Number of matches: \(3 + 5 + 4 + k = 12 + k\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This leaves the 3 matches with 0 goals out of the count of matches: \(13 + 3k = 2(9 + k)\) gives \(k = 5\). Matches with 0 goals still count as matches.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the number of goals scored in the 3-goal matches, \(3 \cdot 11 = 33\), not the value of \(k\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the total number of matches, \(12 + 11 = 23\), not the value of \(k\).

items.stem: The box plot summarizes the scores of 60 students on a history exam. Approximately how many of the students had scores between 61 and 97?
solution: 61 is the first quartile and 97 is the maximum.
About 25% of the scores are below the first quartile, so about 75% are between 61 and 97.
\(0.75 \cdot 60 = 45\) students.

explanation.A: Correct. From the first quartile to the maximum is about 75% of the data, and \(0.75 \cdot 60 = 45\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is about one quarter of the students, the number from the third quartile (78) to the maximum. The scores from 61 to 97 cover three quarters of the data.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(97 - 61 = 36\), the difference between the scores, not a number of students.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is about half the students, the number in the box from 61 to 78. The scores from 78 to 97 are also between 61 and 97.

items.stem: A data set has a median of \(12\) and a range of \(20\). Each value in the data set is multiplied by \(3\), and then \(5\) is subtracted from the result. What are the median and the range of the new data set?
solution: The middle value is changed like every other value: new median \(= 3 \cdot 12 - 5 = 31\).
Multiplying by 3 triples every distance between values, so the range becomes \(3 \cdot 20 = 60\).
Subtracting 5 shifts every value by the same amount, so it does not change the range.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Multiplying every value by 3 spreads the values out, so the range is tripled, not unchanged.
explanation.B: Correct. The median becomes \(3 \cdot 12 - 5 = 31\), and the range becomes \(3 \cdot 20 = 60\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This applies the whole rule to the range, \(3 \cdot 20 - 5 = 55\). Subtracting 5 from every value does not change the distance between the greatest and least values.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This multiplies the median by 3 but forgets to subtract 5: \(3 \cdot 12 - 5 = 31\), not 36.

items.stem: The mean of the 25 scores on a 50-point quiz was recorded as 18. Later, the teacher found that one score had been entered as 47 instead of the correct score, 22. What is the correct mean of the 25 scores?
solution: Recorded total: \(25 \cdot 18 = 450\).
The correct total is \(47 - 22 = 25\) less: \(450 - 25 = 425\).
Correct mean: \(\frac{425}{25} = 17\).

items.stem: The bar graph shows the number of pets in each of 20 households surveyed on one street. What is the mean number of pets per household?
solution: Total pets: \(0 \cdot 6 + 1 \cdot 9 + 2 \cdot 4 + 3 \cdot 1 = 20\).
There are 20 households, so the mean is \(\frac{20}{20} = 1\).

explanation.A: Correct. The 20 households have 20 pets in all, so the mean is 1 pet per household.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the height of the tallest bar, the number of households with 1 pet.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the mean of the categories 0, 1, 2 and 3, \(\frac{6}{4} = 1.5\), which ignores how many households are in each category.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is the mean height of the bars, \(\frac{20}{4} = 5\). That is the average number of households per category, not the average number of pets.

items.stem: Which of the following data sets has the smallest standard deviation?
solution: Standard deviation measures how spread out the values are from their mean, not how large the values are.
\(100, 101, 102, 103, 104\) are all within 2 of their mean, 102. Each of the other data sets has values 4 or more away from its mean.
So that data set has the smallest standard deviation.

explanation.A: Correct. The values are only 1 apart and at most 2 away from their mean of 102, so they have the least spread.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Three of the values are equal, but the mean is 13 and every value is 8 or 12 away from it, so the spread is large.
explanation.C: Incorrect. These are the smallest numbers, but the values are 2 apart and up to 4 away from their mean of 5. Standard deviation does not depend on the size of the values.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The values are evenly spaced, but they are 10 apart and up to 20 away from their mean of 30, so the spread is large.

items.stem: The data set \(4, 7, 9, k, 15\) has a mean equal to its median. Which of the following could be the value of \(k\)?
solution: The mean is \(\frac{35 + k}{5}\). The median depends on where \(k\) falls when the values are put in order.
If \(k \ge 9\), the order is 4, 7, 9, \(k\), 15 (or 4, 7, 9, 15, \(k\)) and the median is 9. Then \(\frac{35 + k}{5} = 9\) gives \(k = 10\), which is at least 9, so it works.
Check: 4, 7, 9, 10, 15 has median 9 and mean \(\frac{45}{5} = 9\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. With \(k = 9\), the median is 9, but the mean is \(\frac{44}{5} = 8.8\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. With \(k = 12\), the median is still 9, but the mean is \(\frac{47}{5} = 9.4\). Keeping the median at 9 is not enough; the mean must also equal 9.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This comes from leaving \(k\) out of the sum: \(\frac{35}{5} = 7\), the median when \(k\) is small. With \(k = 5\), the mean is \(\frac{40}{5} = 8\), but the median is 7.
explanation.D: Correct. With \(k = 10\), the values in order are 4, 7, 9, 10, 15; the median is 9 and the mean is \(\frac{45}{5} = 9\).

items.stem: In a class, the mean score of the boys on a test was 70 and the mean score of the girls was 80. The mean score of the whole class was 74. What fraction of the students in the class are girls?
solution: Let \(p\) be the fraction of students who are girls. Then \(1 - p\) are boys.
The class mean is a weighted mean: \(70(1 - p) + 80p = 74\).

items.stem: A data set has a mean of \(m\) and a standard deviation of \(s\), where \(s > 0\). Two new values, each equal to \(m\), are added to the data set. Which statement about the new data set is true?

choices.A: The mean is \(m\), and the standard deviation is \(s\).
choices.B: The mean is greater than \(m\), and the standard deviation is less than \(s\).
choices.C: The mean is \(m\), and the standard deviation is less than \(s\).
choices.D: The mean is \(m\), and the standard deviation is greater than \(s\).

solution: The two new values add \(2m\) to the total and 2 to the count, so the mean stays \(m\).
Each new value is 0 away from the mean. The total of the squared distances from the mean stays the same, but it is now shared among more values.
So the values are, on average, closer to the mean, and the standard deviation is less than \(s\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. The mean does not change, but the standard deviation does: the new values add no distance from the mean while increasing the number of values, so the typical distance shrinks.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Adding values equal to the mean does not change the mean. The total increases by \(2m\) and the count by 2.
explanation.C: Correct. The mean stays \(m\), and values equal to the mean make the data, on average, closer to the mean, so the standard deviation decreases.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Adding values makes the data set larger, but values equal to the mean make it less spread out, not more.

items.stem: The dot plot shows the number of sixes hit during a season by each of the 9 batters in a school cricket team in Chennai. One value is removed from the data. The median of the remaining 8 values is 0.5 greater than the median of the original 9 values, and the mean of the remaining values is greater than the original mean. Which value could have been removed?
solution: The original median is the 5th value, 6, and the original mean is \(\frac{52}{9} \approx 5.8\).
For the new median to be 6.5, the two middle values of the remaining 8 must be 6 and 7, so the removed value must be less than 6.
Removing 4 leaves 2, 3, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10: the median is \(\frac{6 + 7}{2} = 6.5\) and the mean is \(\frac{48}{8} = 6\), which is greater than about 5.8.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Removing a value above the median pulls the median down: the middle values become 4 and 6, and the median is 5.
explanation.B: Correct. Without 4, the median is \(\frac{6 + 7}{2} = 6.5\), 0.5 more than 6, and the mean rises from about 5.8 to 6.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Removing the median value 6 leaves 4 and 7 in the middle, so the median becomes \(\frac{4 + 7}{2} = 5.5\), which is less than 6.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Removing the largest value lowers the mean, to \(\frac{42}{8} = 5.25\), and the median becomes \(\frac{4 + 6}{2} = 5\).

items.stem: In the data set \(3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 40\), the value \(40\) is changed to \(80\). Which of the following statistics change?

choices.A: The mean, the range and the standard deviation only
choices.B: The mean, the median, the range and the standard deviation
choices.C: The mean and the range only
choices.D: The mean, the range, the standard deviation and the interquartile range

solution: The total increases by 40, so the mean changes. The greatest value changes, so the range changes (from 37 to 77).
The largest value moves farther from the mean, so the standard deviation increases.

The order of the values is the same and the middle value is still 8, so the median does not change. The first and third quartiles depend only on values in the lower and upper halves near the middle (5 and 12), so the interquartile range does not change either.

explanation.A: Correct. The mean, the range and the standard deviation all depend on the largest value, while the median and the interquartile range do not.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The median does not change. The values keep the same order, and the middle (4th) value is still 8.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The standard deviation also changes: the largest value is now much farther from the mean, so the data are more spread out.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The interquartile range does not change. The quartiles come from values near the middle of each half (5 and 12), not from the largest value.

items.stem: A data set consists of 6 positive integers. Its only mode is \(4\), its median is \(5\) and its mean is \(6\). What is the greatest possible value in the data set?
solution: The sum of the 6 integers is \(6 \cdot 6 = 36\). In order, call them \(a \le b \le c \le d \le e \le f\); the median gives \(c + d = 10\).
4 must appear at least twice, so it must be among \(a, b, c\), which forces \(c = 4\) and \(d = 6\), with \(b = 4\).
To make \(f\) as large as possible, make the others small: \(a = 1\). If \(e = 6\), then 6 would appear as often as 4, so \(e = 7\).

items.stem: A data set of 20 values has a mean of 15. The values are split into two groups of 10 values each, and the first group has a mean of 12. If 3 is added to each value in the second group, what is the mean of all 20 values?
solution: Adding 3 to each of the 10 values in the second group increases the total by \(10 \cdot 3 = 30\).
The original total is \(20 \cdot 15 = 300\), so the new total is 330.
The new mean is \(\frac{330}{20} = 16.5\). (The first group's mean is not needed.)

explanation.A: Incorrect. This adds 3 to the mean of all 20 values, as if 3 were added to every value. Only half of the values increase, so the mean increases by 1.5.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the new mean of the second group alone: its old mean is \(\frac{300 - 120}{10} = 18\), and \(18 + 3 = 21\). The question asks for the mean of all 20 values.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The total increases by 30 when 3 is added to 10 of the values, so the mean cannot stay the same.
explanation.D: Correct. The total rises from 300 to 330, and \(\frac{330}{20} = 16.5\).

items.stem: The box plot summarizes the lengths, in minutes, of 41 phone calls made at an office. Which of the following must be true?

choices.A: At least 21 of the calls lasted 28 minutes or longer.
choices.B: The mean length of the calls is greater than 28 minutes.
choices.C: Exactly 10 of the calls lasted more than 20 minutes and less than 28 minutes.
choices.D: The mean length of the calls is 28 minutes.

solution: With 41 values in order, the median is the 21st value, which is 28.
The 21st through the 41st values are all at least 28, and that is 21 calls.
The box plot does not give the mean, and it does not tell how many values equal a quartile, so the other statements might be false.

explanation.A: Correct. The median of 41 values is the 21st value in order, 28. The 21st through 41st values, 21 calls in all, are each at least 28 minutes.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The long right whisker suggests a few long calls, but the mean is not guaranteed to be greater than 28. For example, the box plot also fits a data set in which 19 calls lasted exactly 20 minutes and 10 lasted exactly 28 minutes, and that data set has a mean of less than 28.
explanation.C: Incorrect. About a quarter of the calls are between the first quartile and the median, but several calls could last exactly 20 or exactly 28 minutes, so the number strictly between them is not fixed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. 28 minutes is the median. A box plot does not show the mean, and the mean need not equal the median.

items.stem: Data sets P, Q and R each contain 6 values. P: \(10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 20\); Q: \(10, 15, 15, 15, 15, 20\); R: \(10, 10, 15, 15, 20, 20\). Which list orders the data sets from least to greatest standard deviation?

choices.C: The three standard deviations are equal.

solution: All three data sets have a mean of 15 and a range of 10, so compare the distances from 15.
Q has four values at the mean (distance 0) and two at distance 5. R has two values at the mean and four at distance 5. P has all six values at distance 5.
So the spread increases from Q to R to P.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the order. The values of P are all 5 away from the mean, which is the most spread out, not the least.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Q has more values at the mean than R, so Q is less spread out than R.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The data sets have the same mean and the same range, but their values are at different distances from the mean, so the standard deviations differ.
explanation.D: Correct. Q has the most values at the mean, R has fewer, and P has none, so the standard deviations increase in the order Q, R, P.
